title.zh: 卷五十九 列傳第二十九 汝南王亮 楚王瑋 趙王倫 齊王冏 長沙王乂 成都王潁 河間王顒 東海王越
title.en: Volume 59 Biographies 29: Liang, Prince Wencheng of Ru'nan; Wei, Prince Yin of Chu; Lun, Prince of Zhao; Jiong, Prince of Qi; Ai, Prince of Changsha; Ying, Prince of Chengdu; Yong, Prince of Hejian; Yue, Prince Xiaoxian of Donghai
title.raw: 卷五十九 列傳第二十九 汝南王亮 楚王瑋 趙王倫 齊王冏 長沙王乂 成都王潁 河間王顒 東海王越 Volume 59 Biographies 29: Liang, Prince Wencheng of Ru'nan; Wei, Prince Yin of Chu; Lun, Prince of Zhao; Jiong, Prince of Qi; Ai, Prince of Changsha; Ying, Prince of Chengdu; Yong, Prince of Hejian; Yue, Prince Xiaoxian of Donghai

sentences.zh: 自古帝王之臨天下也，皆欲廣樹蕃屏，崇固維城。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, when emperors and kings have faced All-under-Heaven, they have all wished broadly to plant screens of vassals and to strengthen and secure the cordon of walls that shield the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From ancient times, rulers who held the realm sought to multiply feudal bulwarks and shore up the ring of territories that defend the throne.

sentences.zh: 唐、虞以前，憲章蓋闕，夏、殷以後，遺跡可知。

translations.literal: Before Tang and Yu, statutes and regulations are generally lacking; after Xia and Yin, surviving traces may be known.
translations.idiomatic: Before the age of Yao and Shun, institutions are largely lost to us; from the Xia and Shang onward, we can still follow the historical record.

sentences.zh: 然而玉帛會于塗山，雖云萬國，至於分疆胙土，猶或未詳。

translations.literal: Yet though jade and silk assembled at Mount Tu and it was said there were ten thousand states, as for dividing borders and granting soil in fief, it was still perhaps not yet clear.
translations.idiomatic: Even the assembly at Mount Tu with its tribute of jade and silk—though tradition speaks of myriad domains—leaves the actual partition of territory imperfectly known.

sentences.zh: 泊乎周室，粲焉可觀，封建親賢，並為列國。

translations.literal: Down to the house of Zhou, it shines forth and may be viewed: enfeoffing kin and the worthy, they together became the row of states.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou the picture becomes luminous: the kings enfeoffed kinsmen and worthy men, and those domains stood side by side as independent states.

sentences.zh: 當其興也，周、召贊其升平；

translations.literal: When it rose, the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao assisted its ascendancy to peace;
translations.idiomatic: In its rise the dukes of Zhou and Shao helped sustain its tranquil golden age;

sentences.zh: 及其衰也，桓、文輔其危亂。

translations.literal: When it declined, Huan and Wen aided it amid peril and turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: In decline Lords Huan of Qi and Wen of Jin steadied it through crisis and chaos.

sentences.zh: 故得卜世之祚克昌，卜年之基惟永。

translations.literal: Therefore they obtained that the fortune of divined generations could flourish and the foundation of divined years was enduring.
translations.idiomatic: Hence their dynastic fortune appeared blessed by every oracle of longevity, and their reign seemed built to endure.

sentences.zh: 逮王赧即世，天祿已終，虛位無主，三十餘載。

translations.literal: When King Nan passed from the world, Heaven's emolument had ended; the position stood empty without a lord for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: When the last Zhou king died the Mandate was spent; the throne stood vacant for more than thirty years.

sentences.zh: 爰及暴秦，併吞天下，戒衰周之削弱，忽帝業之遠圖，謂王室之陵遲，由諸候之強大。

translations.literal: Then violent Qin swallowed All-under-Heaven; warning against the weakening of declining Zhou, it neglected the long-range plan of imperial enterprise, holding that the royal house's decline was due to the strength of the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Ruthless Qin then swallowed the realm; wary of weak Zhou, it cast aside far-sighted imperial strategy and blamed the throne's decline on powerful regional lords.

sentences.zh: 於是罷侯置守，獨尊諸己，至乎子弟，並為匹夫，惟欲肆虐陵威，莫顧謀孫翼子。

translations.literal: Thereupon it abolished marquises and installed prefects, honoring itself alone; down to sons and younger kin, all became commoners; it only wished to tyrannize and awe, caring nothing for planning for grandsons or sheltering sons.
translations.idiomatic: So Qin replaced feudal lords with appointed governors and hoarded authority in itself; even imperial kin became commoners. It sought only to bully and overawe, with no thought for securing posterity.

sentences.zh: 枝葉微弱，宗祐孤危，內無社稷之臣，外闕籓維之助。

translations.literal: Branches and leaves were feeble; the ancestral temple stood solitary and perilous; within there were no ministers for the altars of soil and grain; without there lacked the aid of screens and cords.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial lineage grew thin and the ancestral cult stood alone and exposed; at court no ministers could uphold the state, and beyond the capital no feudal shield remained.

sentences.zh: 陳、項一呼，海內沸騰，隕身於望夷，系頸於軹道。

translations.literal: Chen and Xiang gave one shout and within the seas it boiled; one fell dead at Wangyi, another bound his neck at Zhidao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng and Xiang Yu raised a cry and the empire erupted; the Second Emperor perished at Wangyi Palace, and the surrendered ruler met the cord at Zhidao.

sentences.zh: 事不師古，二世而滅。

translations.literal: Affairs did not take antiquity as teacher; in two generations it perished.
translations.idiomatic: Because it refused to learn from the past, Qin lasted only two generations before it was gone.

sentences.zh: 漢祖勃興，爰革斯弊。

translations.literal: The Han founder rose mightily and thereupon reformed this abuse.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder rose in vigor and swept away that failure.

sentences.zh: 於是分王子弟，列建功臣，錫之山川，誓以帶礪。

translations.literal: Thereupon he divided kingships among sons and younger brothers and arrayed meritorious ministers as founders, granting them mountains and rivers and swearing by belt and whetstone.
translations.idiomatic: He then enfeoffed imperial sons and younger brothers and ranked his founding followers, investing them with territory and binding them with oaths meant to last as long as rivers and hills.

sentences.zh: 然而矯枉過直，懲羹吹齏，土地封疆，逾越往古。

translations.literal: Yet in straightening the bent they passed the vertical; warning against hot soup they blew the cold pickle; land and sealed borders exceeded those of former antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Han overcorrected: wary of Qin's excess, it awarded territory on a scale no earlier age had matched.

sentences.zh: 始則韓、彭菹醢，次乃吳、楚稱亂。

translations.literal: First Han Xin and Peng Yue were pickled and minced; next Wu and Chu proclaimed rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: First came the executions of Han Xin and Peng Yue; then the kings of Wu and Chu rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 然雖克滅權偪，猶足維翰王畿。

translations.literal: Yet although it overcame and destroyed power that pressed in, it was still sufficient to be retaining posts for the royal domain.
translations.idiomatic: Even after crushing over-mighty vassals, those domains still helped buttress the capital region.

sentences.zh: 洎成、哀之後，戚籓陵替，君臣乘茲間隙，竊位偷安。

translations.literal: Down to after Cheng and Ai, kin screens declined; ruler and ministers rode this gap to steal position and seek ease.
translations.idiomatic: By the reigns of Cheng and Ai the imperial kin's feudal shield had worn thin; ruler and ministers exploited the opening to usurp authority and coast along.

sentences.zh: 光武雄略緯天，慷慨下國，遂能除凶靜亂，復禹配天，休祉盛於兩京，鼎祚隆於四百，宗支繼絕之力，可得而言。

translations.literal: Guangwu's heroic strategy spanned Heaven; generously he descended to the regional states; thus he was able to remove the fierce and quiet turmoil, restore Yu's alignment with Heaven; blessings flourished in the two capitals; the tripod fortune rose for four hundred years; the strength by which the lineage continued cut-off lines may be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu's sweeping strategy reunited the realm; he swept away rebels and restored Han's mandate. Blessings overflowed in Luoyang and Chang'an, and the dynasty flourished for four hundred years—such was the power of a lineage that could revive what seemed lost.

sentences.zh: 魏武忘經國之宏規，行忌刻之小數，功臣無立錐之地，子弟君不使之人，徒分茅社，實傳虛爵，本根無所庇廕，遂乃三葉而亡。

translations.literal: Wei Wu forgot the great norms for ordering the state and practiced petty calculations of jealousy and harshness; meritorious ministers had no ground to stand a cone; sons and younger brothers were people the ruler did not employ; vainly they divided straw-clod altars but in truth transmitted empty titles; the root had nowhere for sheltering shade; thus in three generations it perished.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao abandoned statecraft on a grand scale for petty suspicion: his generals were granted no real foothold, and imperial sons were kept from power. Feudal rites were hollow honorifics, not roots that could shelter the dynasty—so Wei lasted barely three generations.

sentences.zh: 有晉思改覆車，復隆磐石，或出擁旄節，{艸涖}岳牧之榮；

translations.literal: Jin wished to change the overturned cart and again elevate the great stone; some went out bearing command banners and staff and arrived to the glory of regional governors;
translations.idiomatic: Western Jin sought to avoid Wei's mistake and again elevate princes as pillars of state: some took command in the provinces with the honors due a governor;

sentences.zh: 入踐臺階，居端揆之重。

translations.literal: entering they trod the terrace steps and occupied the weight of the premier's post.
translations.idiomatic: others entered the capital to mount the central terrace and bear the chief minister's burden.

sentences.zh: 然而付託失所，授任乖方，政令不恆，賞罰斯濫。

translations.literal: Yet entrustment missed its proper place; appointments deviated from the right method; government orders were not constant; rewards and punishments were thereby excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Yet trust was misplaced, appointments mishandled, policy swung erratically, and rewards and punishments became arbitrary.

sentences.zh: 或有材而不任，或無罪而見誅，朝為伊、周，夕為莽、卓。

translations.literal: Some had talent but were not employed; some without guilt were seen executed; morning they were Yi and Zhou, evening they were Mang and Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Able men went unused while others died guiltless; a prince might be hailed as Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou at dawn and reviled as Wang Mang or Dong Zhuo by dusk.

sentences.zh: 機權失於上，禍亂作於下。

translations.literal: Opportunity and power were lost above; disaster and turmoil arose below.
translations.idiomatic: With control lost at court, catastrophe welled up in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 楚、趙諸王，相仍構釁，徒興晉陽之甲，竟匪勤王之師。

translations.literal: The kings of Chu, Zhao, and others, one after another, constructed provocations; vainly they raised the armor of Jinyang; in the end they were not armies that aided the king.
translations.idiomatic: The kings of Chu and Zhao and their ilk traded blows and grudges; they trumped up armies like the march on Jinyang, yet none truly came to rescue the throne.

sentences.zh: 始則為身擇利，利未加而害及；

translations.literal: At first they chose profit for themselves; profit had not yet been added but harm arrived;
translations.idiomatic: They began by chasing private advantage and paid for it before any gain arrived;

sentences.zh: 初乃無心憂國，國非憂而奚拯！

translations.literal: Originally they had no mind to worry for the state; if the state is not worried for, how save it!
translations.idiomatic: they never meant to carry the state's burdens—yet without that care, how could the realm be saved?

sentences.zh: 遂使昭陽興廢，有甚弈棋；

translations.literal: Thereupon they caused Zhaoyang's rise and fall to be more than chess;
translations.idiomatic: Emperors rose and fell in the inner palace faster than pieces on a weiqi board;

sentences.zh: 乘輿幽縶，更同羑裏。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage was confined and bound, again like Youli.
translations.idiomatic: the sovereign himself was held captive like King Wen of Zhou in Youli.

sentences.zh: 胡羯陵侮，宗廟丘墟，良可悲也。

translations.literal: Hu and Jie insulted and abused; ancestral temples became mounds and ruins—truly lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Hu and Jie armies trampled the north until the altars lay in ruins—a tragedy beyond words.

sentences.zh: 夫為國之有籓屏，猶濟川之有舟楫，安危成敗，義實相資。

translations.literal: Now for a state to have screens is like crossing a river's having boat and oar; safety and peril, completion and defeat, in principle truly rely on each other.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal shields are to a dynasty what boats are to a river crossing: fortune and ruin truly depend on them.

sentences.zh: 舟楫且完，波濤不足稱其險；

translations.literal: If boat and oar are moreover intact, waves and billows are insufficient to be called dangerous;
translations.idiomatic: With hull and oars sound, even heavy seas lose their terror;

sentences.zh: 籓屏式固，禍亂何以成其階！

translations.literal: If screens are thereby firm, how should disaster and turmoil complete their steps!
translations.idiomatic: with loyal bulwarks in place, rebellion cannot easily climb to power.

sentences.zh: 向使八王之中，一籓繄賴，如梁王之禦大故，若硃虛之除大憝，則外寇焉敢憑陵，內難奚由竊發！

translations.literal: If among the eight kings one screen had been relied upon, like the Prince of Liang's defending the great cause, like Zhu Xu's removing the great villain, then how would outer bandits dare to press in; how would inner difficulties steal to arise!
translations.idiomatic: Had even one of the eight princes stood firm like Liu Wu of Liang facing the Rebellion of the Seven States or Liu Zhang of Zhuxu purging the Lü clan, barbarians could not have swept south and palace coups would have found no opening.

sentences.zh: 縱令天子暗劣，鼎臣奢放，雖或顛沛，未至土崩。

translations.literal: Granting the Son of Heaven dim and inferior; tripod ministers extravagant and unrestrained—although perhaps overturned and exhausted, it would not reach earth-splitting collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Even with a weak emperor and reckless ministers at the helm, the realm might stumble yet need not shatter outright.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: By what speak thus?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say so?

sentences.zh: 琅邪譬彼諸王，權輕眾寡，度長絜大，不可同年。

translations.literal: Langye compared to those various kings: power light, masses few; measuring length and comparing greatness, they cannot be the same year.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Prince Langye beside those princes: his authority was slighter and his following smaller—there is no comparing their stature.

sentences.zh: 遂能匹馬濟江，奄有吳會，存重宗社，百有餘年。

translations.literal: Yet he was able with a single horse to cross the Yangzi and suddenly possess Wu and Kuaiji; preserving and emphasizing the ancestral temple, more than a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he crossed the Yangzi almost alone, seized Wu and the southeast, and preserved the dynasty's altars for another century.

sentences.zh: 雖曰天時，抑亦人事。

translations.literal: Although it is called Heaven's timing, also it is human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven lent a hand, but human choices mattered every bit as much.

sentences.zh: 豈如趙倫、齊冏之輩，河間、東海之徒，家國俱亡，身名並滅。

translations.literal: How does it compare to the likes of Zhao Lun and Qi Jiong, the fellows of Hejian and Donghai—house and state together perished, body and name together extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: How far that is from Prince Lun of Zhao, Prince Jiong of Qi, Prince Yong of Hejian, and Prince Yue of Donghai—men who destroyed both realm and reputation.

sentences.zh: 善惡之數，此非其效歟！

translations.literal: The reckoning of good and evil—is this not its demonstration!
translations.idiomatic: Such is the ledger of merit and guilt laid bare.

sentences.zh: 西晉之政亂朝危，雖由時主，然而煽其風，速其禍者，咎在八王，故序而論之，總為其傳云耳。

translations.literal: Western Jin's government in chaos and court in peril, although due to the rulers of the time, yet those who fanned its wind and hastened its disaster—the blame lies with the eight kings; therefore I order and discuss them, gathering them into one composite biography.
translations.idiomatic: Western Jin's turmoil owes something to each emperor, yet the men who fanned the flames were the eight princes; I therefore preface this chapter and give their deeds in a single joint biography.

sentences.zh: 汝南文成王亮

translations.literal: Prince Wencheng of Runan, Liang
translations.idiomatic: Sima Liang, Prince Wencheng of Runan

sentences.zh: 汝南文成王亮，字子翼，宣帝第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince Wencheng of Runan, Liang, courtesy name Ziyi, was Emperor Xuan's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Liang, Prince Wencheng of Runan, whose courtesy name was Ziyi, was the fourth son of Emperor Xuan of Jin.

sentences.zh: 少清警有才用，仕魏為散騎侍郎、萬歲亭侯，拜東中郎將，進封廣陽鄉侯。

translations.literal: In youth he was clear and alert and had talent for use; serving Wei he was Gentleman Attendant at Leisure and Marquis of Wansui Precinct, was appointed General of the Central Army of the East, and advanced to enfeoffment as Village Marquis of Guangyang.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was sharp and capable; under Wei he rose to Gentleman Attendant at Leisure and Marquis of Wansui Pavilion, then East Central Army general, and finally Village Marquis of Guangyang.

sentences.zh: 討諸葛誕于壽春，失利，免官。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Zhuge Dan at Shouchun, he suffered defeat and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Zhuge Dan at Shouchun but lost and was stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 頃之，拜左將軍，加散騎常侍、假節，出監豫州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed General of the Left, added Regular Attendant at Leisure and credential-bearing authority, and went out to supervise Yu Province military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named General of the Left with concurrent Regular Attendant at Leisure and credential authority to oversee Yu Province forces.

sentences.zh: 五等建，改封祁陽伯，轉鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were established, his enfeoffment was changed to Earl of Qiyang; he was transferred to General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei adopted the five noble ranks he became Earl of Qiyang and then General Who Guards the West.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，封扶風郡王，邑萬戶，置騎司馬，增參軍掾屬，持節、都督關中雍、涼諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Fufeng Commandery with a fief of ten thousand households; a Cavalry Commandant was established and adjutants and clerks increased; he bore credentials and supervised Guanzhong, Yong, and Liang military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's Emperor Wu took the throne Liang became Prince of Fufeng with ten thousand households, a full princely staff, and authority over Yong and Liang as credential-bearing area commander.

sentences.zh: 會秦州刺史胡烈為羌虜所害，亮遣將軍劉旂、騎督敬琰赴救，不進，坐是貶為平西將軍。

translations.literal: When Qin Province Inspector Hu Lie was killed by Qiang bandits, Liang sent General Liu Qi and Cavalry Supervisor Jing Yan to rescue but they did not advance; sitting on this he was demoted to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: When Inspector Hu Lie of Qin was killed by Qiang raiders, Liang dispatched Liu Qi and Jing Yan to relieve him; they halted, and Liang was demoted to General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 旂當斬，亮與軍司曹冏上言，節度之咎由亮而出，乞丐旂死。

translations.literal: Qi ought to be beheaded; Liang and Army Marshal Cao Jiong submitted words that the fault of command coordination stemmed from Liang and begged Qi spared from death.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi faced execution; Liang and army marshal Cao Jiong memorialized that command responsibility was Liang's own and pleaded for Qi's life.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「高平困急，計城中及旂足以相拔，就不能徑至，尚當深進。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Gaoping was trapped and urgent; reckoning the city within and Qi were sufficient mutually to rescue; even if they could not go straight to arrive, still they ought deeply to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: "Gaoping was desperate; the city and Liu Qi together could have broken the siege—if not directly, then by pressing deeper.

sentences.zh: 今奔突有投，而坐視覆敗，故加旂大戮。

translations.literal: Now there was someone to whom to rush strike; yet sitting they watched overturn and defeat; therefore great punishment was added to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: There was an opening to strike, yet he watched the army collapse—that is why Qi faces capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 今若罪不在旂，當有所在。

translations.literal: Now if the guilt is not on Qi, there ought to be where it is.
translations.idiomatic: If the fault is not Qi's, it must lie elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 」有司又奏免亮官，削爵土。

translations.literal: " The offices further memorialized to dismiss Liang from office and strip title and territory.
translations.idiomatic: " Officials then memorialized to dismiss Liang and strip his rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 詔惟免官。

translations.literal: The edict only dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spared his title and dismissed him from office only.

sentences.zh: 頃之，拜撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored as General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 是歲，吳將步闡來降，假亮節都督諸軍事以納之。

translations.literal: That year Wu general Bu Chan came to surrender; Liang was lent credentials to supervise all military affairs to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: That year when Wu's Bu Chan defected, Liang received credentials to command the forces that accepted him.

sentences.zh: 尋加侍中之服。

translations.literal: Soon was added the attire of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was shortly granted the vestments of a Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，以扶風池陽四千一百戶為太妃伏氏湯沐邑，置家令丞僕，後改食南郡枝江。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianning, with Fufeng's Chiyang's four thousand one hundred households as Grand Consort Fu's bathing fief, Household Superintendent, Assistants, and stewards were established; later it was changed to feed on Nan Commandery's Zhijiang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning, four thousand one hundred households at Chiyang in Fufeng were set aside as Grand Consort Fu's personal estate with a full household staff; later her income was shifted to Zhijiang in Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 太妃嘗有小疾，祓于洛水，亮兄弟三人侍從，並持節鼓吹，震耀洛濱。

translations.literal: The Grand Consort once had a minor illness and purified herself at the Luo River; Liang's three brothers attended and followed, all bearing credentials, drums, and pipes, shaking and dazzling the Luo's bank.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Consort Fu took a minor purification rite at the Luo, Liang and his three brothers attended with credentials, band, and escort—splendor that shook the riverside.

sentences.zh: 武帝登陵雲台望見，曰：「伏妃可謂富貴矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu ascended Lingyun Terrace, looked and saw, saying: "Consort Fu may be called wealthy and noble.
translations.idiomatic: From Lingyun Terrace Emperor Wu watched and remarked, "Lady Fu knows wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: 」其年進號衛將軍，加侍中。

translations.literal: " That year he advanced in title to General of the Guard and added Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: " That year Liang was promoted to General of the Guard with concurrent status as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時宗室殷盛，無相統攝，乃以亮為宗師，本官如故，使訓導觀察，有不遵禮法，小者正以義方，大者隨事聞奏。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial house was abundant and flourishing, without mutual overseeing; thereupon Liang was made Master of the Imperial Clan; original offices as before; he was caused to instruct and guide and observe; those not observing ritual and law—small ones he corrected with righteous standards; large ones he followed affairs and reported.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clan had grown large without oversight, so Liang was named Master of the Imperial Clan while keeping his posts; he was to teach and monitor kin, correcting minor lapses locally and memorializing major ones.

sentences.zh: 三年，徙封汝南，出為鎮南大將軍、都督豫州軍事，開府、假節，之國，給追鋒車、皁輪犢車，錢五十萬。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred enfeoffment to Runan and went out as Grand General Who Guards the South and supervised Yu Province military affairs, opening office and credential-bearing authority, proceeding to his state; he was given Swift Pursuit carriage, black-wheeled calf cart, and five hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianning his fief moved to Runan; he became Grand General Who Guards the South with Yu Province command, an independent headquarters and credentials, and went to his principality with imperial carriages and a grant of five hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 頃之，征亮為侍中、撫軍大將軍，領後軍將軍，統冠軍、步兵、射聲、長水等營，給兵五百人，騎百匹。

translations.literal: Shortly Liang was summoned as Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Pacifies the Army, concurrently General of the Rear Army, commanding Champion, Infantry, Sound-of-the-Bow, and Eternal Flow camps; five hundred soldiers were given, one hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as Palace Attendant and Grand General Who Pacifies the Army, heading the Rear Army while commanding several guard camps—five hundred troops and a hundred mounts.

sentences.zh: 遷太尉、錄尚書事、領太子太傅，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Commandant, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, concurrently Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent; Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Commandant with recording duties over the Secretariat and concurrent appointment as the heir apparent's tutor while retaining his palace post.

sentences.zh: 及武帝寢疾，為楊駿所排，乃以亮為侍中、大司馬、假黃鉞、大都督、督豫州諸軍事，出鎮許昌，加軒懸之樂，六佾之舞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu lay gravely ill, squeezed out by Yang Jun, thereupon Liang was made Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal, lent the yellow axe, Grand Commander, supervising Yu Province military affairs, going out to garrison Xuchang; suspended carriage music was added, six rows of dancers.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu fell mortally ill, Yang Jun edged Liang aside by naming him Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal with yellow axe and grand command, sent to hold Xuchang—honors that included royal music and a six-row guard dance.

sentences.zh: 封子羕為西陽公。

translations.literal: His son Yang was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sima Yang was made Duke of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 未發，帝大漸，詔留亮委以後事。

translations.literal: Before he set out, the emperor greatly declined; an edict detained Liang and entrusted him with later affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, the emperor sank rapidly; an edict kept Liang at court to entrust him with the succession.

sentences.zh: 楊駿聞之，從中書監華暠索詔視，遂不還。

translations.literal: Yang Jun heard it; from Palace Secretariat Supervisor Hua Gao he demanded the edict to view, and thereupon did not return it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun learned of it, borrowed the edict from Hua Gao of the Palace Secretariat to read—and never gave it back.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，亮懼駿疑己，辭疾不入，于大司馬門外敘哀而已，表求過葬。

translations.literal: The emperor died; Liang feared Jun suspected himself; declining illness he did not enter; outside the Grand Marshal gate he narrated grief only and submitted a memorial requesting to pass burial.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor died Liang stayed away for fear Yang Jun would suspect him, offering only condolence outside the Grand Marshal's gate and asking to defer the funeral audience.

sentences.zh: 駿欲討亮，亮知之，問計于廷尉何勖。

translations.literal: Jun wished to campaign against Liang; Liang knew it and asked plan from Commandant of Justice He Xu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jun planned to move against him, Liang consulted Commandant of Justice He Xu.

sentences.zh: 勖曰：「今朝廷皆歸心於公，公何不討人而懼為人所討！

translations.literal: Xu said: "Now the court all turns heart to you; why do you not campaign against others but fear being campaigned against by others!
translations.idiomatic: He Xu answered, "The court already favors you—strike first instead of waiting to be struck!

sentences.zh: 」或說亮率所領入廢駿，亮不能用，夜馳赴許昌，故得免。

translations.literal: " Someone urged Liang to lead those he commanded to enter and depose Jun; Liang could not use it; night galloping he hastened to Xuchang, therefore obtained escape.
translations.idiomatic: " Others urged him to march on the capital and depose Yang Jun, but Liang refused; he fled by night to Xuchang and so escaped.

sentences.zh: 及駿誅，詔曰：「大司馬、汝南王亮體道沖粹，通識政理，宣翼之績，顯於本朝，《二南》之風，流于方夏，將憑遠猷，以康王化。

translations.literal: When Jun was executed, an edict said: "The Grand Marshal, Prince of Runan Liang embodies the Way pure and simple, thoroughly comprehends government principle; the deeds of spreading wings are manifest in this court; the wind of the 'Two Souths' flows through the regional Xia; will rely on far-reaching plans to bring peace to royal transformation.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Jun died, an edict declared: "Grand Marshal Sima Liang, Prince of Runan, embodies pure virtue and masters statecraft; his aid to the throne recalls the Odes of the south; we look to his long vision to restore good rule.

sentences.zh: 其以亮為太宰、錄尚書事，入朝不趨，劍履上殿，增掾屬十人，給千兵百騎，與太保衛瓘對掌朝政。

translations.literal: Thereupon take Liang as Grand Tutor, Recorder of Masters of Writing affairs, entering court not hurrying, sword and shoes on hall; increase adjutants and clerks by ten; give one thousand soldiers, one hundred riders; with Grand Protector Wei Guan face palm court government.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint him Grand Tutor with recording powers over the Secretariat: he may enter court without running, wear sword and shoes in the hall, add ten staff, command a thousand soldiers and a hundred riders, and share governance with Grand Protector Wei Guan.

sentences.zh: 」亮論賞誅楊駿之功過差，欲以苟悅眾心，由是失望。

translations.literal: " Liang discussed rewards and punishing Yang Jun's merits with imbalance; wishing thereby casually to please the masses' hearts, on this account there was disappointment.
translations.idiomatic: " But Liang mishandled rewards for Yang Jun's purge in a bid to please everyone, and instead alienated them.

sentences.zh: 楚王瑋有勳而好立威，亮憚之，欲奪其兵權。

translations.literal: Prince Wei of Chu had merit but liked to establish awesomeness; Liang feared him and wished to strip his military authority.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Wei of Chu was meritorious but loved throwing his weight around; Liang feared him and moved to strip his command.

sentences.zh: 瑋甚憾，乃承賈后旨，誣亮與瓘有廢立之謀，矯詔遣其長史公孫宏與積弩將軍李肇夜以兵圍之。

translations.literal: Wei greatly resented; thereupon receiving Empress Jia's intent, he falsely accused Liang and Guan of having a plot to depose and establish; falsely by edict he sent his Chief Clerk Gongsun Hong and Repeated Crossbow General Li Zhao night with troops to surround them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei nursed a deep grudge; at Empress Jia's bidding he accused Liang and Wei Guan of plotting to replace the emperor, forged an edict, and sent Gongsun Hong and Li Zhao with troops to surround Liang by night.

sentences.zh: 帳下督李龍白外有變，請距之，亮不聽。

translations.literal: Tent Commander Li Long reported white: outside there is change; requested to resist; Liang did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: His guard officer Li Long warned of trouble outside and asked to fight back; Liang refused.

sentences.zh: 俄然楚兵登牆而呼，亮驚曰：「吾無二心，何至於是！

translations.literal: Suddenly Chu troops climbed the wall and shouted; Liang startled said: "I have no second heart; how reach to this!
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chu soldiers scaled the walls, shouting; Liang cried in alarm, "I am innocent—how could it come to this?

sentences.zh: 若有詔書，其可見乎？

translations.literal: If there is an edict document, may it be shown?
translations.idiomatic: If there is truly an edict, let me see it.

sentences.zh: 」宏等不許，促兵攻之。

translations.literal: " Hong and others did not permit; urged troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: " Hong refused and drove his men to attack.

sentences.zh: 長史劉准謂亮曰：「觀此必是奸謀，府中俊乂如林，猶可盡力距戰。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Liu Zhun said to Liang: "Observing this must be treacherous plotting; within the bureau worthy talents are like a forest; still can exert strength to resist battle.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Liu Zhun urged him: "This is clearly treachery—you still have plenty of able men in the bureau to fight.

sentences.zh: 」又弗聽，遂為肇所執，而歎曰：「我之忠心，可破示天下也，如何無道，枉殺不辜！

translations.literal: " Again he did not listen; thereupon was seized by Zhao and sighed saying: "My loyal heart may be split open to show All-under-Heaven; how lacking in the Way, wrongly killing the guiltless!
translations.idiomatic: " Again Liang refused and Li Zhao seized him. He sighed, "My loyalty could be cut open for all to see—what lawless men, to murder the innocent!

sentences.zh: 」是時大熱，兵人坐亮于車下，時人憐之，為之交扇。

translations.literal: " At this time it was greatly hot; soldiers sat Liang under a cart; people of the time pitied him and for him mutually fanned.
translations.idiomatic: " In sweltering heat the troops seated him beneath a cart; onlookers pitied him and fanned him in turn.

sentences.zh: 將及日中，無敢害者。

translations.literal: Nearing reaching midday, none dared harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Until nearly noon no one dared strike him.

sentences.zh: 瑋出令曰：「能斬亮者，賞布千匹。

translations.literal: Wei went out and ordered: "He who can behead Liang is rewarded a thousand bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Wei stepped out and offered a thousand bolts of cloth for Liang's head.

sentences.zh: 」遂為亂兵所害，投於北門之壁，鬢髮耳鼻皆悉毀焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was harmed by riotous troops; cast upon the north gate's wall; sideburns hair ear nose all entirely destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: " Rioting soldiers then killed him and threw him against the north gate—hair, ears, and nose torn away.

sentences.zh: 及瑋誅，追復亮爵位，給東園溫明秘器，朝服一襲，錢三百萬，布絹三百匹，喪葬之禮如安平獻王孚故事，廟設軒懸之樂。

translations.literal: When Wei was executed, Liang's title and position were pursued restored; Eastern Park warm-bright secret vessels were given; one set court robes; three million cash; three hundred bolts cloth silk; funeral and burial ritual like Prince Xian of Anping Fu's precedent; temple had suspended carriage music.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei was executed Liang's titles were posthumously restored with full honors—imperial coffin gifts, court dress, cash and silk, burial rites matching Prince Xian of Anping, and temple music befitting a king.

sentences.zh: 有五子：粹、矩、羕、宗、熙。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Cui, Ju, Yang, Zong, Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Sima Cui, Ju, Yang, Zong, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 粹字茂弘。

translations.literal: Cui's courtesy name was Maohong.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Cui, courtesy name Maohong.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: Died early.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 矩字延明。

translations.literal: Ju's courtesy name was Yanming.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ju, courtesy name Yanming.

sentences.zh: 拜世子，為屯騎校尉，與父亮同被害。

translations.literal: He was appointed heir son; was Colonel of Garrison Cavalry; together with father Liang same time was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Named heir as Colonel of Garrison Cavalry, he was murdered together with his father.

sentences.zh: 追贈典軍將軍，諡懷王。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted General Who Maintains the Army; posthumous title Prince Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named General Who Maintains the Army with the posthumous title Prince Huai.

sentences.zh: 子祐立，是為威王。

translations.literal: Son You established; this is Prince Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sima You succeeded him as Prince Wei.

sentences.zh: 羕字延年。

translations.literal: Yang's courtesy name was Yannian.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yang's courtesy name was Yannian.

sentences.zh: 太康末，封西陽縣公，拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the end of Taikang he was enfeoffed Duke of Xiyang County and appointed Regular Attendant at Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taikang he received the ducal title for Xiyang County and a concurrent appointment as Regular Attendant at Leisure.

sentences.zh: 亮之被害也，羕時年八歲，鎮南將軍裴楷與之親姻，竊之以逃，一夜八遷，故得免。

translations.literal: When Liang was harmed, Yang at the time was eight years old; Grand General Who Guards the South Pei Kai was marriage-connected with him and stole him away to flee; one night eight relocations; therefore obtained escape.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Liang was murdered, Yang was eight. Pei Kai, Grand General Who Guards the South, was related by marriage and smuggled the boy out—eight moves in one night—so he survived.

sentences.zh: 及瑋誅，進爵為王，曆步兵校尉、左軍驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Wei was executed, he advanced in nobility to prince; he passed through Colonel of Infantry and General of Agile Cavalry of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Wei was executed Yang was promoted to prince and served successively as Colonel of Infantry and General of Agile Cavalry of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 元康初，進封郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang he advanced enfeoffment to Prince of Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuankang his title was raised to prince of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 永興初，拜侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxing he was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongxing he became Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以長沙王乂黨，廢為庶人。

translations.literal: Because he was of Prince Yi of Changsha's faction, he was degraded to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: As an ally of Prince Yi of Changsha he was stripped of rank and reduced to common status.

sentences.zh: 惠帝還洛，復羕封，為撫軍將軍，又以汝南期思、西陵益其國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui returned to Luoyang, Yang's enfeoffment was restored; he was General Who Pacifies the Army; further with Runan's Qisi and Xiling his state was increased.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Hui returned to Luoyang Yang's titles were restored as General Who Pacifies the Army, and the districts of Qisi and Xiling in Runan were added to his fief.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，拜鎮軍將軍，加散騎常侍，領後軍將軍，復以邾、蘄春益之，並前三萬五千戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongjia he was appointed General Who Guards the Army, added Regular Attendant at Leisure, concurrently General of the Rear Army; further Zhu and Qichun were used to increase it; together with before thirty-five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongjia he became General Who Guards the Army with concurrent Regular Attendant at Leisure and command of the Rear Army; Zhu and Qichun were added to his domain, bringing his registered households to thirty-five thousand.

sentences.zh: 隨東海王越東出鄄城，遂南渡江。

translations.literal: Following Prince Yue of Donghai east out of Juancheng, thereupon he crossed south over the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Yue of Donghai east from Juancheng and crossed the Yangzi into the south.

sentences.zh: 元帝承制，更拜撫軍大將軍、開府，給千兵百騎，詔與南頓王宗統流人以實中州，江西荒梗，復還。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan assumed regulation and again appointed Grand General Who Pacifies the Army, opening office; one thousand soldiers and one hundred riders were given; an edict ordered him with Prince Zong of Nandun to oversee displaced persons to fill the central plain; Jiangxi was desolate and blocked; again returned.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuan of Jin's provisional regime Yang was named Grand General Who Pacifies the Army with an independent headquarters and a guard of a thousand foot and a hundred horse; he was ordered with Prince Zong of Nandun to settle refugees in the central plains, but Jiangxi proved too broken and he came back.

sentences.zh: 及元帝踐阼，進位侍中、太保。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, he advanced position to Palace Attendant and Grand Protector.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan took the throne Yang rose to Palace Attendant and Grand Protector.

sentences.zh: 以羕屬尊，元會特為設床。

translations.literal: Because Yang's relation was honored, at the Yuan meeting a couch was specially set for him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his senior standing among kin, a seat was reserved for him at the New Year court.

sentences.zh: 太興初，錄尚書事，尋領大宗師，加羽葆、斧鉞，班劍六十人，進位太宰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daxing he recorded Masters of Writing affairs; soon he concurrently headed the Grand Master of the Imperial Clan; there were added feather canopy, axe and halberd, sixty court swords bearers; he advanced position to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daxing he took charge of the Secretariat, soon added stewardship of the imperial clan with feather canopy, ceremonial axe, and sixty sword attendants, and was promoted to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 及王敦平，領太尉。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun was pacified, he concurrently held Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun's rebellion was crushed he added the Grand Commandant's portfolio.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，以羕宗室元老，特為之拜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, because Yang was senior elder of the imperial house, especially for him was performed obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne he bowed to Yang in recognition of his seniority among the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 羕放縱兵士劫鈔，所司奏免羕官，詔不問。

translations.literal: Yang indulged soldiers to rob and seize; the offices memorialized to dismiss Yang from office; the edict did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Yang let his troops loot; officials impeached him, but the throne took no action.

sentences.zh: 及帝寢疾，羕與王導同受顧命輔成帝。

translations.literal: When the emperor lay gravely ill, Yang together with Wang Dao received testamentary charge to assist Emperor Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming lay dying Yang and Wang Dao were named regents for Emperor Cheng.

sentences.zh: 時帝幼沖，詔羕依安平獻王孚故事，設床帳於殿上，帝親迎拜。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was young and tender; an edict ordered Yang according to Prince Xian of Anping Fu's precedent to set bed curtains on the hall; the emperor personally went out to greet and bow.
translations.idiomatic: The boy emperor's edict granted Yang the old privilege of Prince Fu of Anping: a screened couch in the hall while Cheng himself came forward to bow.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，坐弟南頓王宗免官，降為弋陽縣王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianhe, sitting because younger brother Prince Zong of Nandun he was dismissed from office and degraded to Prince of Yiyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianhe his brother Prince Zong of Nandun's case cost him his offices and reduced him to Prince of Yiyang County.

sentences.zh: 及蘇峻作亂，羕詣峻稱述其勳，峻大悅，矯詔復羕爵位。

translations.literal: When Su Jun rose in rebellion, Yang went to Jun and declared his merits; Jun greatly rejoiced; falsely by edict restored Yang's title and position.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun seized the capital Yang presented himself and rehearsed his past services; Jun was delighted and forged an edict restoring his titles.

sentences.zh: 峻平，賜死。

translations.literal: Jun pacified, death was gifted.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun fell Yang was sentenced to suicide.

sentences.zh: 世子播、播弟充及息崧並伏誅，國除。

translations.literal: Heir son Bo, Bo's younger brother Chong, and son Song together submitted to execution; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Bo, Bo's brother Chong, and son Song were executed and the principality was abolished.

sentences.zh: 咸康初，復其屬籍，以羕孫瑉為奉車都尉、奉朝請。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiankang his clan register was restored; Yang's grandson Min was made Coachman Commandant and Recipient of Morning Audience.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiankang his line was readmitted to the imperial register; grandson Sima Min received appointments as Coachman Commandant and Recipient of Morning Audience.

sentences.zh: 宗與王導、庾亮志趣不同，連結輕俠，以為腹心，導、亮並以為言。

translations.literal: Zong with Wang Dao and Yu Liang had different aims and interests; he connected and joined light knights-errant, taking them as belly and heart; Dao and Liang together took this as matter for words.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zong disagreed with Wang Dao and Yu Liang and surrounded himself with swordsmen he trusted; both ministers warned the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝以宗戚屬，每容之。

translations.literal: The emperor because Zong was kin relative, each time tolerated him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor indulged him because he was family.

sentences.zh: 及帝疾篤，宗、胤密謀為亂，亮排闥入，升御床，流涕言之，帝始悟。

translations.literal: When the emperor's illness was critical, Zong and Yin secretly plotted to make turmoil; Liang pushed door and entered, ascended the imperial couch, with flowing tears spoke it; the emperor began to awaken.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming lay dying Zong and Zhao Yin plotted a coup; Yu Liang forced his way in, climbed onto the imperial couch weeping, until the emperor finally understood.

sentences.zh: 轉為驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Zong was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 胤為大宗正。

translations.literal: Yin was Grand Master of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yin became Grand Master of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 宗遂怨望形於辭色。

translations.literal: Zong thereupon resentment appeared in words and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's resentment showed openly in word and face.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，御史中丞鐘雅劾宗謀反，庾亮使右衛將軍趙胤收之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianhe, Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk Zhong Ya impeached Zong for plotting rebellion; Yu Liang caused General of the Right Guard Zhao Yin to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianhe Censor-in-Chief Zhong Ya charged Zong with treason; Yu Liang sent General of the Right Guard Zhao Yin to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 宗以兵距戰，為胤所殺，貶其族為馬氏，徙妻子于晉安，既而原之。

translations.literal: Zong with troops resisted battle; was killed by Yin; his clan was degraded to Ma surname; wife and children were moved to Jin'an; after a while they were forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Zong fought back and Zhao Yin killed him; his clan was given the surname Ma and his family banished to Jin'an, though they were later pardoned.

sentences.zh: 三子：綽、超、演，廢為庶人。

translations.literal: Three sons: Chuo, Chao, Yan, were degraded to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: His three sons—Chuo, Chao, and Yan—were reduced to common status.

sentences.zh: 咸康中，復其屬籍。

translations.literal: In Xiankang, his clan register was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiankang their names were restored to the imperial register.

sentences.zh: 綽為奉車都尉、奉朝請。

translations.literal: Chuo was Coachman Commandant and Recipient of Morning Audience.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo received appointments as Coachman Commandant and Recipient of Morning Audience.

sentences.zh: 熙初封汝陽公，討劉喬有功，進爵為王。

translations.literal: At the beginning Xi was enfeoffed Duke of Ruyang; campaigning against Liu Qiao had merit; advanced in nobility to prince.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xi first held the ducal title of Ruyang; he earned promotion to prince for his part against Liu Qiao.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，沒于石勒。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia he sank among Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: He fell into Shi Le's hands at the end of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 楚隱王瑋

translations.literal: Prince Yin of Chu, Wei
translations.idiomatic: Sima Wei, Prince Yin of Chu

sentences.zh: 楊駿之誅也，瑋屯司馬門。

translations.literal: When Yang Jun was executed, Wei garrisoned the Sima Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jun fell Prince Wei held the Sima Gate.

sentences.zh: 瑋少年果銳，多立威刑，朝廷忌之。

translations.literal: Wei in youth was decisive and keen; much he established awe and punishments; the court feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Young and ruthless, Wei ruled through terror; the court feared him.

sentences.zh: 汝南王亮、太保衛瓘以瑋性很戾，不可大任，建議使與諸王之國，瑋甚忿之。

translations.literal: Prince Liang of Runan and Grand Protector Wei Guan because Wei's nature was very harsh and perverse, could not greatly be entrusted; they proposed causing him together with the various princes to go to their states; Wei greatly resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang of Runan and Grand Protector Wei Guan judged Wei too vicious for high office and proposed packing him off to his fief with other princes; Wei seethed.

sentences.zh: 長史公孫宏、舍人岐盛並薄於行，為瑋所昵。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Gongsun Hong and Gentleman Attendant Qi Sheng together were shallow in conduct; they were made intimate by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Gongsun Hong and attendant Qi Sheng were men of questionable morals yet favored by Wei.

sentences.zh: 瓘等惡其為人，慮致禍亂，將收盛。

translations.literal: Guan and others hated their persons as men, worried they would bring disaster and turmoil, were about to seize Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan detested them and moved to arrest Qi Sheng before they stirred revolt.

sentences.zh: 盛知之，遂與宏謀，因積弩將軍李肇矯稱瑋命，譖亮、瓘于賈后。

translations.literal: Sheng knew it; thereupon with Hong plotted; through Repeated Crossbow General Li Zhao falsely claiming Wei's command, slandered Liang and Guan to Empress Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Sheng learned of it and with Gongsun Hong put Repeated Crossbow General Li Zhao up to forging orders in Wei's name and denouncing Liang and Guan to Empress Jia.

sentences.zh: 而后不之察，使惠帝為詔曰：「太宰、太保欲為伊、霍之事，王宜宣詔，令淮南、長沙、成都王屯宮諸門，廢二公。

translations.literal: But the empress did not examine it; she caused Emperor Hui to make an edict saying: "The Grand Tutor and Grand Protector wish to do Yi and Huo's affair; the prince ought proclaim edict, order Princes of Huainan, Changsha, and Chengdu garrison the palace's various gates, depose the two lords.
translations.idiomatic: The empress never questioned it and had Emperor Hui issue words: "The Grand Tutor and Grand Protector mean to play Yi Yin and Huo Guang—Prince, you shall publish our command for the princes of Huainan, Changsha, and Chengdu to hold every palace gate and dismiss both ministers.

sentences.zh: 」夜使黃門齎以授瑋。

translations.literal: " Night caused a Yellow Gate to carry it to hand to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " That night a eunuch courier delivered the text to Wei.

sentences.zh: 瑋欲覆奏，黃門曰：「事恐漏泄，非密詔本意也。

translations.literal: Wei wished to submit again for review; the Yellow Gate said: "The affair fears leaking; it is not the secret edict's original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei wanted to memorialize again; the eunuch said secrecy would be lost—hardly the point of a sealed order.

sentences.zh: 」瑋乃止。

translations.literal: " Wei thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " So Wei relented.

sentences.zh: 遂勒本軍，復矯詔召三十六軍，手令告諸軍曰：「天禍晉室，凶亂相仍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he restrained his original army; again falsely by edict summoned thirty-six armies; hand order told the various armies saying: "Heaven calamitizes the Jin house; fierce turmoil follows one another.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied his own command and forged another summons to thirty-six armies, issuing a handwritten order: "Heaven scourges the house of Jin and disasters pile one upon another.

sentences.zh: 間者楊駿之難，實賴諸君克平禍亂。

translations.literal: Recently Yang Jun's disaster, truly relied on you gentlemen being able to pacify calamity and turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: In Yang Jun's coup it was you who restored order.

sentences.zh: 而二公潛圖不軌，欲廢陛下以絕武帝之祀。

translations.literal: But the two lords secretly plotted not upright, wish to depose Your Majesty to cut off Emperor Wu's sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those two ministers plot sedition and would depose you to sever Emperor Wu's line.

sentences.zh: 今輒奉詔，免二公官。

translations.literal: Now rashly upholding edict, dismiss the two lords' offices.
translations.idiomatic: By edict I hereby dismiss both men from office.

sentences.zh: 吾今受詔都督中外諸軍。

translations.literal: I now receive edict to supervise all armies within and without.
translations.idiomatic: I am ordered to command every army of the realm.

sentences.zh: 諸在直衛者皆嚴加警備，其在外營，便相率領，徑詣行府。

translations.literal: All those on duty guard ought strictly to add alert preparation; those in outer camps, then mutually lead and command, go straight to the mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: All palace guards stand ready; field troops are to rally at once to my forward headquarters.

sentences.zh: 助順討逆，天所福也。

translations.literal: Assisting compliant punishing rebellious, Heaven what blesses.
translations.idiomatic: To aid the loyal and crush traitors is to earn Heaven's blessing.

sentences.zh: 懸賞開封，以待忠效。

translations.literal: Suspend rewards open enfeoffment, to await loyal effectiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Bounties and noble titles await those who prove loyal.

sentences.zh: 皇天后土，實聞此言。

translations.literal: August Heaven and rear Earth, truly hear these words.
translations.idiomatic: Let Heaven and Earth witness these words.

sentences.zh: 」又矯詔使亮、瓘上太宰太保印綬、侍中貂蟬，之國，官屬皆罷遣之。

translations.literal: " Again falsely by edict caused Liang and Guan to submit Grand Tutor and Grand Protector seals and ribbons, Palace Attendant sable-cicada; go to their states; officials and subordinates all dismissed and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: " Another forged edict ordered Liang and Guan to surrender seals of Grand Tutor and Grand Protector, their palace regalia, and return to their fiefs—every aide dismissed.

sentences.zh: 又矯詔赦亮、瓘官屬曰：「二公潛謀，欲危社稷，今免還第。

translations.literal: Again falsely by edict pardoned Liang and Guan's officials and subordinates saying: "The two lords secretly plotted, wished to endanger the altars; now pardon return to mansions.
translations.idiomatic: A third forgery pardoned their staffs: "Those ministers plotted against the state but their subordinates may go home untouched.

sentences.zh: 官屬以下，一無所問。

translations.literal: Officials and subordinates below, altogether nothing interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: Rank and file face no inquiry.

sentences.zh: 若不奉詔，便軍法從事。

translations.literal: If do not uphold edict, then military law handles matters.
translations.idiomatic: Disobey and martial law applies.

sentences.zh: 能率所領先出降者，封侯受賞。

translations.literal: Those able to lead those commanded first to come out surrender, enfeoff marquis receive reward.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever brings his unit out first to yield receives a marquisate and reward.

sentences.zh: 朕不食言。

translations.literal: We do not eat words.
translations.idiomatic: The throne does not break its word.

sentences.zh: 」遂收亮、瓘，殺之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon seized Liang and Guan, killed them.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang and Guan were seized and killed.

sentences.zh: 岐盛說瑋，可因兵勢誅賈模、郭彰，匡正王室，以安天下。

translations.literal: Qi Sheng persuaded Wei: may ride army momentum execute Jia Mo and Guo Zhang, rectify upright the royal house, thereby pacify All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Sheng urged Wei to use the army to kill Jia Mo and Guo Zhang, restore the throne, and settle the realm.

sentences.zh: 瑋猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Wei hesitated not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Wei hesitated.

sentences.zh: 會天明，帝用張華計，遣殿中將軍王宮齎騶虞幡麾眾曰：「楚王矯詔。

translations.literal: When dawn brightened, the emperor employed Zhang Hua's plan; sent Palace-Hall General Wang Gong carrying the Zouyu banner to signal the masses saying: "Prince Chu falsely edict.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Emperor Hui followed Zhang Hua's advice and sent Wang Gong into the ranks with the mercy banner crying, "The Prince of Chu forged his orders!

sentences.zh: 」眾皆釋杖而走。

translations.literal: " The masses all released staffs and ran.
translations.idiomatic: " The troops dropped their weapons and fled.

sentences.zh: 瑋左右無復一人，窘迫不知所為，惟一奴年十四，駕牛車將赴秦王柬。

translations.literal: Wei's left and right had no again one person; distressed urgent not knowing what to do; only one slave fourteen years old, driving ox cart about to go to Prince Su of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei stood abandoned and helpless with only a fourteen-year-old slave driving an ox cart toward Prince Su of Qin.

sentences.zh: 帝遣謁者詔瑋還營，執之于武賁署，遂下廷尉。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Herald to edict Wei return camp; seized him at Wuben office; thereupon handed down to Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent heralds ordering Wei back to camp, seized him at the palace guard office, and handed him to the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 詔以瑋矯制害二公父子，又欲誅滅朝臣，謀圖不軌，遂斬之，時年二十一。

translations.literal: An edict took Wei falsely controlling harmed two lords father and sons; further wished to execute annihilate court ministers; plotted without upright; thereupon beheaded him; at the time age twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: An edict condemned him for forging orders that killed two ministers and their sons, plotting to slaughter the bureaucracy—he was executed at twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 其日大風，雷雨霹靂。

translations.literal: That day great wind; thunder rain lightning thunderbolt.
translations.idiomatic: That day brought gale winds, thunder, and lightning.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「周公決二叔之誅，漢武斷昭平之獄，所不得已者。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The Duke of Zhou decided two uncles' executions; Han Wu judged Zhaoping's prison—what could not be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: The throne cited how the Duke of Zhou condemned his uncles and Emperor Wu cut short Princess Zhuoping—acts forced by circumstance.

sentences.zh: 廷尉奏瑋已伏法，情用悲痛，吾當發哀。

translations.literal: The Commandant memorialized Wei already submitted to law; feeling employs grief pain; We ought issue mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant reported Wei's execution with grief; the emperor would observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 」瑋臨死，出其懷中青紙詔，流涕以示監刑尚書劉頌曰：「受詔而行，謂為社稷，今更為罪，托體先帝，受枉如此，幸見申列。

translations.literal: " Wei facing death, produced from his bosom the green-paper edict; with flowing tears showed Supervising Execution Minister Liu Song saying: "Received edict and acted, thought it for altars of soil and grain; now further become crime; entrusted body former emperor; received injustice thus; fortunate see extend arrange.
translations.idiomatic: " At execution Wei drew the ink edict from his robe and wept as he showed Minister Liu Song: "I obeyed what I took for the state's good—now I am criminal though my blood comes from the late emperor; let my case be heard.

sentences.zh: 」頌亦歔欷不能仰視。

translations.literal: " Song also sobbed sigh could not look up.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Song wept and could not lift his eyes.

sentences.zh: 公孫宏、岐盛並夷三族。

translations.literal: Gongsun Hong and Qi Sheng together extirpated three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Hong and Qi Sheng were executed along with their extended kin.

sentences.zh: 瑋性開濟好施，能得眾心，及此莫不隕淚，百姓為之立祠。

translations.literal: Wei's nature was open and generous fond of giving; could obtain masses' hearts; reaching this none did not fall tears; common people for him erected shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was generous and popular—his death drew tears everywhere and commoners raised shrines to him.

sentences.zh: 賈后先惡瓘、亮，又忌瑋，故以計相次誅之。

translations.literal: Empress Jia first hated Guan and Liang; further feared Wei; therefore by stratagem in sequence executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia already hated Guan and Liang and feared Wei; she picked them off one by one by design.

sentences.zh: 永寧元年，追贈驃騎將軍，封其子范為襄陽王，拜散騎常侍，後為石勒所害。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongning, posthumously gifted General of Agile Cavalry; enfeoffed his son Fan as Prince of Xiangyang; appointed Regular Attendant at Leisure; later was harmed by Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongning he was posthumously named General of Agile Cavalry; his son Fan became Prince of Xiangyang with rank as Regular Attendant until Shi Le killed him.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao, Lun
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao

sentences.zh: 趙王倫，字子彝，宣帝第九子也，母曰柏夫人。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Lun, courtesy name Ziyi, was Emperor Xuan's ninth son; mother was called Lady Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, courtesy name Ziyi, was Emperor Xuan's ninth son by Lady Bo.

sentences.zh: 魏嘉平初，封安樂亭侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei Jiaping he was enfeoffed Marquis of Anle Precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei he became Marquis of Anle Precinct early in Jiaping.

sentences.zh: 五等建，改封東安子，拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were established, enfeoffment was changed to Viscount of Dong'an; appointed Grandee Remonstrant.
translations.idiomatic: When the five ranks were instituted he became Viscount of Dong'an and Grandee Remonstrant.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封琅邪郡王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received abdication, he was enfeoffed Prince of Langye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's Emperor Wu took the throne Lun became Prince of Langye Commandery.

sentences.zh: 坐使散騎將劉緝買工所將盜禦裘，廷尉杜友正緝棄市，倫當與緝同罪。

translations.literal: Sitting because he caused General of Attendant Cavalry Liu Ji to buy what craftsmen commanded stolen imperial fur robe; Commandant Du You corrected Ji abandoned market; Lun ought share same guilt with Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He had lent Liu Ji of the Palace Guard money to buy stolen imperial fur; Commandant Du You sentenced Ji to public execution, and Lun faced the same charge.

sentences.zh: 有司奏倫爵重屬親，不可坐。

translations.literal: The offices memorialized Lun's rank heavy kin relation, cannot sit guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Officials argued Lun's noble rank and kinship exempted him.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫劉毅駁曰：「王法賞罰，不阿貴賤，然後可以齊禮制而明典刑也。

translations.literal: Grandee Remonstrant Liu Yi refuted saying: "Royal law rewards punishments, does not bend noble base; after then can align ritual regulation and clarify statutes punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Grandee Remonstrant Liu Yi answered: "Law must judge high and low alike or ritual and punishment mean nothing.

sentences.zh: 倫知裘非常，蔽不語吏，與緝同罪。

translations.literal: Lun knew the fur was not ordinary; concealed did not speak to clerks; shares same guilt with Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Lun knew the robe was contraband yet hid it from the judge—he shares Ji's guilt.

sentences.zh: 當以親貴議減，不得闕而不論。

translations.literal: Ought by kin noble discuss reduction; cannot omit and not discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Kinship may commute the sentence but cannot excuse silence.

sentences.zh: 宜自于一時法中，如友所正。

translations.literal: Ought self fall within one time law within, as You corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Apply the statute as Du You ruled.

sentences.zh: 」帝是毅駁，然以倫親親故，下詔赦之。

translations.literal: " The emperor affirmed Yi's refutation; yet because Lun was kin kin reason, issued edict pardoning him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted Liu Yi's argument yet pardoned Lun as kin.

sentences.zh: 及之國，行東中郎將、宣威將軍。

translations.literal: When he reached his state, he bore General of the Central Army of the East and General Who Spreads Might.
translations.idiomatic: Upon taking up his fief he served as East Central Army general and General Who Spreads Might.

sentences.zh: 咸甯中，改封于趙，遷平北將軍、督鄴城守事，進安北將軍。

translations.literal: In Xianning, enfeoffment was changed to Zhao; transferred General Who Pacifies the North, supervised Ye city guard affairs; advanced General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianning his title shifted to Zhao; he rose from General Who Pacifies the North overseeing Ye's defenses to General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 元康初，遷征西將軍、開府儀同三司，鎮關中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang, transferred General Who Conquers the West, opening office with ceremonial equal to Three Offices, garrisoned Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuankang he became General Who Conquers the West with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies and held Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 倫刑賞失中，氐、羌反叛，征還京師。

translations.literal: Lun punishments rewards missed center; Di and Qiang rebelled; summoned returned capital.
translations.idiomatic: Misrule of rewards and punishments stirred Di and Qiang revolts and brought him back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 尋拜車騎將軍、太子太傅。

translations.literal: Shortly appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He soon added General of Chariots and Cavalry and tutorship of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 深交賈、郭，諂事中宮，大為賈后所親信。

translations.literal: Deeply befriended Jia and Guo; flattered serving central palace; greatly by Empress Jia was trusted intimate.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated Jia Mo and Guo Zhang, toadied to the empress, and became her close confidant.

sentences.zh: 求錄尚書，張華、裴頠固執不可。

translations.literal: Requested recorder Masters of Writing; Zhang Hua and Pei Wei firmly held not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: He sought charge of the Secretariat; Zhang Hua and Pei Wei refused.

sentences.zh: 又求尚書令，華、頠復不許。

translations.literal: Further requested Director of Masters of Writing; Hua and Wei again did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to head the Secretariat; again Zhang Hua and Pei Wei blocked him.

sentences.zh: 湣懷太子廢，使倫領右軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Minhuai was deposed Lun was made to head the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Minhuai was cast aside, Lun was put in charge of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 時左衛司馬督司馬雅及常從督許超，並嘗給事東宮，二人傷太子無罪，與殿中中郎士猗等謀廢賈后，復太子，以華、頠不可移，難與圖權，倫執兵之要，性貪冒，可假以濟事，乃說倫嬖人孫秀曰：「中宮凶妒無道，與賈謐等共廢太子。

translations.literal: At that time Left Guard Army Supervisor Sima Ya and Regular Escort Commander Xu Chao had both once served the Eastern Palace; the two grieved that the crown prince was without guilt; with Palace-Hall Gentleman Shi Yi and others they plotted to depose Empress Jia and restore the crown prince; since Hua and Yi could not be shifted, difficult with them to scheme power; Lun held the military's critical points, his nature greedy and reckless—could borrow him to complete the affair—thereupon they persuaded Lun's favorite Sun Xiu saying: "The central palace is fierce jealous without the Way; together with Jia Mi and others they deposed the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard supervisor Sima Ya and escort commander Xu Chao, both former Eastern Palace attendants, grieved over the heir's unjust deposition. With palace officer Shi Yi they hoped to restore him, but Zhang Hua and Pei Yi could not be moved; Lun alone held real troops and was venal—usable as their lever. They approached Sun Xiu, Lun's favorite: "The empress is cruel and lawless; she and Jia Mi brought down the heir.

sentences.zh: 今國無嫡嗣，社稷將危，大臣將起大事。

translations.literal: Now the state has no legitimate heir; the altars will be in peril; great ministers will raise great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With no rightful heir the altars are endangered and great ministers will rise in arms.

sentences.zh: 而公名奉事中宮，與賈、郭親善，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一朝事起，禍必相及。

translations.literal: Yet your lordship's name serves the central palace in affairs; with Jia and Guo you are intimate good; the crown prince's deposition—all say you knew beforehand; once one morning affairs arise, disaster surely will reach together.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you serve the empress and keep company with Jia and Guo; rumor says you knew the heir's fate in advance—when the reckoning comes you will share their guilt.

sentences.zh: 何不先謀之乎？

translations.literal: Why not first plot against her?
translations.idiomatic: Why not strike first?

sentences.zh: 」秀許諾，言於倫，倫納焉。

translations.literal: " Xiu promised; spoke to Lun; Lun accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu agreed, relayed it to Lun, and Lun took the bait.

sentences.zh: 遂告通事令史張林及省事張衡、殿中侍御史殷渾、右衛司馬督路始，使為內應。

translations.literal: Thereupon he told Petition Clerk Zhang Lin and Shortening Affairs Zhang Heng, Palace Attendant Censor Yin Hun, Right Guard Army Supervisor Lu Shi, causing them to be inner correspondents.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted Petition Clerk Zhang Lin, Zhang Heng of the Secretariat, Censor Yin Hun, and Right Guard supervisor Lu Shi as inside agents.

sentences.zh: 事將起，而秀知太子聰明，若還東宮，將與賢人圖政，量己必不得志，乃更說倫曰：「太子為人剛猛，不可私請。

translations.literal: When the affair was about to rise, Xiu knew the crown prince was clever; if he returned to the Eastern Palace, he would with worthy men plan government; reckoning himself surely could not achieve his aims; thereupon further persuaded Lun saying: "The crown prince as a person is fierce and harsh; cannot be privately petitioned.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the coup Xiu realized the heir was quick-witted: restored to the Eastern Palace he would rule with good men and leave no room for Xiu's ambition. He talked Lun round again: "That heir is fierce and proud—you cannot win him with private pleas.

sentences.zh: 明公素事賈后，時議皆以公為賈氏之黨。

translations.literal: The enlightened duke has always served Empress Jia; current discussion all takes the duke as Jia clan's faction.
translations.idiomatic: You have long served the empress; everyone counts you part of the Jia circle.

sentences.zh: 今雖欲建大功于太子，太子含宿怒，必不加賞於明公矣。

translations.literal: Now although you wish to establish great merit for the crown prince, the crown prince harbors overnight rage; surely he will not add reward to the enlightened duke.
translations.idiomatic: Even if you now win him the throne, old resentments will keep him from rewarding you.

sentences.zh: 當謂逼百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳。

translations.literal: He will say you crossed common expectation to flip and escape guilt only.
translations.idiomatic: He will say you bowed only to popular pressure and switched sides to save yourself.

sentences.zh: 此乃所以速禍也。

translations.literal: This is the means whereby hastening disaster.
translations.idiomatic: That path leads straight to ruin.

sentences.zh: 今且緩其事，賈后必害太子，然後廢後，為太子報仇，亦足以立功，豈徒免禍而已。

translations.literal: Now for the moment slow this affair; Empress Jia surely will harm the crown prince; afterward depose the empress, avenge the crown prince—also sufficient to establish merit; how only escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Better wait: Jia will murder the heir herself; then topple the empress and avenge him—you gain credit without merely saving your skin.

sentences.zh: 」倫從之。

translations.literal: " Lun followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Lun agreed.

sentences.zh: 秀乃微泄其謀，使謐党頗聞之。

translations.literal: Xiu thereupon slightly leaked their plot, causing Mi's faction somewhat to hear it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu quietly leaked the plot so Jia Mi's people caught wind of it.

sentences.zh: 倫、秀因勸謐等早害太子，以絕眾望。

translations.literal: Lun and Xiu thereby urged Mi and others early to harm the crown prince, to cut off popular expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Lun and Xiu then urged Jia Mi to kill the heir at once and crush public hope.

sentences.zh: 太子既遇害，倫、秀之謀益甚，而超、雅懼後難，欲悔其謀，乃辭疾。

translations.literal: After the crown prince had suffered murder, Lun and Xiu's plotting grew worse; while Chao and Ya feared later difficulties and wished to regret their plot, then declining illness.
translations.idiomatic: Once the heir was dead Lun and Xiu pressed harder; Xu Chao and Sima Ya, fearing blowback, feigned illness to back out.

sentences.zh: 秀復告右衛佽飛督閭和，和從之，期四月三日丙夜一籌，以鼓聲為應。

translations.literal: Xiu further told Right Guard Crossbow-Fleet Commander Lü He; He followed it; scheduled third day of fourth month at first watch after midnight one tally, using drum sound as signal.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu enlisted Right Guard fleet commander Lü He for the coup timed to the third of the fourth month, first watch, signaled by drums.

sentences.zh: 至期，乃矯詔敕三部司馬曰：「中宮與賈謐等殺吾太子，今使車騎入廢中宮。

translations.literal: When the time arrived, then falsely by edict ordered the Three Department Majors saying: "The central palace together with Jia Mi and others killed our crown prince; now dispatch chariots and cavalry to enter and depose the central palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the hour he forged orders to the Three Majors: "The empress and Jia Mi murdered the heir—send the army to depose her."

sentences.zh: 汝等皆當從命，賜爵關中侯。

translations.literal: You all ought obey command; bestow noble rank Marquis Within-the-Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Obey and you will be enfeoffed marquises of Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 不從，誅三族。

translations.literal: Disobey—execute three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Refuse and face extinction of three clans.

sentences.zh: 」於是眾皆從之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the masses all followed.
translations.idiomatic: The troops fell in line.

sentences.zh: 倫又矯詔開門夜入，陳兵道南，遣翊軍校尉、齊王冏將三部司馬百人，排閣而入。

translations.literal: Lun again falsely by edict opened gates entering by night; arrayed troops south of the avenue; sent Colonel of the Guards Army Prince Jiong of Qi leading Three Department Majors one hundred men, pushed gates and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Lun forged another order to open the gates by night, drew up troops along the palace road, and sent Colonel of the Guards Prince Jiong of Qi with a hundred Three-Major troops bursting through the gates.

sentences.zh: 華林令駱休為內應，迎帝幸東堂。

translations.literal: Hualin Commandant Luo Xiu was inner correspondent; welcomed the emperor to favor Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Hualin superintendent Luo Xiu acted as insider and brought Emperor Hui to the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 遂廢賈后為庶人，幽之於建始殿。

translations.literal: Thereupon deposed Empress Jia as commoner; confined her at Jianshi Hall.
translations.idiomatic: They deposed Empress Jia to commoner rank and locked her in Jianshi Hall.

sentences.zh: 收吳太妃、趙粲及韓壽妻賈午等，付暴室考竟。

translations.literal: Seized Consort Wu of Wu, Zhao Can, and Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and others; handed to Rough Chamber for interrogation to death.
translations.idiomatic: They arrested Lady Wu, Zhao Can, Jia Wu wife of Han Shou, and sent them to the harem jail for interrogation and execution.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書以廢後事，仍收捕賈謐等，召中書監、侍中、黃門侍郎、八坐，皆夜入殿，執張華、裴頠、解結、杜斌等，於殿前殺之。

translations.literal: Edict ordered Masters of Writing on deposing empress affair; still seized and arrested Jia Mi and others; summoned Palace Secretariat Supervisor, Palace Attendants, Gentlemen of Yellow Gate and Eight Seats—all entered hall by night; seized Zhang Hua, Pei Yi, Xie Jie, Du Bin and others; before the hall killed them.
translations.idiomatic: The forged edict had the Secretariat handle the empress's deposition while guards seized Jia Mi and summoned high ministers into the palace by night—Zhang Hua, Pei Yi, Xie Jie, Du Bin were seized and slaughtered before the hall.

sentences.zh: 尚書始疑詔有詐，郎師景露版奏請手詔。

translations.literal: Masters of Writing first suspected the edict had fraud; Gentleman Lang Shi Jing exposed tablet memorial requesting handwritten edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat doubted the decree until Clerk Shi Jing demanded to see the emperor's own brush—and died for it.

sentences.zh: 倫等以為沮眾，斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Lun and others took it as discouraging the masses; beheaded him to display.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's faction executed him as an example.

sentences.zh: 明日，倫坐端門，屯兵北向，遣尚書和郁持節送賈庶人于金墉。

translations.literal: Next day Lun sat at Duan Gate; garrisoned troops facing north; dispatched Masters of Writing He Yu bearing credentials to escort Commoner Jia to Brick Granary.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Lun held court at Duan Gate with troops to the north while He Yu convoyed the deposed empress to the Brick Granary fortress.

sentences.zh: 誅趙粲叔父中護軍趙浚及散騎侍郎韓豫等，內外群官多所黜免。

translations.literal: Executed Zhao Can's uncle Central Protector Zhao Jun and Gentleman Attendant Han Yu and others; inner and outer host of officials many dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Zhao Jun and Han Yu among others and purged scores of officials inside and outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 倫尋矯詔自為使持節、大都督、督中外諸軍事、相國，侍中、王如故，一依宣、文輔魏故事，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎四人、參軍十人，掾屬二十人、兵萬人。

translations.literal: Lun soon falsely by edict made himself credential-bearing commander-in-chief supervising all armies within and without, Chancellor of State; Palace Attendant and prince as before; wholly according to Xuan and Wen assisting Wei precedent; established Left and Right Chief Clerks, Majors, Retainers four persons, Adjutants ten persons, clerks twenty persons, troops ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lun forged his promotion to commander-in-chief and chancellor with ten thousand household guards and a full princely staff on the model of Sima Yi and Sima Zhao.

sentences.zh: 以其世子散騎常侍荂領冗從僕射；

translations.literal: His heir son Gentleman Attendant Fu commanded Retinue Inspector;
translations.idiomatic: Heir Sima Fu, as Gentleman Attendant, headed the Retinue Inspectorate;

sentences.zh: 子馥前將軍，封濟陽王；

translations.literal: Son Fu (馥) Forward General; enfeoffed Prince of Jiyang;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Fu was Forward General and Prince of Jiyang;

sentences.zh: 虔黃門郎，封汝陰王；

translations.literal: Qian (虔) Gentleman of Yellow Gate; enfeoffed Prince of Ruyin;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian became Gentleman of Yellow Gate and Prince of Ruyin;

sentences.zh: 羽散騎侍郎，封霸城侯。

translations.literal: Yu (羽) Gentleman Attendant; enfeoffed Marquis of Bacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yu became Gentleman Attendant and Marquis of Bacheng.

sentences.zh: 孫秀等封皆大郡，並據兵權，文武官封侯者數千人，百官總己聽於倫。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu and others enfeoffments all great commanderies; together grasped military authority; civil and martial officials enfeoffed marquis were several thousand persons; hundred officials all bent themselves listening to Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu and allies took rich fiefs and army commands; thousands of petty favorites gained noble ranks while every office answered to Lun.

sentences.zh: 倫素庸下，無智策，復受制於秀，秀之威權振於朝廷，天下皆事秀而無求於倫。

translations.literal: Lun was vulgar and low by nature, without wise stratagem; further was controlled by Xiu; Xiu's awe authority shook at court; All-under-Heaven all served Xiu and had no requests for Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was dull and witless, wholly dominated by Sun Xiu until court and realm answered to Xiu, not Lun.

sentences.zh: 秀起自琅邪小史，累官于趙國，以諂媚自達。

translations.literal: Xiu rose from Langye petty clerk; accumulated office in Zhao commandery; by flattery attained himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu rose from a petty clerk in Langye to Zhao staff through flattery alone.

sentences.zh: 既執機衡，遂恣其奸謀，多殺忠良，以逞私欲。

translations.literal: Once grasping the scales of power, thereupon indulged his treacherous plots; many killed loyal good to display private desires.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held power he slaughtered loyal men to satisfy private spite.

sentences.zh: 司隸從事游顥與殷渾有隙，渾誘顥奴晉興，偽告顥有異志。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Clerk You Yi had rift with Yin Hun; Hun enticed Yi's slave Jin Xing; falsely reported Yi had different intent.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial aide You Yi feuded with Yin Hun; Hun bribed Yi's slave Jin Xing to accuse him of treason.

sentences.zh: 秀不詳察，即收顥及襄陽中正李邁，殺之，厚待晉興，以為己部曲督。

translations.literal: Xiu did not examine in detail; immediately seized Yi and Xiangyang Rectifier Li Mai; killed them; generously treated Jin Xing; made him his troop commander.
translations.idiomatic: Without inquiry Xiu seized You Yi and Li Mai and executed them, then rewarded Jin Xing as his guard commander.

sentences.zh: 前衛尉石崇、黃門郎潘嶽皆與秀有嫌，並見誅。

translations.literal: Former Commandant of Guards Shi Chong and Gentleman Attendant Pan Yue both had grudge with Xiu; together were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Former Commandant Shi Chong and Gentleman Pan Yue, old enemies of Xiu, shared their fate.

sentences.zh: 於是京邑君子不樂其生矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon capital worthy gentlemen did not rejoice in living.
translations.idiomatic: No gentleman of the capital felt safe.

sentences.zh: 淮南王允、齊王冏以倫、秀驕僭，內懷不平。

translations.literal: Prince Yun of Huainan and Prince Jiong of Qi because Lun and Xiu were arrogant usurping inward cherished injustice.
