translations.idiomatic: Princes Yun of Huainan and Jiong of Qi nursed grievances against Lun and Xiu's arrogance.

sentences.zh: 秀等亦深忌焉，乃出冏鎮許，奪允護軍。

translations.literal: Xiu and others also deeply feared them; thereupon sent Jiong to garrison Xu; stripped Yun's Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu sidelined them—posting Jiong to Xu and stripping Yun of Central Protector command.

sentences.zh: 允發憤，起兵討倫。

translations.literal: Yun raised indignation; raised troops campaigning against Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yun rose in fury and marched against Lun.

sentences.zh: 允既敗滅，倫加九錫，增封五萬戶。

translations.literal: After Yun already defeated extinguished, Lun added nine bestowals; increased enfeoffment fifty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: After Yun fell Lun took the nine imperial gifts and fifty thousand more households.

sentences.zh: 倫偽為飾讓，詔遣百官詣府敦勸，侍中宣詔，然後受之。

translations.literal: Lun falsely made declining modesty; edict dispatched hundred officials to office earnestly urge; Palace Attendant proclaimed edict; afterward accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Lun staged refusals until officials besieged his mansion and a palace herald read an edict persuading him to accept.

sentences.zh: 加荂撫軍將軍、領軍將軍，馥鎮軍將軍、領護軍將軍，虔中軍將軍、領右衛將軍，詡為侍中。

translations.literal: Added heir Fu General Who Pacifies Army, General Who Commands Army; Fu General Who Guards Army, General Who Commands Protector Army; Qian General of Central Army, General Who Commands Right Guard; Xu was Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Sima Fu took pacification and command of armies; Sima Fu the younger led guard and protectorate forces; Sima Qian commanded central and right guard; Sima Xu became Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 又以孫秀為侍中、輔國將軍、相國司馬，右率如故。

translations.literal: Further made Sun Xiu Palace Attendant, General Who Supports the State, Chancellor of State Major; Right Escort as before.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu became Palace Attendant, supporting general, and chancellor's major while keeping his escort post.

sentences.zh: 張林等並居顯要。

translations.literal: Zhang Lin and others together occupied prominent importance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin and allies filled every key post.

sentences.zh: 增相府兵為二萬人，與宿衛同，又隱匿兵士，眾過三萬。

translations.literal: Increased chancellor office troops to twenty thousand, same as night guard; further concealed soldiers; masses exceeded thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Lun raised his headquarters guard to twenty thousand to match the palace army and hid extra troops until he commanded more than thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 起東宮三門四角華櫓，斷宮東西道為外徼。

translations.literal: Raised Eastern Palace three gates four corners flower watchtowers; cut palace east-west road as outer patrol.
translations.idiomatic: They raised watchtowers at the heir's three gates and sealed east-west palace avenues as outer cordons.

sentences.zh: 或謂秀曰：「散騎常侍楊准、黃門侍郎劉逵欲奉梁王肜以誅倫。

translations.literal: Someone told Xiu saying: "Regular Attendant Yang Zhun and Gentleman Attendant Liu Cheng wish to uphold Prince Rong of Liang to execute Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached Xiu that Yang Zhun and Liu Cheng meant to put Prince Rong of Liang at the head of a strike on Lun.

sentences.zh: 」會有星變，乃徙肜為丞相，居司徒府，轉准、逵為外官。

translations.literal: " Meeting there was stellar anomaly; thereupon moved Rong to Chancellor; dwelled at Minister of Education office; transferred Zhun and Cheng to outer offices.
translations.idiomatic: A celestial portent intervened: Prince Rong was named chancellor with offices at the Minister of Education while Yang Zhun and Liu Cheng were kicked to provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 倫無學，不知書；

translations.literal: Lun had no learning, did not know writing;
translations.idiomatic: Lun was barely literate;

sentences.zh: 秀亦以狡黠小才，貪淫昧利。

translations.literal: Xiu also by sly petty talent, greedy lewd blind to profit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu combined petty cunning with greed and lust.

sentences.zh: 所共立事者，皆邪佞之徒，惟競榮利，無深謀遠略。

translations.literal: Those together standing affairs were all wicked flatterers; only competed glory profit; had no deep plots far strategies.
translations.idiomatic: Their collaborators were all toadies scrambling for spoils with no foresight.

sentences.zh: 荂淺薄鄙陋，馥、虔暗很強戾，詡愚嚚輕訬，而各乖異，互相憎毀。

translations.literal: Heir Fu shallow thin base vulgar; Fu and Qian dim very harsh perverse; Xu foolish vicious light shallow; yet each contrary different; mutually hated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Fu was shallow and coarse; his brothers Fu and Qian were surly brutes; Xu was dull and malicious—they loathed one another openly.

sentences.zh: 秀子會，年二十，為射聲校尉，尚帝女河東公主。

translations.literal: Xiu's son Hui, age twenty, was Colonel of Sound-of-the-Bow; married emperor's daughter Princess of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's twenty-year-old son Hui became Colonel of Sound-of-the-Bow and married Princess Hedong.

sentences.zh: 公主母喪未期，便納聘禮。

translations.literal: Princess mother's mourning not yet full period; then accepted betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Betrothal gifts arrived before the princess mother's mourning year had run.

sentences.zh: 會形貌短陋，奴僕之下者，初與富室兒於城西販馬，百姓忽聞其尚主，莫不駭愕。

translations.literal: Hui's form appearance short ugly; below servants level; first with rich-house youths at city west selling horses; common people suddenly hearing he married princess; none not shocked.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was dwarfish and homely—once a horse-trader with rich youths west of the city—so commoners gaped when he married the princess.

sentences.zh: 倫、秀並惑巫鬼，聽妖邪之說。

translations.literal: Lun and Xiu together were deluded by witches and ghosts; listened to demon evil talk.
translations.idiomatic: Lun and Xiu dabbled in witchcraft and omens.

sentences.zh: 秀使牙門趙奉詐為宣帝神語，命倫早入西宮。

translations.literal: Xiu caused Gate Officer Zhao Feng fraudulently to act Emperor Xuan's spirit speech; ordered Lun early enter Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu had gate guard Zhao Feng fake Emperor Xuan's ghost commanding Lun to seize the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 又言宣帝於北芒為趙王佐助，於是別立宣帝廟於芒山。

translations.literal: Further said Emperor Xuan at Northern Mang acted Zhao King's assistant; thereupon separately established Emperor Xuan temple at Mang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: They claimed Emperor Xuan aided the Prince of Zhao from Mang Hill and built him a shrine there.

sentences.zh: 謂逆謀可成。

translations.literal: Saying rebellious plot could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: They told themselves the coup was Heaven's work.

sentences.zh: 以太子詹事裴劭、左軍將軍卞粹等二十人為從事中郎，掾屬又二十人。

translations.literal: Made Crown Prince Household Affairs Pei Shao and Left Army General Bian Cui and others twenty persons as retainers; clerks another twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty men including Pei Shao and Bian Cui became staff officers with another twenty clerks.

sentences.zh: 秀等部分諸軍，分佈腹心，使散騎常侍、義陽王威兼侍中，出納詔命，矯作禪讓之詔，使使持節、尚書令滿奮，僕射崔隨為副，奉皇帝璽綬以禪位於倫。

translations.literal: Xiu and others allocated various armies; distributed belly and heart; caused Gentleman Attendant Prince Wei of Yiyang concurrently Palace Attendant to exit and enter edict commands; falsely composed abdication edict; caused credential-bearing Director of Masters of Writing Man Fen, Deputy Director Cui Sui as deputies to bear emperor seals and ribbons to abdicate position to Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu stacked commands with cronies, made Prince Wei of Yiyang gatekeeper of edicts, forged abdication, and sent Man Fen and Cui Sui with the imperial seals to offer the throne to Lun.

sentences.zh: 倫偽讓不受。

translations.literal: Lun falsely declined not accepting.
translations.idiomatic: Lun theatrically refused—once.

sentences.zh: 於是宗室諸王、群公卿士咸假稱符瑞天文以勸進，倫乃許之。

translations.literal: Thereupon imperial clan various kings, host of dukes ministers all falsely claimed talisman omens astronomy to urge advance; Lun then permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and ministers chimed in with forged omens until Lun accepted.

sentences.zh: 左衛王輿與前軍司馬雅等率甲士入殿，譬喻三部司馬，示以威賞，皆莫敢違。

translations.literal: Left Guard Wang Yu with Forward Army Sima Ya and others led armored soldiers entering hall; illustrated Three Department Majors; showed them awe rewards; all none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard Wang Yu and Forward Army commander Sima Ya marched armored troops into the hall, threatened and bribed the Three Majors, and faced no refusal.

sentences.zh: 其夜，使張林等屯守諸門。

translations.literal: That night caused Zhang Lin and others garrison guard various gates.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin sealed every gate.

sentences.zh: 義陽王威及駱休等逼奪天子璽綬。

translations.literal: Prince Wei of Yiyang and Luo Xiu and others forced seize Son of Heaven seals and ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei and Luo Xiu wrested the imperial seals from Hui.

sentences.zh: 夜漏未盡，內外百官以乘輿法駕迎倫。

translations.literal: Night clepsydra not yet exhausted; inner and outer hundred officials with imperial carriage law escort welcomed Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn the whole bureaucracy drew up the imperial carriage to fetch Lun.

sentences.zh: 惠帝乘雲母車，鹵簿數百人，自華林西門出居金墉城。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui rode mica carriage; halberd escort several hundred persons; from Hualin west gate exited dwelling Brick Granary fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui left by mica carriage with a few hundred attendants through Hualin's west gate for house arrest at Brick Granary.

sentences.zh: 尚書和郁，兼侍中、散騎常侍、琅邪王睿，中書侍郎陸機從，到城下而反。

translations.literal: Masters of Writing He Yu, concurrently Palace Attendant, Gentleman Attendant Prince Rui of Langye; Masters of Writing Gentleman Lu Ji followed; arrived city wall below then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He Yu, Prince Rui of Langye, and Lu Ji escorted him to the fortress wall and turned back.

sentences.zh: 使張衡衛帝，實幽之也。

translations.literal: Caused Zhang Heng guard emperor; truly confined him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng's "guard" was imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 倫從兵五千人，入自端門，登太極殿，滿奮、崔隨、樂廣進璽綬於倫，乃僭即帝位，大赦，改元建始。

translations.literal: Lun followed troops five thousand persons; entered from Duan Gate; ascended Supreme Ultimate Hall; Man Fen, Cui Sui, Yue Guang advanced seals and ribbons to Lun; then usurped ascending emperor position; great amnesty; changed era inception Jianshi.
translations.idiomatic: Lun entered Duan Gate with five thousand men, climbed the Taiji Hall, took the seals from Man Fen, Cui Sui, and Yue Guang, declared himself emperor, amnestied the realm, and proclaimed era Jianshi.

sentences.zh: 是歲，賢良方正、直言、秀才、孝廉、良將皆不試；

translations.literal: That year Worthy and Good Upright, Straight Speech, Flourishing Talent, Filial Integrity, Fine General all were not examined;
translations.idiomatic: That year's examinations for Worthy and Good, straight critics, flourished talents, filial clerks, and fine generals were cancelled;

sentences.zh: 計吏及四方使命之在京邑者，太學生年十六以上及在學二十年，皆署吏；

translations.literal: account clerks and four quarters missions' envoys at capital; Imperial University students age sixteen above and at study twenty years—all appointed clerks;
translations.idiomatic: every clerk and envoy in the capital plus students over sixteen or twenty years enrolled received appointments;

sentences.zh: 郡縣二千石令長赦日在職者，皆封侯；

translations.literal: commanderies and counties two thousand shi magistrates long those on duty at amnesty day—all enfeoffed marquises;
translations.idiomatic: every magistrate still in office on amnesty day became a marquis;

sentences.zh: 郡綱紀並為孝廉，縣綱紀為廉史。

translations.literal: commandery administrators all became Filial Integrity; county administrators became Integrity Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: commandery aides turned into "filial integrity" picks and county aides into petty "integrity" clerks.

sentences.zh: 以世子荂為太子，馥為侍中、大司農、領護軍、京兆王，虔為侍中、大將軍領軍、廣平王，詡為侍中、撫軍將軍、霸城王，孫秀為侍中、中書監、驃騎將軍、儀同三司，張林等諸黨皆登卿將，並列大封。

translations.literal: Made heir son Fu crown prince; Fu Palace Attendant, Grand Minister of Agriculture, concurrently Protector, Prince of Jingzhao; Qian Palace Attendant, Grand General commanding army, Prince of Guangping; Xu Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies Army, Prince of Bacheng; Sun Xiu Palace Attendant, Palace Secretariat Supervisor, General of Agile Cavalry, ceremonial equal Three Offices; Zhang Lin and various faction all ascended ministers and generals; together ranked great enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: He named heir Fu crown prince, piled minister-general titles on Fu, Qian, and Xu, gave Sun Xiu the Secretariat and agile cavalry with Three Excellencies ritual, and promoted Zhang Lin's clique wholesale.

sentences.zh: 其餘同謀者咸超階越次，不可勝紀，至於奴卒斯役亦加以爵位。

translations.literal: The rest joint plotters all skipped ranks crossed order; could not be recorded exhaustively; reaching slaves runners menials also added noble positions.
translations.idiomatic: Every co-conspirator jumped ranks—uncountable—and even slaves received noble titles.

sentences.zh: 每朝會，貂蟬盈坐，時人為之顏曰：「貂不足，狗尾續。

translations.literal: Each court meeting sable-cicadas filled seats; people of the time for it rhymed saying: "Sables insufficient; dog tails continue.
translations.idiomatic: Court sessions swarmed with high caps till jesters sang: "Too few sable tails—sew on dogs'."

sentences.zh: 」而以苟且之惠取悅人情，府庫之儲不充于賜，金銀冶鑄不給于印，故有白版之侯，君子恥服其章，百姓亦知其不終矣。

translations.literal: " And by careless favors pleasing human sentiment; treasury stores did not suffice for gifts; gold silver casting smelting did not supply for seals; therefore there were white-board marquises; gentlemen ashamed wore their insignia; common people also knew they would not end.
translations.idiomatic: Cheap patronage emptied the treasury—metal ran short for seals—so "white-board marquises" wore blank tablets; gentlemen blushed at their badges and commoners knew the regime could not last.

sentences.zh: 倫親祠太廟，還，遇大風，飄折麾蓋。

translations.literal: Lun personally sacrificed Grand Temple; returning met great wind; blew broke banner canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from ancestral sacrifice Lun met a gale that snapped his canopy.

sentences.zh: 孫秀既立非常之事，倫敬重焉。

translations.literal: After Sun Xiu had established unusual affair, Lun respected him heavily.
translations.idiomatic: After the usurpation Lun deferred to Xiu slavishly.

sentences.zh: 秀住文帝為相國時所居內府，事無巨細，必諮而後行。

translations.literal: Xiu dwelled at Wen Emperor when Chancellor dwelled inner office; affairs nothing huge tiny; must consult afterward act.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu moved into Emperor Wen's old chancellery and stalled every decree until he approved.

sentences.zh: 倫之詔令，秀輒改革，有所與奪，自書青紙為詔，或朝行夕改者數四，百官轉易如流矣。

translations.literal: Lun's edict commands Xiu then altered reform; having grants and takings; himself wrote green paper as edict; sometimes morning act evening changed four times; hundred officials rotated changed like flowing.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's edicts passed through Xiu's edits—green-paper orders scribbled by Xiu—sometimes four revisions from dawn to dusk while offices spun like a mill.

sentences.zh: 時有雉入殿中，自太極東階上殿，驅之，更飛西鐘下，有頃，飛去。

translations.literal: At time there was pheasant entering hall; from Supreme Ultimate east steps ascended hall; drove it; again flew west bell below; after a moment flew away.
translations.idiomatic: A pheasant flew into the hall, climbed the eastern stairs of Taiji, darted under the western bell, then vanished.

sentences.zh: 又倫於殿上得異鳥，問皆不知名，累日向夕，宮西有素衣小兒言是服劉鳥。

translations.literal: Further Lun on hall obtained strange bird; asked all did not know name; accumulated days toward evening; palace west had white-clothed small child saying it was Fu Liu bird.
translations.idiomatic: Lun caught another strange bird none could name until a white-robed boy west of the palace called it the "Fu Liu" creature.

sentences.zh: 倫使錄小兒並鳥閉置牢室，明旦開視，戶如故，並失人鳥所在。

translations.literal: Lun caused seize small child together bird close imprison jail chamber; next dawn opened look; door as before; together lost person bird whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: Guards caged boy and bird overnight; by dawn door sealed tight—both had vanished.

sentences.zh: 倫目上有瘤，時以為妖焉。

translations.literal: Lun eye above had tumor; at time took as demon.
translations.idiomatic: A cyst disfigured Lun's brow—taken for an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 時齊王冏、河間王顒、成都王穎並擁強兵，各據一方。

translations.literal: At time Prince Jiong of Qi, Prince Yong of Hejian, Prince Ying of Chengdu together grasped strong troops; each occupied one corner.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Jiong of Qi, Yong of Hejian, and Ying of Chengdu held powerful armies in separate quarters.

sentences.zh: 秀知冏等必有異圖，乃選親黨及倫故吏為三王參佐及郡守。

translations.literal: Xiu knew Jiong and others surely had different plans; thereupon selected intimate faction and Lun's former clerks as three kings' adjutants and commandery governors.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu suspected the three princes and planted cronies as their staff and prefects.

sentences.zh: 秀本與張林有隙，雖外相推崇，內實忌之。

translations.literal: Xiu originally with Zhang Lin had rift; although outward mutually esteemed; inward truly feared.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu and Zhang Lin despised each other despite polite fronts.

sentences.zh: 及林為衛將軍，深怨不得開府，潛與荂箋，具說秀專權，動違眾心，而功臣皆小人，撓亂朝廷，要一時誅之。

translations.literal: When Lin became General of the Guard; deeply resented not obtaining opening office; secretly with Fu wrote letter; fully explained Xiu monopolized power; moved contrary masses' hearts; yet meritorious ministers all petty men; disturbed court; desired momentarily execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Named General of the Guard but denied independent headquarters, Zhang Lin secretly wrote heir Fu that Xiu tyrannized the court with petty allies who ought to die at once.

sentences.zh: 荂以書白倫，倫以示秀。

translations.literal: Fu by letter informed Lun; Lun showed Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu forwarded the letter to Lun, who showed Xiu.

sentences.zh: 秀勸倫誅林，倫從之。

translations.literal: Xiu persuaded Lun to execute Lin; Lun followed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu urged Lun to kill Zhang Lin, and Lun agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是倫請宗室會于華林園，召林、秀及王輿入，因收林，殺之，誅三族。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lun requested the imperial clan assemble at Hualin Garden; summoned Lin, Xiu, and Wang Yu to enter; thereby seized Lin; killed him; executed three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Lun summoned kinsmen to Hualin Park, lured in Zhang Lin and Sun Xiu with Wang Yu, arrested Zhang Lin, executed him, and wiped out three generations.

sentences.zh: 及三王起兵討倫檄至，倫、秀始大懼，遣其中堅孫輔為上軍將軍，積弩李嚴為折沖將軍，率兵七千自延壽關出，征虜張泓、左軍蔡璜、前軍閭和等率九千人自堮阪關出，鎮軍司馬雅、揚威莫原等率八千人自成皋關出。

translations.literal: When the three kings raised troops campaigning against Lun's proclamation arrived, Lun and Xiu began greatly afraid; dispatched his crack Sun Fu as Superior Army general; Repeated Crossbow Li Yan as Ram-crashing general; led troops seven thousand out from Yanshou Pass; Expedition-conqueror Zhang Hong, Left Army Cai Huang, Forward Army Lü He and others led nine thousand out from Eban Pass; Guard Army Sima Ya, Yang-awe Mo Yuan and others led eight thousand out from Chenggao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies' manifestos arrived Lun and Xiu panicked, deploying Sun Fu and Li Yan toward Yanshou, Zhang Hong and Cai Huang toward Eban, and Sima Ya toward Chenggao—some twenty-four thousand men.

sentences.zh: 召東平王楙為使持節、衛將軍，都督諸軍以距義師。

translations.literal: Summoned Prince Mao of Dongping credential-bearing General of the Guard to supervise all armies to withstand the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: He named Prince Mao of Dongping credential-bearing commander-in-chief to face the coalition.

sentences.zh: 使楊珍晝夜詣宣帝別廟祈請，輒言宣帝謝陛下，某日當破賊。

translations.literal: Caused Yang Zhen day and night to visit Emperor Xuan's separate temple praying; repeatedly said Emperor Xuan thanked Your Majesty; such day should defeat rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yang Zhen to Emperor Xuan's shrine round the clock with fabricated spirits thanking Emperor Hui and promising victory dates.

sentences.zh: 拜道士胡沃為太平將軍，以招福祐。

translations.literal: Appointed Daoist Hu Wo as Grand Peace general to summon fortune blessing.
translations.idiomatic: He titled Daoist Hu Wo "Grand Peace General" for supernatural aid.

sentences.zh: 秀家日為淫祀，作厭勝之文，使巫祝選擇戰日。

translations.literal: Xiu's household daily performed licentious sacrifices; composed suppression texts; caused shamans and prayer-masters to choose battle days.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's household kept impure sacrifices, curse tablets, and shamans picking auspicious days.

sentences.zh: 又令近親于嵩山著羽衣，詐稱仙人王喬，作神仙書，述倫祚長久以惑眾。

translations.literal: Further ordered close kin on Song Mountain to wear feather robes; falsely claimed immortal Wang Qiao; composed immortal scripture narrating Lun's reign long enduring to delude the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives on Mount Song posed as feather-robed immortals calling themselves Wang Qiao and circulated bogus scriptures claiming Lun would reign forever.

sentences.zh: 秀欲遣馥、虔領兵助諸軍戰，馥、虔不肯。

translations.literal: Xiu wished to dispatch Fu and Qian leading troops assisting various armies battle; Fu and Qian refused.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu ordered Fu and Qian into the field; both refused.

sentences.zh: 虔素親愛劉輿，秀乃使輿說虔，虔然後率眾八千為三軍繼援。

translations.literal: Qian was always intimate loving Liu Yu; Xiu thereupon caused Yu to persuade Qian; Qian afterward led masses eight thousand as three armies' follow-up relief.
translations.idiomatic: Qian adored Liu Yu; Xiu sent Liu Yu to sway him, so Qian brought eight thousand reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 而泓、雅等連戰雖勝，義軍散而輒合，雅等不得前。

translations.literal: Yet Hong, Ya and others linked battles although victorious, righteous army scattered yet assembled again; Ya and others could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Ya won skirmishes but the coalition re-formed each time and stalled their advance.

sentences.zh: 許超等與成都王穎軍戰于黃橋，殺傷萬餘人。

translations.literal: Xu Chao and others with Prince Ying of Chengdu's army battled at Yellow Bridge; wounded killed over ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chao clashed with Prince Ying at Yellow Bridge with casualties past ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 泓徑造陽翟，又于城南破齊王冏輜重，殺數千人，遂據城保邸閣。

translations.literal: Hong directly proceeded to Yangzhai; further south of city defeated Prince Jiong's baggage train; killed several thousand persons; thereupon held city protecting granary pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong pushed to Yangzhai, smashed Jiong's supply column south of the walls, killed thousands, and dug into the city granaries.

sentences.zh: 而冏軍已在潁陰，去陽翟四十里。

translations.literal: Yet Jiong's army already was at Yingyin, forty li from Yangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Jiong lay forty li away at Yingyin.

sentences.zh: 冏分軍渡潁，攻泓等不利。

translations.literal: Jiong divided army crossed Ying; attacked Hong and others unfavorably.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong split his force across the Ying but attacked Zhang Hong without success.

sentences.zh: 泓乘勝至於潁上，夜臨潁而陣。

translations.literal: Hong rode victory reaching Yingshang; night approached Ying and arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong pressed to Yingshang and drew up along the Ying by night.

sentences.zh: 冏縱輕兵擊之，諸軍不動，而孫輔、徐建軍夜亂，徑歸洛自首。

translations.literal: Jiong unleashed light troops struck them; various armies unmoved; yet Sun Fu, Xu Jian's army night rioted; straight returned Luoyang confessing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong sent raiders but lines held until Sun Fu and Xu Jian panicked at night and fled to Luoyang to surrender.

sentences.zh: 輔、建之走也，不知諸軍督尚存，乃云：「齊王兵盛，不可當，泓等已沒。

translations.literal: Fu and Jian's flight also did not know various armies supervisors still existed; then said: "Prince Qi's army mighty; cannot withstand; Hong and others already sunk.
translations.idiomatic: Those fugitives thought command still alive—yet lied that Hong had collapsed before mighty Qi army.

sentences.zh: 」倫大震，秘之，而召虔及超還。

translations.literal: " Lun greatly shook; concealed it; yet summoned Qian and Chao back.
translations.idiomatic: Lun hid the panic but recalled Qian and Xu Chao.

sentences.zh: 會泓敗冏露布至，倫大喜，及復遣超，而虔還已至庾倉。

translations.literal: Meeting Hong defeated Jiong bulletin arrived; Lun greatly rejoiced; and again dispatched Chao; yet Qian returning already reached Yu Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Then Hong's victory dispatch arrived and Lun exulted—resending Chao while Qian reached Yu Granary.

sentences.zh: 超還濟河，將士疑阻，銳氣內挫。

translations.literal: Chao returning crossed river; officers and men doubted obstructed; keen qi inward struck.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's troops crossed back doubtful—morale collapsed inward.

sentences.zh: 泓等悉其諸軍濟潁，進攻冏營，冏出兵擊其別率孫髦、司馬譚、孫輔，皆破之，士卒散歸洛陽，泓等收眾還營。

translations.literal: Hong and others exhausted their various armies crossed Ying; advanced attacked Jiong camp; Jiong sent troops struck their separate leads Sun Mao, Sima Tan, Sun Fu; all defeated them; soldiers scattered returned Luoyang; Hong and others gathered masses returned camp.
translations.idiomatic: Hong threw everything across the Ying against Jiong's camp; Jiong shattered detachments under Sun Mao, Sima Tan, and Sun Fu routing Lun's men back toward Luoyang while Hong regrouped.

sentences.zh: 秀等知三方日急，詐傳破冏營，執得冏，以誑惑其眾，令百官皆賀，而士猗、伏胤、孫會皆杖節各不相從。

translations.literal: Xiu and others knew three sides daily urgent; falsely transmitted destroying Jiong camp; seized obtained Jiong; to deceive delude their masses; ordered hundred officials all congratulate; yet Shi Yi, Fu Yin, Sun Hui all bore staffs each not obeying.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing three fronts tighten Xiu forged news of Jiong's capture to cheer Luoyang—officials feasted joy while Shi Yi, Fu Yin, and Sun Hui withheld cooperation.

sentences.zh: 倫復授太子詹事劉琨節，督河北將軍，率步騎千人催諸軍戰。

translations.literal: Lun again conferred Crown Prince Household Liu Kun staffs; supervised Hebei generals; led infantry cavalry thousand urging various armies battle.
translations.idiomatic: Lun handed staffs to Liu Kun to whip northern armies into renewed combat.

sentences.zh: 會等與義軍戰于激水，大敗，退保河上，劉琨燒斷河橋。

translations.literal: Hui and others with righteous army battled at Ji River; greatly defeated; retreated guarding river north; Liu Kun burned broke river bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui lost badly at Ji River, fled north of the stream while Liu Kun burned the bridges.

sentences.zh: 自義兵之起，百官將士咸欲誅倫、秀以謝天下。

translations.literal: From righteous army rising; hundred officials officers soldiers all wished execute Lun and Xiu to apologize All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Since the coalition rose every Luoyang soldier meant to kill Lun and Xiu to atone.

sentences.zh: 秀知眾怒難犯，不敢出省。

translations.literal: Xiu knew masses' wrath hard violate; dared not exit ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu feared the mob and stopped leaving his office.

sentences.zh: 及聞河北軍悉敗，憂懣不知所為。

translations.literal: When hearing Hebei army wholly defeated; anxious depressed not knowing what do.
translations.idiomatic: Northern collapse left him paralyzed with dread.

sentences.zh: 義陽王威勸秀至尚書省與八坐議征戰之備，秀從之。

translations.literal: Prince Wei of Yiyang urged Xiu go Masters of Writing hall debate eight seats expedition preparations; Xiu followed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei dragged Xiu to the Secretariat to plan defense.

sentences.zh: 使京城四品以下子弟年十五以上，皆詣司隸，從倫出戰。

translations.literal: Caused capital fourth rank below sons younger brothers age fifteen above; all proceed Metropolitan Office; follow Lun out battle.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted every youth under fourth rank aged fifteen or more through the Metropolitan Office for Lun's sortie.

sentences.zh: 內外諸軍悉欲劫殺秀，威懼，自崇禮闥走還下舍。

translations.literal: Inner outer various armies all wished seize kill Xiu; Wei feared; from Chongli Gate fled returned lower lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards meant to murder Xiu; Prince Wei fled Chongli Gate back to quarters.

sentences.zh: 許超、士猗、孫會等軍既並還，乃與秀謀，或欲收余卒出戰，或欲焚燒宮室，誅殺不附己者，挾倫南就孫旂、孟觀等，或欲乘船東走入海，許未決。

translations.literal: Xu Chao, Shi Yi, Sun Hui and others armies already together returned; then with Xiu plotted; some wished gather remnant troops exit battle; some wished burn palace halls; execute kill those not attaching self; seize Lun south join Sun Qi, Meng Guan and others; some wished ride boat east flee enter sea; agreement not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chao, Shi Yi, and Sun Hui met Xiu to debate fleeing south to allies, torching the palace, or escaping by sea—no decision.

sentences.zh: 王輿反之，率營兵七百餘人自南掖門入，敕宮中兵各守衛諸門，三部司馬為應於內。

translations.literal: Wang Yu turned against; led camp troops seven hundred persons from south Ye Gate entering; ordered palace troops each guard defend various gates; Three Department Majors responded within.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu defected with seven hundred men through the south Ye Gate, sealed palace gates, and wired Three Majors inside.

sentences.zh: 輿自往攻秀，秀閉中書南門。

translations.literal: Yu personally went attack Xiu; Xiu closed Secretariat south gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu assaulted Xiu who barred the Secretariat south gate.

sentences.zh: 輿放兵登牆燒屋，秀及超、猗遽走出，左衛將軍趙泉斬秀等以徇。

translations.literal: Yu released troops climbed wall burned houses; Xiu and Chao, Yi fled out hastily; Left Guard General Zhao Quan beheaded Xiu and others to display.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu scaled walls and fired the halls; Xiu, Xu Chao, and Shi Yi fled until Zhao Quan executed Xiu publicly.

sentences.zh: 收孫奇于右衛營，付廷尉誅之。

translations.literal: Seized Sun Qi at Right Guard camp; handed Commandant executed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qi was pulled from the Right Guard camp and killed under judgment.

sentences.zh: 執前將軍謝惔、黃門令駱休、司馬督王潛，皆於殿中斬之。

translations.literal: Seized Forward General Xie Dan, Yellow Gate Commandant Luo Xiu, Army Supervisor Wang Qian—all beheaded in hall.
translations.idiomatic: Forward general Xie Dan, eunuch Luo Xiu, and supervisor Wang Qian died in the hall.

sentences.zh: 三部司馬兵於宣化闥中斬孫弼以徇，時司馬馥在秀坐，輿使將士囚之於散騎省，以大戟守省閣。

translations.literal: Three Department Majors troops at Xuande Gate slew Sun Bi to display; at time Sima Fu sat with Xiu; Yu caused officers imprison him at Gentleman Attendant hall; with great halberds guarded hall gates.
translations.idiomatic: Palace troops killed Sun Bi at Xuande Gate; Fu sat beside Xiu until Wang Yu jailed him under halberd guard.

sentences.zh: 八坐皆入殿中，坐東除樹下。

translations.literal: Eight Seats all entered hall; sat east stairs trees below.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Seats gathered east of the hall beneath the trees.

sentences.zh: 王輿屯雲龍門，使倫為詔曰：「吾為孫秀等所誤，以怒三王。

translations.literal: Wang Yu garrisoned Cloud Dragon Gate; caused Lun make edict saying: "We were misled by Sun Xiu and others; thereby angered three kings.
translations.idiomatic: At Cloud Dragon Gate Wang Yu forced Lun to confess: "Sun Xiu misled me and provoked the three princes."

sentences.zh: 今已誅秀，其迎太上復位，吾歸老于農畝。

translations.literal: " Now already executed Xiu; welcome Grand Superior restoring position; We return old at farms.
translations.idiomatic: "Now Xiu is dead—welcome the abdicated emperor home while I retire to the fields."

sentences.zh: 」傳詔以騶虞幡敕將士解兵。

translations.literal: " Transmit edict using Zouyu banner ordered officers soldiers lay down arms.
translations.idiomatic: Heralds waved the mercy pennant ordering troops to stand down.

sentences.zh: 文武官皆奔走，莫敢有居者。

translations.literal: Civil martial officials all fled running; none dared dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Officials bolted—none lingered.

sentences.zh: 黃門將倫自華林東門出，及荂皆還汶陽裏第。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate escorted Lun from Hualin east gate out; together with Fu all returned Wenyang lane mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs hustled Lun out Hualin's east gate with heir Fu to their Wenyang mansion.

sentences.zh: 於是以甲士數千迎天子于金墉，百姓咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: Thereupon with armored soldiers several thousand welcomed Son of Heaven from Brick Granary; common people all called myriad years.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands in armor fetched Emperor Hui from Brick Granary amid cheers.

sentences.zh: 帝自端門入，升殿，禦廣室，送倫及荂等付金墉城。

translations.literal: Emperor from Duan Gate entered; ascended hall; rode Broad Chamber; sent Lun and Fu and others delivered Brick Granary fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Hui entered through Duan Gate to Broad Chamber consigning Lun and Fu to Brick Granary.

sentences.zh: 初，秀懼西軍至，復召虔還。

translations.literal: First Xiu feared western army arriving; again summoned Qian return.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xiu recalled Qian fearing western armies.

sentences.zh: 是日宿九曲，詔遣使者免虔官，虔懼，棄軍將數十人歸於汶陽裏。

translations.literal: That day lodged Jiuyu; edict dispatched envoy dismissed Qian office; Qian feared; abandoned army generals several tens persons returned Wenyang lane.
translations.idiomatic: That night at Jiuyu Hui stripped Qian's posts; Qian fled with dozens of followers to Wenyang.

sentences.zh: 梁王肜表倫父子凶逆，宜伏誅。

translations.literal: Prince Rong of Liang memorialized Lun father son fierce rebellious ought submit execution.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rong of Liang demanded Lun and his sons die for treason.

sentences.zh: 百官會議於朝堂，皆如肜表。

translations.literal: Hundred officials convened assembly at court hall; all like Rong memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Court debate unanimously echoed Prince Rong.

sentences.zh: 遣尚書袁敞持節賜倫死，飲以金屑苦酒。

translations.literal: Dispatched Masters of Writing Yuan Chang bearing staffs gifted Lun death; drank him gold dust bitter wine.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yuan Chang brought Lun gold-flaked poison wine.

sentences.zh: 倫慚，以巾覆面，曰：「孫秀誤我！

translations.literal: Lun ashamed; used kerchief cover face; said: "Sun Xiu misled me!
translations.idiomatic: Lun hid his face in a cloth crying Sun Xiu had ruined him.

sentences.zh: 孫秀誤我！

translations.literal: Sun Xiu misled me!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu misled me!

sentences.zh: 」於是收荂、馥、虔、詡付廷尉獄，考竟。

translations.literal: " Thereupon seized Fu, Fu, Qian, Xu handed Commandant prison; interrogated to death.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, Fu, Qian, and Xu went to jail and died under torture.

sentences.zh: 馥臨死謂虔曰：「坐爾破家也！

translations.literal: Fu facing death said to Qian: "Because you broke family!
translations.idiomatic: Fu told Qian on the scaffold, "You destroyed our house."

sentences.zh: 」百官是倫所用者，皆斥免之，台省府衛僅有存者，自兵興六十餘日，戰所殺害僅十萬人。

translations.literal: " Hundred officials those Lun had employed; all dismissed removed; terrace ministries palace guards barely survivors; from troops rising sixty odd days; battle places killed harmed nearly hundred thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's appointees were cashiered; bureau and guard posts barely staffed—in sixty days of war perhaps one hundred thousand died.

sentences.zh: 凡與倫為逆豫謀大事者：張林為秀所殺；

translations.literal: All who with Lun were rebellious pre-planned great affair: Zhang Lin was by Xiu killed;
translations.idiomatic: Among conspirators Zhang Lin died at Xiu's hands first;

sentences.zh: 許超、士猗、孫弼、謝惔、殷渾與秀為王輿所誅；

translations.literal: Xu Chao, Shi Yi, Sun Bi, Xie Dan, Yin Hun together with Xiu by Wang Yu executed;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chao, Shi Yi, Sun Bi, Xie Dan, and Yin Hun fell to Wang Yu with Xiu;

sentences.zh: 張衡、閭和、孫髦、高越自陽翟還，伏胤戰敗還洛陽，皆斬於東市；

translations.literal: Zhang Heng, Lü He, Sun Mao, Gao Yue from Yangzhai returned; Fu Yin battle defeated returned Luoyang—all beheaded at east market;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng, Lü He, Sun Mao, Gao Yue returning from Yangzhai and Fu Yin after defeat died at the east market;

sentences.zh: 蔡璜自陽翟降齊王冏，還洛自殺；

translations.literal: Cai Huang from Yangzhai surrendered Prince Jiong; returned Luoyang suicide;
translations.idiomatic: Cai Huang surrendered to Jiong then killed himself in Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 王輿以功免誅，後與東萊王蕤謀殺冏，又伏法。

translations.literal: Wang Yu by merit exempted execution; afterward with Prince Rui of Donglai plotted kill Jiong; again submitted law.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu was spared then later plotted with Prince Rui of Donglai against Jiong and paid with his life.

sentences.zh: 齊武閔王冏

translations.literal: Prince Wu Min of Qi Jiong
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong, Prince Wu Min of Qi

sentences.zh: 冏因眾心怨望，潛與離狐王盛、潁川王處穆謀起兵誅倫。

translations.literal: Jiong because masses' hearts resentment secretly with Lihu Wang Sheng, Yingchuan Wang Chu Mu plotted raise troops execute Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong exploited popular hatred to scheme with Wang Sheng of Lihu and Wang Chu Mu of Yingchuan against Lun.

sentences.zh: 倫遣腹心張烏覘之，烏反，曰：「齊無異志。

translations.literal: Lun dispatched belly-heart Zhang Wu spy them; Wu turned said: "Qi has no different intent.
translations.idiomatic: Lun sent Zhang Wu to scout; Wu reported no rebellion brewing.

sentences.zh: 」冏既有成謀未發，恐或泄，乃與軍司管襲殺處穆，送首於倫，以安其意。

translations.literal: " Jiong already had mature plot not issued; feared perhaps leak; then with army marshal Guan Xi killed Chu Mu; sent head to Lun; to settle his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong silenced leaks by having Guan Xi kill Chu Mu and sent the head to Lun as cover.

sentences.zh: 謀定，乃收襲殺之。

translations.literal: Plot settled; then seized Xi killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Once secure Jiong eliminated Guan Xi too.

sentences.zh: 遂與豫州刺史何勖、龍驤將軍董艾等起軍，遣使告成都、河間、常山、新野四王，移檄天下征鎮、州郡縣國，咸使聞知。

translations.literal: Then with Yu Province Inspector He Xu, Soaring Dragon general Dong Ai and others raised army; dispatched envoys informing Chengdu, Hejian, Changshan, Xinye four kings; moved proclamation All-under-Heaven expedition garrisons provinces counties states—all caused hear know.
translations.idiomatic: He mobilized with He Xu and Dong Ai, notified four princes, and circulated manifestos to every commandery.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史郗隆承檄，猶豫未決，參軍王邃斬之，送首於冏。

translations.literal: Yang Province Inspector Xi Long received proclamation; hesitated not decided; adjutant Wang Sui beheaded him; sent head to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Long wavered until adjutant Wang Sui killed him for Jiong.

sentences.zh: 冏屯軍陽翟，倫遣其將閭和、張泓、孫輔出堮阪，與冏交戰。

translations.literal: Jiong garrisoned Yangzhai; Lun dispatched his generals Lü He, Zhang Hong, Sun Fu out Eban; battled Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong held Yangzhai while Lun sent Zhang Hong through Eban against him.

sentences.zh: 冏軍失利，堅壘自守。

translations.literal: Jiong army unfavorable; strengthened ramparts self guarded.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong dug in after setbacks.

sentences.zh: 會成都軍破倫眾于黃橋，冏乃出軍攻和等，大破之。

translations.literal: Meeting Chengdu army defeated Lun masses at Yellow Bridge; Jiong then sent army attacked He and others; greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ying smashed Lun at Yellow Bridge Jiong sallied and routed Zhang Hong.

sentences.zh: 及王輿廢倫，惠帝反正，冏誅討賊党既畢，率眾入洛，頓軍通章署，甲士數十萬，旌旗器械之盛，震於京都。

translations.literal: When Wang Yu deposed Lun; Emperor Hui reversed correctness; Jiong executed punished rebel faction finished; led masses entered Luoyang; halted army Tongzhang office; armored soldiers several hundred thousand; banners weapons such splendor shook capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Yu toppled Lun Jiong entered Luoyang at Tongzhang Gate with hundreds of thousands in armor.

sentences.zh: 天子就拜大司馬，加九錫之命，備物典策，如宣、景、文、武輔魏故事。

translations.literal: Son of Heaven approached appointed Grand Marshal; added nine bestowals mandate; complete goods ceremonial slips; like Xuan, Jing, Wen, Wu assisting Wei precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named him Grand Marshal with the nine gifts like Sima Yi and his sons.

sentences.zh: 冏於是輔政，居攸故宮，置掾屬四十人。

translations.literal: Jiong thereupon assisted government; dwelled You's former palace; established adjutants forty persons.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong governed from Sima You's old mansion with forty staff officers.

sentences.zh: 大築第館，北取五穀市，南開諸署，毀壞廬舍以百數，使大匠營制，與西宮等。

translations.literal: Great built mansions halls; north took Five Grains Market; south opened various offices; destroyed ruined huts hovels numbering hundred; caused grand artisan construct regulate; equal western palace.
translations.idiomatic: He seized land north to the grain market and south to offices, demolishing hundreds of homes for a palace rivaling the western compound.

sentences.zh: 鑿千秋門牆以通西閣，後房施鐘懸，前庭舞八佾，沈於酒色，不入朝見。

translations.literal: Dug Thousand Autumn Gate wall to connect western pavilion; rear chambers hung bells; front court danced eight rows; sank in wine women; did not enter court audience.
translations.idiomatic: He broke through Thousand Autumn Gate for private halls with bells, eight-row dances, and endless revels—skipping formal audiences.

sentences.zh: 坐拜百官，符敕三台，選舉不均，惟寵親昵。

translations.literal: Sat appointing hundred officials; tally orders Three Terraces; selection promotion uneven; only favored intimate kin.
translations.idiomatic: He handed out posts by whim, routed orders through the Three Terraces, and favored cronies alone.

sentences.zh: 以車騎將軍何勖領中領軍。

translations.literal: Made General of Chariots He Xu concurrently Central Protector.
translations.idiomatic: He Xu became General of Chariots with Central Protector rank.

sentences.zh: 封葛<方與>為牟平公，路秀小黃公，衛毅陰平公，劉真安鄉公，韓泰封丘公，號曰「五公」，委以心膂。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed Ge Fangyu Marquis of Mouping, Lu Xiu Marquis of Xiaohuang, Wei Yi Marquis of Yinping, Liu Zhen Marquis of Anxiang, Han Tai Marquis of Fengqiu—called "Five Dukes"; entrusted belly back.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed the "Five Dukes"—Ge Fangyu, Lu Xiu, Wei Yi, Liu Zhen, Han Tai—as his core circle.

sentences.zh: 殿中御史桓豹奏事，不先經冏府，即考竟之。

translations.literal: Hall Censor Huan Bao submitted affairs; not first passing Jiong office; immediately interrogated death.
translations.idiomatic: Palace censor Huan Bao bypassed Jiong's bureau and died for it.

sentences.zh: 於是朝廷側目，海內失望矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon court sidelong glance; within seas disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers glared and the empire lost hope.

sentences.zh: 南陽處士鄭方露版極諫，主簿王豹屢有箴規，冏並不能用，遂奏豹殺之。

translations.literal: Nanyang recluse Zheng Fang exposed tablet utmost remonstrance; registrar Wang Bao repeatedly had admonition rules; Jiong together could not use; then memorialized Bao killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Recluse Zheng Fang remonstrated openly; registrar Wang Bao advised repeatedly—Jiong ignored both and executed Wang Bao.

sentences.zh: 有白頭公入大司馬府大呼，言有兵起，不出甲子旬。

translations.literal: There was white-haired old man entered Grand Marshal mansion great shouting; saying troops arising; not exiting within jiazi decade.
translations.idiomatic: A white-haired man shouted in Jiong's mansion that rebellion would erupt within ten days.

sentences.zh: 即收殺之。

translations.literal: Immediately seized killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong had him seized and killed.

sentences.zh: 冏驕恣日甚，終無悛志。

translations.literal: Jiong arrogant unrestrained daily worse; finally no reform intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong grew ever more arrogant and showed no repentance.

sentences.zh: 前賊曹屬孫惠復上諫曰：

translations.literal: Former thief-court clerk Sun Hui again submitted remonstrance saying:
translations.idiomatic: Staffer Sun Hui offered another memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 惠聞天下五難，四不可，而明公皆以居之矣。

translations.literal: Hui heard All-under-Heaven five difficulties; four impossibles; yet enlightened duke all already dwell them.
translations.idiomatic: You have stumbled into five famed hardships and four forbiddings.

sentences.zh: 捐宗廟之主，忽千乘之重，躬貫甲胄，犯冒鋒刃，此一難也。

translations.literal: Cast ancestral temple masters; neglect thousand-chariot weight; personally wearing armor; offending sharp blades—this first difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: First you risked the ancestral shrines and charged the blades yourself.

sentences.zh: 奮三百之卒，決全勝之策，集四方之眾，致英豪之士，此二難也。

translations.literal: Roused three hundred soldiers; decided complete victory plan; gathered four quarters masses; assembled heroic persons—this second difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Second you rallied troops and heroes from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 舍殿堂之尊，居單幕之陋，安囂塵之慘，同將士之勞，此三難也。

translations.literal: Abandoned hall temple honor; dwelled single curtain lowliness; endured clamor dust bitterness; shared officers soldiers labor—this third difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Third you endured camp hardship like common soldiers.

sentences.zh: 驅烏合之眾，當凶強之敵，任神武之略，無疑阻之懼，此四難也。

translations.literal: Drove flock-united masses; faced fierce strong enemy; applied divine martial stratagem; without doubt obstruction fear—this fourth difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth you led irregular levies against vicious foes without flinching.

sentences.zh: 檄六合之內，著盟信之誓，升幽宮之帝，復皇祚之業，此五難也。

translations.literal: Proclaimed within six directions; established oath alliance faith; elevated imprisoned emperor; restored imperial lineage enterprise—this fifth difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth you summoned the realm, freed the emperor, and restored the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 大名不可久荷，大功不可久任，大權不可久執，大威不可久居。

translations.literal: Great name cannot long bear; great merit cannot long hold; great power cannot long grasp; great awe cannot long dwell.
translations.idiomatic: No man long bears great fame, merit, power, or terror.

sentences.zh: 未有行其五難而不以為難，遺其不可而謂之為可。

translations.literal: Never one walks five hardships yet does not regard hardship; abandons impossibles yet calls possible.
translations.idiomatic: None counts those trials easy or claims impossibles as trivial.

sentences.zh: 惠竊所不安也。

translations.literal: Hui privately what uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: That is what troubles your servant.

sentences.zh: 自永熙以來，十有一載，人不見德，惟戮是聞。

translations.literal: From Yongxi onward; eleven years; people see no virtue; only slaughter heard.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yongxi eleven years the people have heard only slaughter, not virtue.

sentences.zh: 公族構篡奪之禍，骨肉遭梟夷之刑，群王被囚檻之困，妃主有離絕之哀。

translations.literal: Ducal houses suffered usurpation disasters; flesh bones met owl-extinction punishments; various kings endured cage hardship; consorts princesses had separation grief.
translations.idiomatic: Princes fell to usurpation, kin to execution, kings to cages, ladies to bereavement.

sentences.zh: 曆觀前代，國家之禍，至親之亂，未有今日之甚者也。

translations.literal: Surveying former ages; state's disaster; closest kin turmoil; never reached today's extremity.
translations.idiomatic: History records no closer kinship wrecked like today's.

sentences.zh: 良史書過，後嗣何觀！

translations.literal: Good historians record faults—what posterity surveys!
translations.idiomatic: Good historians record faults—what will posterity read?

sentences.zh: 天下所以不去于晉，符命長存於世者，主無嚴虐之暴，朝無酷烈之政，武帝餘恩，獻王遺愛，聖慈惠和，尚經人心。

translations.literal: All-under-Heaven reason not abandon Jin; tally mandate long exists generation's reason—lord lacks cruel tyranny's violence; court lacks harsh fierce governance; Emperor Wu surplus kindness; Prince Xian surplus love; sagely kindness mild harmony still binds hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The realm still cleaves to Jin because rulers were seldom cruel, court seldom harsh, Emperor Wu's kindness and Prince Xian's grace still touch hearts.

sentences.zh: 四海所系，實在於茲。

translations.literal: Within four seas what binds truly rests here.
translations.idiomatic: The realm's fate hinges on this moment.

sentences.zh: 今明公建不世之義，而未為不世之讓，天下惑之，思求所悟。

translations.literal: Now enlightened duke establishes never-age righteousness; yet does not perform never-age yielding; All-under-Heaven perplexes it; seeks obtain understanding.
translations.idiomatic: You have done what none before attempted yet refuse the yielding all expect—the world is baffled.

sentences.zh: 長沙、成都，魯、衛之密，國之親親，與明公計功受賞，尚不自先。

translations.literal: Changsha, Chengdu—Lu, Wei's closeness—state's nearest kin compare merit receiving rewards still not self first.
translations.idiomatic: Princes of Changsha and Chengdu—kin close as Lu and Wei—still ranked themselves behind others when honors were shared.

sentences.zh: 今公宜放桓、文之勳，邁臧、劄之風，芻狗萬物，不仁其化，崇親推近，功遂身退，委萬機于二王，命方岳於群後，燿義讓之旗，鳴思歸之鑾，宅大齊之墟，振泱泱之風，垂拱青、徐之域，高枕營丘之籓。

translations.literal: Now duke ought release Huan and Wen's merit; surpass Zang and Zha's wind; straw dog myriad things; not benevolent its transforming; elevate kin push near; merit accomplished body withdraws; entrust myriad affairs to two kings; command regional peaks to host of lords; shine righteousness yielding banner; ring longing-return bells; dwell Great Qi's ruins; stir vast vast wind; hang draped hands blue Xu regions; high pillow Yingqiu's screen.
translations.idiomatic: Yield like Lords Huan and Wen and worthies Zang and Zha—renounce power, entrust the two princes and provincial commanders, retire east among Qi ruins, and let virtue speak louder than rule.

sentences.zh: 金石不足以銘高，八音不足以讚美，姬文不得專聖於前，太伯不得獨賢於後。

translations.literal: Metal stone insufficient engrave height; eight tones insufficient praise beauty; Ji Wen cannot monopolize sage before; Taibo cannot alone worthy after.
translations.idiomatic: Bronze could not record such virtue nor music praise it—King Wen would not eclipse you nor Taibo stand alone.

sentences.zh: 今明公忘亢極之悔，忽窮高之凶，棄五嶽之安，居累卵之危，外以權勢受疑，內以百揆損神。

translations.literal: Now enlightened duke forgets utmost apex regret; neglects utmost height peril; abandons five peaks peace; dwells piled eggs peril; outward by power situation receives suspicion; inward by hundred affairs harms spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you cling to supremacy's peril—rejecting Mount Tai's safety for an egg-stack throne—suspected without yet drained within.

sentences.zh: 雖處高臺之上，逍遙重仞之墉，及其危亡之憂，過於潁、翟之慮。

translations.literal: Although dwelling high terrace above; roaming free thousand-ren walls; reaching its peril extinction worry exceeds Ying, Zhai anxieties.
translations.idiomatic: Even atop high walls your peril outmatches anyone fighting at Ying or Yangzhai.

sentences.zh: 群下竦戰，莫之敢言。

translations.literal: Underlings stand trembling battle; none of them dares speak.
translations.idiomatic: Your staff tremble silent.

sentences.zh: 惠以衰亡之余，遭陽九之運，甘矢石之禍，赴大王之義，脫褐冠胄，從戎于許。

translations.literal: Hui with declining remnant; encountering yang-nine fortune; sweetly suffered stone arrows calamity; proceeded great king's righteousness; cast off cloth cap helmet; followed army at Xu.
translations.idiomatic: I, Hui, survivor of collapse, followed your host from common cloth to Xu.

sentences.zh: 契闊戰陣，功無可記，當隨風塵，待罪初服。

translations.literal: Tramped battle lines; merit nothing recordable; ought follow wind dust; await guilt first garments.
translations.idiomatic: I earned no glory—only the wind's dust—and deserve rustic clothes again.

sentences.zh: 屈原放斥，心存南郢；

translations.literal: Qu Yuan banished; heart lodged southern Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yuan exiled yet loved Chu.

sentences.zh: 樂毅適趙，志戀北燕。

translations.literal: Yue Yi went Zhao; intent loves northern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yi fled Zhao yet longed for Yan.

sentences.zh: 況惠受恩，偏蒙識養，雖復暫違，情隆二臣，是以披露血誠，冒昧幹迕。

translations.literal: Moreover Hui received favor; specially received nurture recognition; although again brief separation; affection loftier two ministers; therefore expose drip blood sincerity; risk offense blunt.
translations.idiomatic: I owe you more than Qu or Yue owed old lords—so I bleed my plea though it offends.

sentences.zh: 言入身戮，義讓功舉，退就鈇鑕，此惠之死賢於生也。

translations.literal: Words enter body execution; righteousness yields merit raised; retreat approach axe chopping block; this Hui's death worthier than life.
translations.idiomatic: Kill me if you must—death for this counsel would crown my life.

sentences.zh: 冏不納，亦不加罪。

translations.literal: Jiong did not accept; also did not add crime.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong neither listened nor punished him.

sentences.zh: 翊軍校尉李含奔于長安，詐云受密詔，使河間王顒誅冏，因導以利謀。

translations.literal: Colonel of Guards Army Li Han fled to Chang'an; falsely claimed received secret edict; caused Prince Yong of Hejian execute Jiong; thereby guided with profit plotting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han fled to Chang'an forged orders urging Prince Yong to destroy Jiong.

sentences.zh: 顒從之，上表曰：

translations.literal: Yong followed it; submitted memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yong agreed and memorialized:

sentences.zh: 王室多故，禍難罔已。

translations.literal: The royal house has many troubles; disasters are unending.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Jin faces ceaseless calamity.

sentences.zh: 大司馬冏雖唱義有興復皇位之功，而定都邑，克寧社稷，實成都王勳力也。

translations.literal: Although Grand Marshal Jiong raised the righteous cause and had merit in restoring the emperor's throne, settling the capital and securing the altars was truly the merit of the Prince of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong claimed credit for rallying loyalists, but Prince Ying of Chengdu truly stabilized the capital.

sentences.zh: 而冏不能固守臣節，實協異望。

translations.literal: Yet Jiong could not steadfastly uphold a minister's duty; he indeed harbored ambitions beyond his station.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong broke faith as a minister and nursed designs of his own.

sentences.zh: 在許昌營有東西掖門，官置治書侍御史，長史、司馬直立左右，如侍臣之儀。

translations.literal: At his Xuchang headquarters he had east and west Ye Gates; he installed Clerk Attendants, chief clerks, and majors standing left and right like palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His camp at Xuchang mirrored the palace gates with officers arrayed like imperial attendants.

sentences.zh: 京城大清，篡逆誅夷，而率百萬之眾來繞洛城。

translations.literal: The capital had been cleared and usurpers executed, yet he led hosts of a million to surround Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Though Luoyang was cleansed of traitors, he ringed the capital with vast armies.

sentences.zh: 阻兵經年，不一朝覲，百官拜伏，晏然南面。

translations.literal: He blocked roads with troops for a full year, never once attending court; officials bowed while he calmly faced south like a sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: For a year his army besieged the court—he held court facing south without homage to the throne.

sentences.zh: 壞樂官市署，用自增廣。

translations.literal: He tore down music bureaus and market offices to enlarge his own mansions.
translations.idiomatic: He demolished public offices to expand his private compounds.

sentences.zh: 輒取武庫秘杖，嚴列不解。

translations.literal: He seized secret halberds from the arsenal and kept them ranked under arms without dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He armed himself from the imperial arsenal and kept weapons permanently drawn.

sentences.zh: 故東萊王蕤知其逆節，表陳事狀，而見誣陷，加罪黜徙。

translations.literal: Therefore Prince Rui of Donglai, knowing his rebellious intent, memorialized the facts—and was slandered, convicted, and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui exposed him and paid with exile.

sentences.zh: 以樹私黨，僭立官屬。

translations.literal: He planted private factions and arrogantly appointed his own staff.
translations.idiomatic: He stacked offices with cronies.

sentences.zh: 幸妻嬖妾，名號比之中宮。

translations.literal: He favored wives and concubines whose titles rivaled the empress.
translations.idiomatic: His favorites bore titles echoing the middle palace.

sentences.zh: 沈湎酒色，不恤群黎。

translations.literal: He drowned in wine and women and cared nothing for the people.
translations.idiomatic: He sank into debauchery and ignored the common folk.

sentences.zh: 董艾放縱，無所畏忌，中丞按奏，而取退免。

translations.literal: Dong Ai acted without restraint and feared nothing; though the Censor-in-Chief impeached him, Jiong let him walk free.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Ai flouted law yet survived impeachment.

sentences.zh: 張偉惚恫，擁停詔可，葛旟小豎，維持國命。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei intimidated officials into freezing edicts; petty Ge Yu held the state's mandate in hand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei stalled imperial orders while Ge Yu pulled strings.

sentences.zh: 操弄王爵，貨賂公行。

translations.literal: He toyed with noble rank and sold offices openly.
translations.idiomatic: He trafficked in titles and took bribes in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 群奸聚黨，擅斷殺生。

translations.literal: Villains gathered in factions and wielded life-and-death power.
translations.idiomatic: His clique killed at will.

sentences.zh: 密署腹心，實為貨謀。

translations.literal: He planted trusted agents everywhere—purely for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Every trusted post served private greed.

sentences.zh: 斥罪忠良，伺窺神器。

translations.literal: He drove away the loyal and eyed the throne itself.
translations.idiomatic: He purged good ministers and coveted the sacred regalia.

sentences.zh: 臣受重任，蕃衛方嶽，見冏所行，實懷激憤。

translations.literal: Your servant bears heavy duty guarding the frontiers; witnessing Jiong's conduct fills me with rage.
translations.idiomatic: I guard the regions—Jiong's deeds kindle my fury.

sentences.zh: 即日翊軍校尉李含乘驛密至，宣騰詔旨。

translations.literal: Today Colonel Li Han rode post-horses in secret to deliver your edict's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Li Han has just brought me your sealed command by relay.

sentences.zh: 臣伏讀感切，五情若灼。

translations.literal: Your servant knelt to read it; every sentiment burns within.
translations.idiomatic: Reading it scorches my heart.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義，君親無將。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that ruler and kin must never harbor armed rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Annals say high lords may not raise arms against the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 冏擁強兵，樹置私黨，權官要職，莫非腹心。

translations.literal: Jiong keeps massive armies and plants personal followers; every powerful office is his intimate.
translations.idiomatic: His hosts and every key post are packed with his creatures.

sentences.zh: 雖復重責之誅，恐不義服。

translations.literal: Even repeated punishments may not make him yield righteously.
translations.idiomatic: Execution alone may not curb him.

sentences.zh: 今輒勒兵，精卒十萬，與州征並協忠義，共會洛陽。

translations.literal: Your servant therefore mobilizes a hundred thousand picked troops; together with loyal provincial forces we will converge on Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: I march one hundred thousand veterans to join righteous armies at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍長沙王乂，同奮忠誠，廢冏還第。

translations.literal: General of Agile Cavalry Prince Yi of Changsha likewise acts in loyalty to depose Jiong and send him home.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Changsha joins me to strip Jiong of power.

sentences.zh: 有不順命，軍法從事。

translations.literal: Whoever disobeys shall face military justice.
translations.idiomatic: Disobey and martial law applies.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎明德茂親，功高勳重，往歲去就，允合眾望，宜為宰輔，代冏阿衡之任。

translations.literal: Prince Ying of Chengdu is virtuous, eminent among kin, with towering merit; his past conduct matched popular hope—he should be chief minister and replace Jiong as premier.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying should succeed Jiong as minister of state.

sentences.zh: 顒表既至，冏大懼，會百僚曰：「昔孫秀作逆，篡逼帝王，社稷傾覆，莫能禦難。

translations.literal: When Yong's memorial arrived Jiong greatly feared; convened hundred officials saying: "Formerly Sun Xiu rebelled; usurped and pressed the emperors; altars overturned—none could ward disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong's memorial terrified Jiong, who told his council: "Sun Xiu once usurped the throne and none could stop him."

sentences.zh: 孤糾合義眾，掃除元惡，臣子之節，信著神明。

translations.literal: I gathered righteous hosts; swept the chief villain; minister-son's duty—faith proved before spirits.
translations.idiomatic: I rallied loyal armies and killed that traitor—my duty was clear to gods and men."

sentences.zh: 二王今日聽信讒言，造構大難，當賴忠謀以和不協耳。

translations.literal: The two kings today listen to slander and brew great disaster—we must rely on loyal counsel to harmonize this discord.
translations.idiomatic: Now two princes heed lies and stir civil war—we need wise counsel to heal the rift."

sentences.zh: 」司徒王戎、司空東海王越說冏委權崇讓。

translations.literal: " Minister of Education Wang Rong and Minister of Works Prince Yue of Donghai urged Jiong to yield power and honor modest refusal.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Rong and Prince Yue urged Jiong to step down gracefully.

sentences.zh: 冏從事中郎葛旟怒曰：「趙庶人聽任孫秀，移天易日，當時喋喋，莫敢先唱。

translations.literal: Jiong's retainer Ge Yu angrily said: "The Zhao commoner listened to Sun Xiu and shifted heaven—then everyone murmured yet none dared speak first.
translations.idiomatic: Retainer Ge Yu thundered: "When illegitimate Lun obeyed Sun Xiu you all stayed mute."

sentences.zh: 公蒙犯矢石，躬貫甲胄，攻圍陷陣，得濟今日。

translations.literal: You braved arrows and stones; personally wore armor; besieged and stormed the lines to win this day.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord endured battle to win today.

sentences.zh: 計功行封，事殷未遍。

translations.literal: Merit was tallied and ranks awarded; the task was huge and not yet finished everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards still lag—the work was vast.

sentences.zh: 三台納言，不恤王事，賞報稽緩，責不在府。

translations.literal: The Three Terraces' spokesmen neglect royal business; rewards are slow—fault lies not with the Grand Marshal's bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Central offices ignore state affairs and delay rewards—not Jiong's fault.

sentences.zh: 讒言僭逆，當共誅討，虛承偽書，令公就第。

translations.literal: Slanderers cry treason worth joint execution; you lightly trust forged letters telling the duke to go home.
translations.idiomatic: They brand you traitor on forged orders to dismiss you.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏以來，王侯就第甯有得保妻子者乎！

translations.literal: Since Han and Wei has any prince sent home kept wife and children safe?
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Wei no prince "retired" home with his family intact.

sentences.zh: 議者可斬。

translations.literal: Those who argue thus deserve beheading.
translations.idiomatic: Such advisers deserve the axe.

sentences.zh: 」於是百官震悚，無不失色。

translations.literal: " Thereupon hundred officials trembled; none kept color.
translations.idiomatic: Officials went white with fear.

sentences.zh: 長沙王乂徑入宮，發兵攻冏府。

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Changsha entered the palace directly and sent troops against Jiong's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi burst into the palace and struck Jiong's compound.

sentences.zh: 冏遣董艾陳兵宮西。

translations.literal: Jiong sent Dong Ai to array troops west of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong lined Dong Ai west of the hall.

sentences.zh: 乂又遣宋洪等放火燒諸觀閣及千秋、神武門。

translations.literal: Yi further sent Song Hong and others to burn the towers and Thousand Autumn and Divine Martial gates.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had Song Hong torch the watchtowers and gates.

sentences.zh: 冏令黃門令王湖悉盜騶虞幡，唱云：「長沙王矯詔。

translations.literal: Jiong ordered Yellow Gate Director Wang Hu to steal every Zouyu banner crying: "Prince of Changsha forged the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong's eunuch stole the mercy banners claiming Yi forged orders.

sentences.zh: 」乂又稱：「大司馬謀反，助者誅五族。

translations.literal: " Yi answered: "Grand Marshal rebels—helpers die to five degrees of kin.
translations.idiomatic: Yi countered that Jiong was the traitor and allies faced mass execution.

sentences.zh: 」是夕，城內大戰，飛矢雨集，火光屬天。

translations.literal: " That night the city warred; arrows fell like rain; fire linked heaven.
translations.idiomatic: That night Luoyang blazed; arrows darkened the sky.

sentences.zh: 帝幸上東門，矢集御前。

translations.literal: The emperor went to Upper East Gate; arrows clustered before his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Hui took refuge at Upper East Gate under arrow fire.

sentences.zh: 群臣救火，死者相枕。

translations.literal: Courtiers fought the flames; dead lay head to heel.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers battled the blaze while corpses piled up.

sentences.zh: 明日，冏敗，乂擒冏至殿前，帝惻然，欲活之。

translations.literal: Next day Jiong lost; Yi seized him before the hall; the emperor pitied him and wished to spare him.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Yi dragged Jiong bound before Hui, who wanted mercy.

sentences.zh: 乂叱左右促牽出，冏猶再顧，遂斬於閶闔門外，徇首六軍。

translations.literal: Yi shouted for guards to haul him out; Jiong looked back twice; beheaded outside Changhe Gate; head shown to six armies.
translations.idiomatic: Yi overruled him—Jiong died at Changhe Gate, head displayed to the host.

sentences.zh: 諸黨屬皆夷三族。

translations.literal: Every faction member suffered three-clan extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong's party was extirpated to three clans.

sentences.zh: 幽其子淮陵王超、樂安王冰、濟陽王英于金墉。

translations.literal: His sons Chao of Huailing, Bing of Le'an, and Ying of Jiyang were locked in Brick Granary.
translations.idiomatic: His three sons were imprisoned at Brick Granary.

sentences.zh: 暴冏屍於西明亭，三日而莫敢收斂。

translations.literal: Jiong's corpse lay exposed at Ximing Pavilion three days with no burial.
translations.idiomatic: His body rotted at Ximing Pavilion unburied for days.

sentences.zh: 冏故掾屬荀闓等表乞殯葬，許之。

translations.literal: Former clerks such as Xun Kai memorialized for funeral rites; permission came.
translations.idiomatic: Old aides begged to bury him—permission followed.

sentences.zh: 初，冏之盛也，有一婦人詣大司馬府求寄產。

translations.literal: When Jiong was powerful a woman asked the Grand Marshal mansion to lodge childbirth.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiong's height a woman sought shelter to give birth.

sentences.zh: 吏詰之，婦人曰：「我截齊便去耳。

translations.literal: Clerks questioned her; she said: "I cut Qi short then leave.
translations.idiomatic: She said she came only to "cut Qi" short—ominous wordplay.

sentences.zh: 」識者聞而惡之。

translations.literal: " Hearers thought it inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners shuddered at the omen.

sentences.zh: 時又謠曰：「著布袙腹，為齊持服。

translations.literal: A rhyme said: "Cloth wrapped belly—mourning garb for Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Ballads sang of wearing mourning for Qi.

sentences.zh: 」俄而冏誅。

translations.literal: " Soon Jiong was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jiong fell.

sentences.zh: 永興初，詔以冏輕陷重刑，前勳不宜堙沒，乃赦其三子超、冰、英還第，封超為縣王，以繼冏祀，曆員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Yongxing edict said Jiong's harsh sentence wronged him; former merit must stand; pardoned sons Chao, Bing, Ying home; Chao enfeoffed county prince continuing sacrifices; served Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing restored his sons—Chao inherited the line as supernumerary attendant.

sentences.zh: 光熙初，追冊冏曰：「咨故大司馬、齊王冏：王昔以宗籓穆胤紹世，緒于東國，作翰許京，允鎮靜我王室。

translations.literal: Guangxi posthumous patent to Jiong said: "Late Grand Marshal Prince of Qi: you as clan heir carried the eastern line; as wing at Xu you steadied the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi patent praised his Qi succession and service at Xu.

sentences.zh: 涎率義徒，同盟觸澤，克成元勳，大濟潁東。

translations.literal: You led righteous followers allied at Chimei Marsh; achieved founding merit; greatly saved land east of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: You raised armies at Chimei and saved the eastern heartland.

sentences.zh: 朕用應嘉茂績，謂篤爾勞，俾式先典，以疇茲顯懿。

translations.literal: We respond to your splendid deeds; affirm your toil; model ancient canon to enshrine this bright virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The throne records his glory by ancient forms.

sentences.zh: 廓士殊分，跨兼吳楚，崇禮備物，寵侔蕭、霍，庶憑翼戴之重，永隆邦家之望。

translations.literal: Broad fiefs spanned Wu and Chu; honors matched Xiao and Huo—hoping your wings would long uphold the state.
translations.idiomatic: His honors rivaled Xiao He and Huo Guang.

sentences.zh: 而恭德不建，取侮二方，有司過舉，致王於戮。

translations.literal: Yet reverent virtue failed; insult came from two quarters; officials erred and brought the prince to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Proud conduct drew shame; judges erred and killed him.

sentences.zh: 古人有言曰：'用其法，猶思其人。

translations.literal: The ancients said: 'Use his law—still think of the man.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb runs: even applying his statute one remembers the man.

sentences.zh: '況王功濟朕身，勳存社稷，追惟既往，有悼於厥心哉！

translations.literal: ' How much more when his merit succored Us and served the altars—looking back Our heart grieves!
translations.idiomatic: How much more a prince who saved us—we mourn afresh.

sentences.zh: 今復王本封，命嗣子還紹厥緒，禮秩典度，一如舊制。

translations.literal: Now We restore his fief; order heir to continue the line; ritual ranks follow old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: His title and heir are restored under former rules.

sentences.zh: 使使持節、大鴻臚即墓賜策，祠乙太牢。

translations.literal: Credential-bearing Grand Herald bestows patent at tomb with great bull and boar sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: A herald grants the posthumous patent at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 魂而有靈，祗服朕命，肆寧爾心，嘉茲寵榮。

translations.literal: If soul aware—revere Our charge; calm your heart and accept glory.
translations.idiomatic: May his ghost accept this honor.

sentences.zh: 」子超嗣爵。

translations.literal: " Son Chao inherited title.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Chao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，懷帝下詔，重述冏唱義元勳，還贈大司馬，加侍中、假節，追諡。

translations.literal: Yongjia: Emperor Huai again praised Jiong as first to raise the cause; restored Grand Marshal; added Palace Attendant, credentials, posthumous name.
translations.idiomatic: Huai restored Jiong's honors in Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽傾覆，超兄弟皆沒于劉聰，冏遂無後。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell Chao brothers fell to Liu Cong—Jiong's line ended.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's fall left Liu Cong holding the sons—Jiong had no heirs.

sentences.zh: 太元中，詔以故南頓王宗子柔之襲封齊王，紹攸、冏之祀，曆散騎常待。

translations.literal: Taiyuan edict had Rouzhi, grandson of Prince Zong of Nandun, inherit Prince of Qi for You and Jiong's cult; served Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan reassigned the Qi title to Rouzhi from Prince Zong's line.

sentences.zh: 元興初，會稽王道子將討桓玄，詔柔之兼侍中，以騶虞幡宣告江、荊二州，至姑孰，為玄前鋒所害。

translations.literal: Yuanxing: Prince Daozi of Kuaiji campaigned against Huan Xuan; edict made Rouzhi concurrent Palace Attendant proclaiming Yang-Jing with Zouyu banner; at Gushu vanguard killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Rouzhi died on Daozi's Huan Xuan campaign at Gushu.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿勳。

translations.literal: Posthumously Minister Splendid Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named Minister of Splendid Brightness.

sentences.zh: 子建之立。

translations.literal: Son Jian established.
translations.idiomatic: Son Jian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，國除。

translations.literal: Song abdication abolished the state.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu Song usurpation ended the principality.

sentences.zh: 鄭方者，字子回，慷慨有志節，博涉史傳，卓犖不常，鄉閭有識者歎其奇，而未能薦達。

translations.literal: Zheng Fang, courtesy Zihui, was generous and principled, widely read histories—local worthies sighed at his talent yet none promoted him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Fang (courtesy Zihui) was learned and bold but obscure.

sentences.zh: 及冏輔政專恣，方發憤步詣洛陽，自稱荊楚逸民，獻書於冏曰：「方聞聖明輔世，夙夜祗懼，泰而不驕，所以長守貴也。

translations.literal: When Jiong ruled unchecked Fang walked to Luoyang styled recluse of Jing-Chu and wrote Jiong: "Fang hears sages aid the age fearing night and day, secure yet humble—thereby long guarding honor.
translations.idiomatic: Fang marched to Luoyang as a "recluse" to warn Jiong: wise regents stay vigilant.

sentences.zh: 今大王安不慮危，耽于酒色，燕樂過度，其失一也。

translations.literal: Now the great king rests without fearing peril; drowns in wine and women; feasts beyond measure—first fault.
translations.idiomatic: First fault: you ignore danger and revel.

sentences.zh: 大王檄命，當使天下穆如清風，宗室骨肉永無纖介，今則不然，其失二也。

translations.literal: The great king's commands ought make the realm mild as clear wind and kin never estranged—now not so—second fault.
translations.idiomatic: Second: your edicts should unify kin but breed division.

sentences.zh: 四夷交侵，邊境不靜，大王自以功業興隆，不以為念，其失三也。

translations.literal: Four barbarians raid together; borders unquiet; great king thinks merit secure and ignores it—third fault.
translations.idiomatic: Third: barbarians press the frontiers while you ignore them.

sentences.zh: 大王興義，群庶競赴，天下雖甯，人勞窮苦，不聞大王振救之令，其失四也。

translations.literal: The great king raised righteous hosts; the masses flocked; though the realm is quiet the people toil in bitter want—We hear no mandate from the great king to succor them—this is the fourth fault.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: you raise righteous war yet issue no relief while the people suffer.

sentences.zh: 又與義兵歃血而盟，事定之後，賞不逾時，自清泰已來，論功未分，此則食言，其失五也。

translations.literal: You also smeared blood in covenant with the righteous army; when the deed was done rewards should not be delayed; since the Pure Peace era began merit has not been apportioned—this breaks your word—fifth fault.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: you swore to reward the allies but after victory broke your promise.

sentences.zh: 大王建非常之功，居宰相之任，謗聲盈塗，人懷忿怨，方以狂愚，冒死陳誠。

translations.literal: The great king achieved extraordinary merit and holds the chief minister's post; slander fills the roads and men nurse rage—Your servant, foolish, risks death to speak truth.
translations.idiomatic: You did great deeds yet earn hatred—your servant dares this blunt word.

sentences.zh: 」冏含忍答之云：「孤不能致五闕，若無子，則不聞其過矣。

translations.literal: " Jiong contained himself and answered: "I could not avoid five faults; were it not for you, I would not have heard of them."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong answered testily: without Zheng Fang he would ignore his five errors.

sentences.zh: 」未幾而敗焉。

translations.literal: " Not long after he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell.

sentences.zh: 長沙厲王乂

translations.literal: Prince Li of Changsha, Yi
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi, Prince Li of Changsha

sentences.zh: 長沙厲王乂，字士度，武帝第六子也。

translations.literal: Prince Li of Changsha, Yi, courtesy Shidu, was Emperor Wu's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi, Prince Li of Changsha, courtesy Shidu, sixth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 太康十年受封，拜員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Tenth year of Taikang he received investiture; appointed Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Taikang 10 he took his fief and supernumerary attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 及武帝崩，乂時年十五，孺慕過禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu died Yi was fifteen; his child-grief exceeded ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he mourned his father past the rites.

sentences.zh: 會楚王瑋奔喪，諸王皆近路迎之，乂獨至陵所，號慟以俟瑋。

translations.literal: When Prince Wei of Chu came to mourn the funeral, the other princes met him along the road; Yi alone went to the mausoleum and wailed bitterly awaiting Wei.
translations.idiomatic: While other princes greeted Prince Wei along the route, Yi waited weeping at the tomb itself.

sentences.zh: 拜步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Colonel of Infantry.
translations.idiomatic: He became Colonel of Infantry.

sentences.zh: 及瑋之誅二公也，乂守東掖門。

translations.literal: When Wei executed the two dukes, Yi guarded the eastern Ye Gate.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei's coup Yi held the east Ye Gate.

sentences.zh: 會騶虞幡出，乂投弓流涕曰：「楚王被詔，是以從之，安知其非！

translations.literal: When the Zouyu banner appeared Yi cast aside his bow with tears saying: "Prince Chu followed an edict—how could I know it wrong!
translations.idiomatic: When the mercy banner flew Yi dropped his weapon weeping that he had trusted Wei's forged order.

sentences.zh: 」瑋既誅，乂以同母，貶為常山王，之國。

translations.literal: " After Wei died Yi, sharing the same mother, was degraded to Prince of Changshan and sent to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei's death Yi—Wei full brother—was demoted to Prince of Changshan and sent away.

sentences.zh: 乂身長七尺五寸，開朗果斷，才力絕人，虛心下士，甚有名譽。

translations.literal: Yi stood seven chi five cun tall; open bright decisive; talent and strength surpassed others; humble toward gentlemen; enjoyed great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven foot five, decisive and stronger than most, humble to scholars and widely admired.

sentences.zh: 三王之舉義也，乂率國兵應之，過趙國，房子令距守，乂殺之，進軍為成都後系。

translations.literal: When the three kings raised the righteous cause Yi led his state's troops to join; passing Zhao commandery the Fangzi magistrate barred him—Yi killed him and advanced as Chengdu's rear wing.
translations.idiomatic: Yi marched to join the coalition, killed the magistrate who blocked him at Fangzi, and covered Prince Ying's rear.

sentences.zh: 常山內史程恢將貳於乂，乂到鄴，斬恢及其五子。

translations.literal: Changshan interior secretary Cheng Hui plotted to betray Yi; Yi reached Ye and executed Hui and his five sons.
translations.idiomatic: He slew Cheng Hui and five sons at Ye for plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 至洛，拜撫軍大將軍，領左軍將軍。

translations.literal: Arriving at Luoyang he was appointed Grand General Who Pacifies the Army concurrently Left Army general.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang he became Grand General Who Pacifies the Army and Left Army commander.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷驃騎將軍、開府，復本國。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted General of Agile Cavalry with independent headquarters and restoration of his original principality.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he added agile cavalry command, his own headquarters, and his old title.

sentences.zh: 乂見齊王冏漸專權，嘗與成都王穎俱拜陵，因謂穎曰：「天下者，先帝之業也，王宜維之。

translations.literal: Yi saw Prince Jiong of Qi gradually monopolize power; once while paying tomb respects with Prince Ying of Chengdu he told Ying: "The realm is the late emperor's legacy—you must uphold it.
translations.idiomatic: At the imperial tombs he warned Prince Ying that Jiong threatened their father's legacy.

sentences.zh: 」時聞其言者皆憚之。

translations.literal: " Those who heard his words feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners trembled at his bluntness.

sentences.zh: 及河間王顒將誅冏，傳檄以乂為內主。

translations.literal: When Prince Yong of Hejian prepared to kill Jiong he circulated a manifesto naming Yi as inner coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's proclamation against Jiong named Yi as Luoyang's inside agent.

sentences.zh: 冏遣其將董艾襲乂，乂將左右百餘人，手斫車幰，露乘馳赴宮，閉諸門，奉天子與冏相攻，起火燒冏府，連戰三日，冏敗，斬之，並誅諸黨與二千餘人。

translations.literal: Jiong sent Dong Ai to strike Yi; Yi took a hundred followers, slashed his carriage screen, and rode bare to the palace; sealed the gates; upheld the emperor while attacking Jiong; burned Jiong's compound; fought three days; defeated and beheaded Jiong and executed over two thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: Yi broke into the palace, rallied Hui against Jiong, torched Jiong's mansion, and after three days killed Jiong and two thousand partisans.

sentences.zh: 顒本以乂弱冏強，冀乂為冏所擒，然後以乂為辭，宣告四方共討之，因廢帝立成都王，己為宰相，專制天下。

translations.literal: Yong originally thought Yi weak Jiong strong; hoped Yi would be seized by Jiong; then use Yi as excuse proclaim four quarters jointly punish him; thereby depose emperor establish Prince of Chengdu; himself be chancellor monopolize realm.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong bet Yi would lose to Jiong so he could march as rescuer, depose Hui, crown Prince Ying, and rule as premier.

sentences.zh: 即而乂殺冏，其計不果，乃潛使侍中馮蓀、河南尹李含、中書令卞粹等襲乂。

translations.literal: Yet Yi killed Jiong; the scheme failed; thereupon secretly sent Palace Attendant Feng Sun, Henan Intendant Li Han, Director Bian Cui and others strike Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi slew Jiong instead Yong sent Feng Sun, Li Han, and Bian Cui to ambush him.

sentences.zh: 乂並誅之。

translations.literal: Yi executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yi killed every conspirator.

sentences.zh: 顒遂與穎同伐京都。

translations.literal: Yong thereupon with Ying jointly campaigned capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Prince Ying marched on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 穎遣刺客圖乂，時長沙國左常侍王矩侍直，見客色動，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Ying sent assassins plotting Yi; then Changsha state's Left Regular Attendant Wang Ju on duty saw guest color shift—thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's assassin fell to Wang Ju on night watch.

sentences.zh: 詔以乂為大都督以距顒。

translations.literal: Edict appointed Yi Grand Commander to withstand Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Hui named Yi commander-in-chief against Yong.

sentences.zh: 連戰自八月至十月，朝議以乂、穎兄弟，可以辭說而釋，乃使中書令王衍行太尉，光祿勳石陋行司徒，使說穎，令與乂分陝而居，穎不從。
