translations.literal: Battling repeatedly from eighth month to tenth month court discussion held Yi and Ying brothers might be released by persuasion—thereupon sent Director Wang Yan acting Grand Minister Splendid, Minister Shi Lou acting Minister of Education persuade Ying ordering divide Shan dwelling with Yi—Ying refused.
translations.idiomatic: From August to October courtiers hoped Wang Yan and Shi Lou could reconcile brothers Yi and Ying—Ying refused partition.

sentences.zh: 乂因致書於穎曰：

translations.literal: Yi thereupon sent letter to Ying saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yi wrote Prince Ying:

sentences.zh: 先帝應乾撫運，統攝四海，勤身苦己，克成帝業，六合清泰，慶流子孫。

translations.literal: Former emperor responded Heaven nurturing fortune governing capturing four seas; toiled body bitter self accomplished emperor enterprise; six directions pure peace blessing flowed descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Our father suffered to forge Jin—peace reached every corner.

sentences.zh: 孫秀作逆，反易天常，卿興義眾，還復帝位。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu rebelled perverting heaven constant; you raised righteous masses restoring emperor throne.
translations.idiomatic: You ended Sun Xiu's coup.

sentences.zh: 齊王恃功，肆行非法，上無宰相之心，下無忠臣之行，遂其讒惡，離逖骨肉，主上怨傷，尋已蕩除。

translations.literal: Prince Jiong relied on merit wantonly acting unlawful; above lacked premier heart below lacked minister conduct—followed slander alienating flesh bones—lord above grievously wounded—soon already swept away.
translations.idiomatic: You destroyed tyrannical Jiong.

sentences.zh: 吾之與卿，友于十人，同產皇室，受封外都，各不能闡敷王教，經濟遠略。

translations.literal: My relation with you brotherly among ten born same palace invested outer commanderies each unable spread royal teachings extend far strategy.
translations.idiomatic: We brothers rule provinces yet failed to guide the realm.

sentences.zh: 今卿復與太尉共起大眾，阻兵百萬，重圍宮城。

translations.literal: Now you again with Grand Marshal jointly raise great masses block troops million heavily besiege palace city.
translations.idiomatic: Now you and Yong seal the capital with hosts.

sentences.zh: 群臣同忿，聊即命將，示宣國威，未擬摧殄。

translations.literal: Hosts ministers alike furious—I merely ordered generals display state's awe—not intending annihilate.
translations.idiomatic: Angered ministers sent armies to show force—not to slaughter.

sentences.zh: 自投溝澗，蕩平山谷，死者日萬，酷痛無罪。

translations.literal: Yet you threw yourselves ditches gorges filling valleys—dead daily myriad innocent extreme pain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet troops pile dead by myriad innocent.

sentences.zh: 豈國恩之不慈，則用刑之有常。

translations.literal: Is state's kindness unkind then punishments have norm?
translations.idiomatic: Should mercy spare needless slaughter?

sentences.zh: 卿所遣陸機不樂受卿節鉞，將其所領，私通國家。

translations.literal: Lu Ji whom you sent unwilling accept your staff banners leads those commanded secretly attaching court.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji rejects your command and courts Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 想來逆者，當前行一尺，卻行一丈，卿宜還鎮，以甯四海，令宗族無羞，子孫之福也。

translations.literal: Reflect rebels ought advance one chi retreat one chi—king ought return garrison quiet four seas—order clan without shame blessing descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Pull back one pace for each pace forth—return to Ye for family's honor.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，念骨肉分裂之痛，故復遣書。

translations.literal: If not—thinking flesh bones cleaving pain—again send letter.
translations.idiomatic: Else recall kinship broken—I write again.

sentences.zh: 穎復書曰：「文、景受圖，武皇乘運，庶幾堯、舜，共康政道，恩隆洪業，本枝百世。

translations.literal: Ying replied saying: "Wen and Jing received charts Martial Emperor rode fortune—almost Yao Shun together prosperous governance kindness vast enterprise branches hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Ying answered citing Wen Jing and Wu—golden age lineage.

sentences.zh: 豈期骨肉豫禍，後族專權，楊、賈縱毒，齊、趙內篡。

translations.literal: Who expected flesh bones advance disaster rear clan monopoly Yang Jia ran poison Qi Zhao inner usurp.
translations.idiomatic: Who thought imperial wives and princes would poison the realm.

sentences.zh: 幸以誅夷，而未靜息。

translations.literal: Fortunately executed slaughter yet still unquiet.
translations.idiomatic: Execution spared disaster unrepaired.

sentences.zh: 每憂王室，心悸肝爛。

translations.literal: Always worrying royal house heart burned liver.
translations.idiomatic: My heart tears for the throne.

sentences.zh: 羊玄之、皇甫商等恃寵作禍，能不興慨！

translations.literal: Yang Xuanzhi Huangfu Shang relied favor making havoc—can raise no sigh!
translations.idiomatic: Villains Yang Xuanzhi and Huangfu Shang torment court.

sentences.zh: 於是征西羽檄，四海雲應。

translations.literal: Thereupon expedition west feather proclamations four seas cloud responded.
translations.idiomatic: Westward call brought every quarter.

sentences.zh: 本謂仁兄同其所懷，便當內擒商等，收級遠送。

translations.literal: Originally thought kind elder brother shared that heart—should inside seize Shang and others sever heads send far.
translations.idiomatic: I thought you would bind Shang and send their heads.

sentences.zh: 如何迷惑，自為戎首！

translations.literal: How confused becoming spearhead yourself!
translations.idiomatic: Instead you lead rebellion.

sentences.zh: 上矯君詔，下離愛弟，推移輦轂，妄動兵威，還任豺狼，棄戮親善。

translations.literal: Above forge lord edict below part beloved brother shift imperial carriage wantonly move troops restore wolves slaughter kin.
translations.idiomatic: You forge orders, divide brothers, march wolves against kin.

sentences.zh: 行惡求福，如何自勉！

translations.literal: Doing evil seeking fortune—how urge yourself!
translations.idiomatic: Seeking blessing through evil—have shame?

sentences.zh: 前遣陸機董督節鉞，雖黃橋之退，而溫南收勝，一彼一此，未足增慶也。

translations.literal: Former sending Lu Ji supervising staffs although Yellow Bridge retreat yet Wen south gathered victory—one loss one gain—not worth added rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji lost Yellow Bridge yet scored south—not decisive.

sentences.zh: 今武士百萬，良將銳猛，要當與兄整頓海內。

translations.literal: Now warriors million keen generals fierce sharp—must with elder brother rectify realm.
translations.idiomatic: A million blades await to settle the realm with you.

sentences.zh: 若能從太尉之命，斬商等首，投戈退讓，自求多福，穎亦自歸鄴都，與兄同之。

translations.literal: If able follow Grand Marshal orders sever Shang heads cast weapons yield retreat seek fortune—Ying also self return Ye capital share elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Obey Yong—kill Shang—lay arms—and I return Ye with you.

sentences.zh: 奉覽來告，緬然慷慨。

translations.literal: Receiving letter contemplatively stirred generous.
translations.idiomatic: Reading your letter moves me.

sentences.zh: 慎哉大兄，深思進退也！」

translations.literal: Caution elder brother deeply ponder advance retreat!"
translations.idiomatic: Think twice, brother!"

sentences.zh: 乂前後破穎軍，斬獲六七萬人。

translations.literal: Yi front rear defeated Ying armies beheaded captured sixty seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yi smashed sixty-seventy thousand of Ying's men.

sentences.zh: 戰久糧乏，城中大饑，雖曰疲弊，將士同心，皆願效死。

translations.literal: War long provisions exhausted; inside city great famine; although called weary exhausted officers soldiers same heart all wished devote death.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang starved yet troops stood loyal.

sentences.zh: 而乂奉上之禮未有虧失，張方以為未可克，欲還長安。

translations.literal: Yet Yi serving superiors ritual never lacked fault; Zhang Fang thought not yet conquerable wished return Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yi kept honoring Hui; Zhang Fang deemed siege hopeless.

sentences.zh: 而東海王越慮事不濟，潛與殿中將收乂送金墉城。

translations.literal: Yet Prince Yue of Donghai feared affair unsuccessful secretly with palace generals seized Yi deliver Brick Granary fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue feared Yi winning—had him seized to Brick Granary.

sentences.zh: 乂表曰：「陛下篤睦，委臣朝事。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized: "Your Majesty devoted harmony entrusted minister court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yi wrote: "You entrusted me governance."

sentences.zh: 臣小心忠孝，神祇所鑒。

translations.literal: Your servant small heart loyalty filial spirits gods mirror.
translations.idiomatic: My loyalty heaven knows.

sentences.zh: 諸王承謬，率眾見責，朝臣無正，各慮私困，收臣別省，送臣幽宮。

translations.literal: Various kings bearing errors led masses blaming court ministers without righteousness each anxious private distress seized servant separate hall delivered servant secluded palace.
translations.idiomatic: Princes blame ministers—I lie chained apart.

sentences.zh: 臣不惜軀命，但念大晉衰微，枝黨欲盡，陛下孤危。

translations.literal: Servant not sparing body life but worries great Jin declining branches factions nearly exhausted Your Majesty solitary peril.
translations.idiomatic: I fear not death—fear Jin falls.

sentences.zh: 若臣死國寧，亦家之利。

translations.literal: If servant death state tranquil also family's profit.
translations.idiomatic: My death may steady state.

sentences.zh: 但恐快凶人之志：無益于陛下耳。」

translations.literal: Only fear pleasing villains' ambition—no benefit Your Majesty ear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet villains alone profit—not Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 殿中左右恨乂功垂成而敗，謀劫出之，更以距穎。

translations.literal: Palace left-right hated Yi merit hanging verge defeat plotted seize him out renew withstand Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Guards meant to free Yi to fight Ying.

sentences.zh: 越懼難作，欲遂誅乂。

translations.literal: Yue feared disaster arising wished execute Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue feared riot—resolved to kill Yi.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎潘滔勸越密告張方，方遣部將郅輔勒兵三千，就金墉收乂，至營，炙而殺之。

translations.literal: Gentleman Pan Tao urged Yue secretly inform Zhang Fang; Fang dispatched division commander Zhi Fu restrain troops three thousand arriving Brick Granary seize Yi; reaching camp roasted killing.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Tao tipped Zhang Fang—Zhi Fu roasted Yi alive.

sentences.zh: 乂冤痛之聲達於左右，三軍莫不為之垂涕。

translations.literal: Yi's wronged painful sounds reached left-right three armies none not for him shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: His screams shook army tears.

sentences.zh: 時年二十八。

translations.literal: Age twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 乂將殯於城東，官屬莫敢往，故掾劉佑獨送之，步持喪車，悲號斷絕，哀感路人。

translations.literal: Yi about bury east city subordinates none dared go former clerk Liu You alone escorted him walking pulling mourning carriage grief cry cut off sorrow touching passersby.
translations.idiomatic: Only Liu You dared bury him—mourners wept on road.

sentences.zh: 張方以其義士，不之問也。

translations.literal: Zhang Fang because his righteous knight did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Fang spared Liu You.

sentences.zh: 初，乂執權之始，洛下謠曰：「草木萌牙殺長沙。

translations.literal: First Yi grasped power beginning Luoyang rhyme said: "Plants sprouting buds kill Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Omen ran: spring sprouts slay Changsha.

sentences.zh: 」乂以正月二十五日廢，二十七日死，如謠言焉。

translations.literal: " Yi deposed twenty-fifth first month died twenty-seventh like rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: Yi fell twenty-fifth killed twenty-seventh—as rhyme.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，懷帝以乂子碩嗣，拜散騎常侍，後沒于劉聰。

translations.literal: Yongjia Emperor Huai Yi son Shuo succeeded appointed Gentleman Attendant later lost Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Huai named son Shuo attendant until Liu Cong took him.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎

translations.literal: Prince Ying of Chengdu Ying
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu

sentences.zh: 成都王穎，字章度，武帝第十六子也。

translations.literal: Prince Ying Chengdu Ying courtesy Zhangdu Emperor Wu sixteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying courtesy Zhangdu—sixteenth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 太康末受封，邑十萬戶。

translations.literal: Taikang end received investiture fief hundred thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Late Taikang he gained principality with hundred thousand households.

sentences.zh: 後拜越騎校尉，加散騎常侍、車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Later appointed Colonel of Agile Cavalry added Gentleman Attendant General of Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to agile cavalry attendant and chariot general.

sentences.zh: 賈謐嘗與皇太子博，爭道。

translations.literal: Jia Mi once played weiqi with crown prince—disputed move.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi quarreled over a weiqi move with the heir.

sentences.zh: 穎在坐，厲聲呵謐曰：「皇太子國之儲君，賈謐何得無禮！

translations.literal: Ying seated stern voice berated Mi saying: "Crown prince state's heir-apparent—how dare Jia Mi rude!
translations.idiomatic: Ying shouted Mi down for insulting the heir.

sentences.zh: 」謐懼，由此出穎為平北將軍，鎮鄴。

translations.literal: " Mi feared—thereby outgoing Ying as General Who Pacifies North garrisoned Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Mi banished Ying to Ye as northern pacifier.

sentences.zh: 轉鎮北大將軍。

translations.literal: Transferred Grand General Who Guards North.
translations.idiomatic: He became Grand General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫之篡也，進征北大將軍，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: King Lun's usurpation advanced General Who Conquers North added privilege equal Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Lun's coup he gained northern command and Three Excellencies ritual.

sentences.zh: 及齊王冏舉義，穎發兵應冏，以鄴令盧志為左長史，頓丘太守鄭琰為右長史，黃門郎程牧為左司馬，陽平太守和演為右司馬。

translations.literal: When Prince Jiong raised righteous cause Ying sent troops responding Jiong naming Ye magistrate Lu Zhi left chief clerk Dunqiu prefect Zheng Yan right chief clerk Gentleman Cheng Mu left Major Yangping prefect He Yan right Major.
translations.idiomatic: Against Lun he staffed Lu Zhi, Zheng Yan, Cheng Mu, He Yan.

sentences.zh: 使兗州刺史王彥，冀州刺史李毅，督護趙驤、石超等為前鋒。

translations.literal: Caused Yan Province Inspector Wang Yan Ji Province Inspector Li Yi protector Zhao Xiang Shi Chao and others forward van.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan and Li Yi spearheaded with Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao.

sentences.zh: 羽檄所及，莫不回應。

translations.literal: Where feather proclamations reached none failed respond.
translations.idiomatic: Every province answered his call.

sentences.zh: 至朝歌，眾二十餘萬。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhaoge masses over two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhaoge he held two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 趙驤至黃橋，為倫將士猗、許超所敗，死者八千餘人，士眾震駭。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiang reached Yellow Bridge defeated by Lun generals Shi Yi Xu Chao eight thousand dead masses shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiang lost eight thousand at Yellow Bridge.

sentences.zh: 穎欲退保朝歌，用盧志、王彥策，又使趙驤率眾八萬，與王彥俱進。

translations.literal: Ying wished retreat guard Zhaoge using Lu Zhi Wang Yan plan again sent Zhao Xiang leading masses eighty thousand with Wang Yan jointly advance.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi urged another eighty thousand under Zhao Xiang with Wang Yan.

sentences.zh: 倫復遣孫會、劉琨等率三萬人，與猗、超合兵距驤等，精甲耀日，鐵騎前驅。

translations.literal: Lun again dispatched Sun Hui Liu Kun leading thirty thousand merging Yi Chao combined troops resisting Xiang others gleaming armor dazzle sun iron cavalry front.
translations.idiomatic: Lun sent Sun Hui and Liu Kun thirty thousand joining Yi and Chao.

sentences.zh: 猗既戰勝，有輕驤之心。

translations.literal: Yi already battle victory held light Xiang heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yi grew careless after win.

sentences.zh: 未及溫十餘里，復大戰，猗等奔潰。

translations.literal: Before reaching Wen ten odd li again great battle Yi and others routed fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: Past Wen Yi routed Lun's van.

sentences.zh: 穎遂過河，乘勝長驅。

translations.literal: Ying then crossed river riding victory long drive.
translations.idiomatic: Ying crossed Yellow River in triumph.

sentences.zh: 左將軍王輿殺孫秀，幽趙王倫，迎天子反正。

translations.literal: Left General Wang Yu killed Sun Xiu imprisoned King Lun welcomed emperor restoring righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu killed Sun Xiu and caged Lun—Hui restored.

sentences.zh: 及穎入京都，誅倫。

translations.literal: When Ying entered capital executed Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Ying entered Luoyang and executed Lun.

sentences.zh: 使趙驤、石超等助齊王冏攻張泓于陽翟，泓等遂降。

translations.literal: Sent Zhao Xiang Shi Chao assisted Prince Jiong attack Zhang Hong at Yangzhai Hong etc thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He aided Jiong against Zhang Hong at Yangzhai until surrender.

sentences.zh: 冏始率眾入洛，自以首建大謀，遂擅威權。

translations.literal: Jiong beginning led masses entered Luoyang self thinking first establishing great stratagem thereupon monopolized awe authority.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong entered Luoyang first and seized power.

sentences.zh: 穎營於太學，及入朝，天子親勞焉。

translations.literal: Ying camped at Imperial Academy; when entering court Son of Heaven personally consoled.
translations.idiomatic: Ying pitched at the academy; Emperor Hui greeted him at court.

sentences.zh: 穎拜謝曰：「此大司馬臣冏之勳，臣無豫焉。

translations.literal: Ying bowed thanks saying: "This Grand Marshal subject Jiong's merit—your servant had no part.
translations.idiomatic: "This victory belongs to Prince Jiong—not me."

sentences.zh: 」見訖，即辭出，不復還營，便謁太廟，出自東陽城門，遂歸鄴。

translations.literal: " Audience finished—immediately took leave exiting—not returning camp—visited Grand Temple—out east Yang Gate—thereupon returned Ye.
translations.idiomatic: After court he bypassed camp, worshipped ancestors, left eastern Yang gate for Ye.

sentences.zh: 遣信與冏別，冏大驚，馳出送穎，至七里澗及之。

translations.literal: Sent messenger part with Jiong—Jiong greatly alarmed—galloped out sending Ying—reached Seven-li Gorge overtaking.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong raced after him to Seven-li Brook.

sentences.zh: 穎住車言別，流涕，不及時事，惟乙太妃疾苦形于顏色，百姓觀者莫不傾心。

translations.literal: Ying stopped carriage speaking parting; flowing tears; not reaching current affairs; only his mother Consort sick pain showing in face—commoners watching none not poured heart.
translations.idiomatic: At parting he wept only for his ailing mother—onlookers were moved.

sentences.zh: 至鄴，詔遣兼太尉王粹加九錫殊禮，進位大將軍、都督中外諸軍事、假節、加黃鉞、錄尚書事，入朝不趨，劍履上殿。

translations.literal: Reaching Ye edict dispatched concurrent Grand Master Wang Cui add nine bestowals special rites; advanced position Grand General supervise all armies within and without; credential; added yellow axe; record Masters of Writing; enter court not hurrying; sword shoes on hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ye received him with nine gifts, full command, yellow axe, and grand secretariat powers.

sentences.zh: 穎拜受徽號，讓殊禮九錫，表論興義功臣盧志、和演、董洪、王彥、趙驤等五人，皆封開國公侯。

translations.literal: Ying bowed accepted honorific title; declined special rites nine bestowals; memorial discussed rising merit meritorious subjects Lu Zhi, He Yan, Dong Hong, Wang Yan, Zhao Xiang etc five persons—each enfeoffed founding marquis or earl.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the trappings but enfeoffed Lu Zhi, He Yan, Dong Hong, Wang Yan, and Zhao Xiang.

sentences.zh: 又表稱：「大司馬前在陽翟，與強賊相持既久，百姓創痍，饑餓凍餒，宜急振救。

translations.literal: Also memorial said: "Grand Marshal former at Yangzhai with strong bandits stalemated long; common people wounded; hungry cold—ought urgently rescue.
translations.idiomatic: He asked relief for Yangzhai's starving people after the long siege.

sentences.zh: 乞差發郡縣車，一時運河北邸閣米十五萬斛，以振陽翟饑人。

translations.literal: Beg dispatch commandery county wagons at once transport Hebei granary rice hundred fifty thousand hu to relieve Yangzhai hungry people.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen million pecks from Hebei granaries were to feed Yangzhai.

sentences.zh: 」盧志言於穎曰：「黃橋戰亡者有八千餘人，既經夏暑，露骨中野，可為傷惻。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi spoke to Ying: "Yellow Bridge war dead have over eight thousand; already after summer heat bare bones mid-field—may pity.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi urged burial for eight thousand dead at Yellow Bridge.

sentences.zh: 昔周王葬枯骨，故《詩》云'行有死人，尚或墐之'。

translations.literal: Former Zhou king buried dry bones—therefore Odes says 'along road dead men yet someone buries them.'
translations.idiomatic: The Odes praise burying war dead.

sentences.zh: 況此等致死王事乎！

translations.literal: How much more those dying king's affairs!
translations.idiomatic: These died for Jin—they deserve graves.

sentences.zh: 」穎乃造棺八千餘枚，以成都國秩為衣服，斂祭，葬于黃橋北，樹枳籬為之塋域。

translations.literal: Ying then made coffins eight thousand; using Chengdu state revenues as garments encoffined sacrificed buried Yellow Bridge north planted thorn hedges as burial ground.
translations.idiomatic: He spent Chengdu revenue on eight thousand coffins and a walled burial ground north of Yellow Bridge.

sentences.zh: 又立都祭堂，刊石立碑，紀其赴義之功，使亡者之家四時祭祀有所。

translations.literal: Also erected communal memorial hall; carved stone erected stele recording their righteous merit—making bereaved families four seasons sacrifice had place.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a hall and stele so families could mourn seasonally.

sentences.zh: 仍表其門閭，加常戰亡二等。

translations.literal: Still inscribed their gate lintels—two grades above usual battle dead.
translations.idiomatic: Honored their gates above standard war dead.

sentences.zh: 又命河內溫縣埋藏趙倫戰死士卒萬四千餘人。

translations.literal: Also ordered Hanoi Wen county bury Zhao Lun battle-dead soldiers fourteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He buried Lun's fourteen thousand dead near Wen.

sentences.zh: 穎形美而神昏，不知書，然器性敦厚，委事於志，故得成其美焉。

translations.literal: Ying form handsome yet spirit dull did not know writing—yet disposition nature honest thick—entrusted affairs to Zhi—therefore accomplished his beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome but slow-witted, Ying delegated to Lu Zhi and flourished.

sentences.zh: 及齊王冏驕侈無禮，於是眾望歸之。

translations.literal: When Prince Jiong arrogant extravagant without propriety—thereupon popular hope returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong turned tyrant popular hope shifted to Ying.

sentences.zh: 詔遣侍中馮蓀、中書令卞粹喻穎入輔政，並使受九錫。

translations.literal: Edict dispatched Palace Attendant Feng Sun Director Bian Cui instruct Ying enter assisting government—and caused receive nine bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: Court sent Feng Sun and Bian Cui urging Ying to govern and take nine gifts.

sentences.zh: 穎猶讓不拜。

translations.literal: Ying still declined not accepting.
translations.idiomatic: Ying refused.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子太保。

translations.literal: Shortly added Grand Protector to Heir.
translations.idiomatic: He soon added Grand Tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 穎嬖人孟玖不欲還洛，又程太妃愛戀鄴都，以此議久不決。

translations.literal: Ying's favorite Meng Jiu did not wish return Luoyang; also Consort Cheng loved Ye capital—thereby discussion long undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jiu and his mother Consort Cheng kept him in Ye.

sentences.zh: 留義募將士既久，咸怨曠思歸，或有輒去者，乃題鄴城門云：「大事解散蠶欲遽。

translations.literal: Retained righteous recruited officers soldiers long—all resented delay longing return—some suddenly left—then inscribed Ye city gate saying: "Great affair dissolves silkworms wish hurry.
translations.idiomatic: Idle troops graffitied Ye's gates demanding release.

sentences.zh: 請且歸，赴時務。

translations.literal: Please temporarily return attend pressing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: "Let us go home for now."

sentences.zh: 昔以義來，今以義去。

translations.literal: Formerly came for righteousness—now leave for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: "We came for duty—now duty sends us home."

sentences.zh: 若復有急更相語。

translations.literal: If again urgent mutually speak.
translations.idiomatic: "Call us if crisis returns."

sentences.zh: 」穎知不可留，因遣之，百姓乃安。

translations.literal: " Ying knew unable detain—thereupon dispatched them—commoners then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Ying dismissed them and calm returned.

sentences.zh: 及冏敗，穎懸執朝政，事無巨細，皆就鄴諮之。

translations.literal: When Jiong defeated Ying suspended holding court government—affairs nothing huge tiny—all consulted Ye.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiong fell Ying ran the realm from Ye.

sentences.zh: 後張昌擾亂荊土，穎拜表南征，所在響赴。

translations.literal: Later Zhang Chang disturbed Jing lands—Ying memorialized southern expedition—where arrived echoed joining.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chang rioted Ying marched south and provinces rallied.

sentences.zh: 既恃功驕奢，百度弛廢，甚于冏時。

translations.literal: Already relying merit arrogant lavish hundred measures lax wasted worse than Jiong time.
translations.idiomatic: Success made him more corrupt than Jiong.

sentences.zh: 穎方恣其欲，而憚長沙王乂在內，遂與河間王顒表請誅後父羊玄之、左將軍皇甫商等，檄乂使就第。

translations.literal: Ying just indulged desires yet feared Prince Yi Changsha inside—thereupon with Prince Yong Hejian memorial requested execute empress father Yang Xuanzhi Left General Huangfu Shang etc—proclamation Yi go mansion.
translations.idiomatic: He allied with Yong against Yi and demanded Yang Xuanzhi and Huangfu Shang killed.

sentences.zh: 乃與顒將張方伐京都，以平原內史陸機為前鋒都督、前將軍、假節。

translations.literal: Then with Yong general Zhang Fang campaign capital—named Pingyuan Interior Secretary Lu Ji forward commander Forward General credential-bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lu Ji ahead with Zhang Fang.

sentences.zh: 穎次朝歌，每夜矛戟有光若火，其壘井中皆有龍象。

translations.literal: Ying halted Zhaoge—each night spears halberds had light like fire—their ramparts wells all had dragon signs.
translations.idiomatic: Omens lit Zhaoge camp—dragon shapes in wells.

sentences.zh: 進軍屯河南，阻清水為壘，造浮橋以通河北，以大木函盛石，沈之以系橋，名曰石鱉。

translations.literal: Advanced army garrisoned south of river—blocked clear water as rampart—built floating bridge linking north—large wooden box holding stones sunk to anchor bridge—named stone turtles.
translations.idiomatic: He bridged the river with stone anchors dubbed turtles.

sentences.zh: 陸機戰敗，死者甚眾，機又為孟玖所譖，穎收機斬之，夷其三族，語在《機傳》。

translations.literal: Lu Ji battle defeated dead very many; Ji again Meng Jiu slandered—Ying seized Ji executed—extirpated three clans—account in Lu Ji biography.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji lost; Meng Jiu framed him—Ying executed Ji and his clan.

sentences.zh: 於是進攻京城。

translations.literal: Thereupon advanced attacking capital.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時常山人王輿合眾萬餘，欲襲穎，會乂被執，其黨斬輿降。

translations.literal: At time Changshan man Wang Yu gathered masses over ten thousand wished raid Ying—meeting Yi seized—his faction beheaded Yu surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu's coup collapsed when allies killed him.

sentences.zh: 穎既入京師，復旋鎮於鄴，增封二十郡，拜丞相。

translations.literal: Ying already entered capital—again rotated garrisoned Ye—increased enfeoffment twenty commanderies—appointed Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After Luoyang Ying returned to Ye as chancellor with twenty commanderies.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒表穎宜為儲副，遂廢太子覃，立穎為皇太弟，丞相如故，制度一依魏武故事，乘輿服御皆遷於鄴。

translations.literal: Prince Yong Hejian memorialized Ying ought be heir-apparent—thereupon deposed Crown Prince Tan—established Ying imperial younger brother—Chancellor as before—institutions wholly followed Wei Wu precedent—imperial equipage all moved Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yong made Ying heir in place of Crown Prince Tan and moved the court gear to Ye.

sentences.zh: 表罷宿衛兵屬相府，更以王官宿衛。

translations.literal: Memorial dismissed night guard troops attach chancellor office—replaced with prince household guard night duty.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guard transferred to Ying's bureau.

sentences.zh: 僭侈日甚，有無君之心，委任孟玖等，大失眾望。

translations.literal: Usurping extravagance daily worse—had mind without lord—entrusted Meng Jiu etc—greatly lost popular hope.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled through Meng Jiu and alienated everyone.

sentences.zh: 永興初，左衛將軍陳眕，殿中中郎褾苞、成輔及長沙故將上官巳等，奉大駕討穎，馳檄四方，赴者雲集。

translations.literal: Yongxing start Left Guard General Chen Zhen Palace-Hall Gentlemen Biao Bao Cheng Fu and Changsha former general Shangguan Si etc upheld grand carriage campaigning Ying—feather proclamation four quarters—respondents cloud gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhen and allies marched on Ying with imperial guards.

sentences.zh: 軍次安陽，眾十餘萬，鄴中震懼。

translations.literal: Army halted Anyang—masses over hundred thousand—Ye within shaken feared.
translations.idiomatic: They camped at Anyang with a hundred thousand—Ye panicked.

sentences.zh: 穎欲走，其掾步熊有道術，曰：「勿動！

translations.literal: Ying wished flee—his clerk Bu Xiong had dao arts saying: "Do not move!
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Bu Xiong forbade flight.

sentences.zh: 南軍必敗。

translations.literal: South army surely defeated.
translations.idiomatic: "The southern host will lose."

sentences.zh: 」穎會其眾問計，東安王繇乃曰：「天子親征，宜罷甲，縞素出迎請罪。

translations.literal: " Ying convened masses asking plan—Prince Yao of Dong'an then said: "Son of Heaven personally campaigns—ought lay armor white silk exit welcome confess guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yao urged surrender in white.

sentences.zh: 」司馬王混、參軍崔曠勸穎距戰，穎從之，乃遣奮武將軍石超率眾五萬，次於蕩陰。

translations.literal: " Major Wang Hun adjutant Cui Kuang urged Ying resist battle—Ying followed—sent Fearless General Shi Chao masses fifty thousand halted Dangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun and Cui Kuang talked him into fighting—Shi Chao held Dangyin.

sentences.zh: 眕二弟匡、規自鄴赴王師，云：「鄴中皆已離散。

translations.literal: Chen Zhen two younger brothers Kuang Gui from Ye rushed royal army saying: "Ye within all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's brothers reported Ye collapsing.

sentences.zh: 」由是不甚設備。

translations.literal: " Thereby not greatly set defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Ying relaxed his guard.

sentences.zh: 超眾奄至，王師敗績，矢及乘輿，侍中嵇紹死於帝側，左右皆奔散，乃棄天子于槁中。

translations.literal: Chao masses suddenly arrived—royal army crushed—arrows reached imperial carriage—Palace Attendant Ji Shao died emperor side—left-right all fled scattered—then abandoned Son of Heaven in hay cart.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chao routed Hui; Ji Shao died shielding him—Hui was abandoned in a wagon.

sentences.zh: 超遂奉帝幸鄴。

translations.literal: Chao then upheld Emperor favoring Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chao convoyed Hui to Ye.

sentences.zh: 穎改元建武，害東安王繇，署置百官，殺生自己，立郊于鄴南。

translations.literal: Ying changed era Jianwu—harmed Prince Yao of Dong'an—installed hundred officials—life death from self—established suburban altar south Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Ying changed reign name, killed Prince Yao, packed court with cronies, built suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 安北將軍王浚、甯北將軍東嬴公騰殺穎所置幽州刺史和演，穎征浚，浚屯冀州不進，與騰及烏丸、羯硃襲穎。

translations.literal: General Who Guards North Wang Jun Ningbei Duke Teng of Dongying killed Ying's appointed You Province Inspector He Yan—Ying campaigned Jun—Jun garrisoned Ji Province not advancing—with Teng and Wuhuan Jie tribe raided Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun and Duke Teng killed He Yan and struck Ye with Wuhuan and Jie auxiliaries.

sentences.zh: 候騎至鄴，穎遣幽州刺史王斌及石超、李毅等距浚，為羯硃等所敗。

translations.literal: Scouts reached Ye—Ying dispatched You Inspector Wang Bin and Shi Chao Li Yi resist Jun—defeated by Jie tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Ying lost to Wang Jun's tribal allies.

sentences.zh: 鄴中大震，百僚奔走，士卒分散。

translations.literal: Ye within great shake—hundred officials fled—soldiers scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Ye collapsed in panic.

sentences.zh: 穎懼，將帳下數十騎，擁天子，與中書監慮志單車而走，五日至洛。

translations.literal: Ying feared—led tent several tens riders—upholding Son of Heaven—with Palace Secretariat Supervisor Lu Zhi single cart fled—five days reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ying fled toward Luoyang with Hui and Lu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 羯硃追至朝歌，不及而還。

translations.literal: Jie tribe pursued reaching Zhaoge—not overtook returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Jie broke off pursuit at Zhaoge.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒遣張方率甲卒二萬救穎，至洛，方乃挾帝，擁穎及豫章王並高光、慮志等歸於長安。

translations.literal: Prince Yong dispatched Zhang Fang armor soldiers twenty thousand rescue Ying—reaching Luoyang—Fang seized Emperor—upholding Ying and Prince Zhaoge of Yuzhang together Gao Guang Lu Zhi etc returned Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang took Hui and Ying west to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 顒廢穎歸籓，以豫章王為皇太弟。

translations.literal: Yong deposed Ying return fief—established Prince Zhaoge imperial younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yong stripped Ying and named Prince Zhaoge heir.

sentences.zh: 穎既廢，河北思之。

translations.literal: Ying already deposed—Hebei misses him.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei still longed for Ying.

sentences.zh: 鄴中故將公師籓、汲桑等起兵以迎穎，眾情翕然。

translations.literal: Ye former generals Gongshi Fan Ji Sang raised troops welcoming Ying—mass sentiment agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Ye generals Gongshi Fan and Ji Sang rose to recall him.

sentences.zh: 顒復拜穎鎮軍大將軍、都督河北諸軍事，給兵千人，鎮鄴。

translations.literal: Yong again appointed Ying Guard Army Grand General supervise Hebei military affairs—given troops thousand—garrison Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yong restored Ying to guard Hebei with a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 穎至洛，而東海王越率眾迎大駕，所在鋒起。

translations.literal: Ying reached Luoyang—yet Prince Yue Donghai led masses welcoming grand carriage—everywhere spearheads rose.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang Prince Yue rose with imperial escort.

sentences.zh: 穎以北方盛強，懼不可進，自洛陽奔關中。

translations.literal: Ying because north flourished strong feared unable advance—from Luoyang fled Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Ying fled north's strength for Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 值大駕還洛，穎自華陰趨武關，出新野。

translations.literal: Meeting grand carriage returning Luoyang—Ying from Huayin hurried Wuguan—exited Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui returned Luoyang Ying raced south via Wuguan.

sentences.zh: 帝詔鎮南將軍劉弘、南中郎將劉陶收捕穎，於是棄母妻，單車與二子廬江王普、中都王廓渡河赴朝歌，收合故將士數百人，欲就公師籓。

translations.literal: Emperor edict Guard South Liu Hong Southern Colonel Liu Tao seize capture Ying—thereupon abandoned mother wife—single cart with two sons Prince Pu of Lujiang Prince Kuo of Zhongdu crossed river toward Zhaoge gathering former officers soldiers hundred persons—wished join Gongshi Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts hunted him—he fled toward Gongshi Fan abandoning family.

sentences.zh: 頓丘太守馮嵩執穎及普、廓送鄴，范陽王虓幽之，而無他意。

translations.literal: Dunqiu prefect Feng Song seized Ying and Pu Kuo delivered Ye—Prince Xiao of Fanyang confined him—without other intent.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Song captured him for Prince Xiao who jailed him.

sentences.zh: 屬虓暴薨，虓長史劉輿見穎為鄴都所服，慮為後患，秘不發喪，偽令人為台使，稱詔夜賜穎死。

translations.literal: Meeting Xiao sudden death—Xiao chief clerk Liu Yu saw Ying obeyed Ye capital—worried later trouble—secret not issued mourning—falsely made person as terrace envoy—claimed edict night gifted Ying death.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao died Liu Yu forged an order killing Ying.

sentences.zh: 穎謂守者田徽曰：「范陽王亡乎？

translations.literal: Ying told guard Tian Hui: "Prince Xiao dead?
translations.idiomatic: Ying asked guard Tian Hui if Xiao had died.

sentences.zh: 」徽曰：「不知。

translations.literal: " Hui said: "Not know.
translations.idiomatic: "I do not know."

sentences.zh: 」穎曰：「卿年幾？

translations.literal: " Ying said: "Your age how many?
translations.idiomatic: "How old are you?"

sentences.zh: 」徽曰：「五十。

translations.literal: " Hui said: "Fifty.
translations.idiomatic: "Fifty."

sentences.zh: 」穎曰：「知天命不？

translations.literal: " Ying said: "Know heaven's mandate?
translations.idiomatic: "Do you know Heaven's will?"

sentences.zh: 」徽曰：「不知。

translations.literal: " Hui said: "Not know.
translations.idiomatic: "I do not."

sentences.zh: 」穎曰：「我死之後，天下安乎不安乎？

translations.literal: " Ying said: "After I die All-under-Heaven tranquil or not tranquil?
translations.idiomatic: "Will the realm know peace after I die?"

sentences.zh: 我自放逐，於今三年，身體手足不見洗沐，取數斗湯來！

translations.literal: I self banished—until now three years—body hands feet not seen wash bathe—bring several dou hot water!
translations.idiomatic: I have not bathed three years—bring water.

sentences.zh: 」其二子號泣，穎敕人將去。

translations.literal: His two sons wailed—Ying ordered people lead away.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his sons away.

sentences.zh: 乃散發東首臥，命徽縊之，時年二十八。

translations.literal: Then loosed hair east head lay—ordered Hui strangle—age twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He lay east-facing and had Tian Hui strangle him at twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 二子亦死。

translations.literal: Two sons also died.
translations.idiomatic: His sons died too.

sentences.zh: 鄴中哀之。

translations.literal: Ye within mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Ye mourned him.

sentences.zh: 穎之敗也，官屬並奔散，惟盧志隨從不怠，論者稱之。

translations.literal: Ying's defeat—officials all fled—only Lu Zhi followed without slack—commentators praised.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lu Zhi stayed loyal.

sentences.zh: 其後汲桑害東贏公騰，稱為穎報仇，遂出穎棺，載之於軍中，每事啟靈，以行軍令。

translations.literal: Later Ji Sang harmed Duke Teng of Dongying—claimed avenging Ying—thereupon exhumed Ying coffin—loaded army—each affair consulted spirit—used execute military orders.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang carried Ying's coffin as a talisman.

sentences.zh: 桑敗，度棺于故井中。

translations.literal: Sang defeated—placed coffin old well.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang dumped the coffin in a well.

sentences.zh: 穎故臣收之，改葬於洛陽，懷帝加以縣王禮。

translations.literal: Ying former ministers collected—reburied Luoyang—Emperor Huai added county prince rites.
translations.idiomatic: Old aides reburied him at Luoyang with princely honors.

sentences.zh: 穎死後數年，開封間有傳穎子年十餘歲，流離百姓家，東海王越遣人殺之。

translations.literal: Several years after Ying died Kaifeng rumor transmitted Ying son age ten odd wandering common households—Prince Yue Donghai dispatched person kill.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue hunted down a rumored surviving son.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，立東萊王蕤子遵為穎嗣，封華容縣王。

translations.literal: Yongjia established Prince Rui's son Zun as Ying heir—enfeoffed Prince of Huarong county.
translations.idiomatic: Huai made Sima Zun his nominal heir.

sentences.zh: 後沒于賊，國除。

translations.literal: Later lost to bandits—state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The line ended when Zun fell to rebels.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒

translations.literal: Prince Yong of Hejian Yong
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian

sentences.zh: 河間王顒，字文載，安平獻王孚孫，太原烈王瑰之子也。

translations.literal: Prince Yong Hejian Yong courtesy Wenzai—Prince Xian of Anping Fu grandson—Prince Lie of Taiyuan Gui son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong, courtesy Wenzai, was grandson of Prince Fu and son of Prince Gui.

sentences.zh: 初襲父爵，咸寧二年就國。

translations.literal: First inherited father's noble rank—Xianning second year proceeded state.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited in Xianning 2.

sentences.zh: 三年，改封河間。

translations.literal: Third year changed enfeoffment Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Year three he became Prince of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 少有清名，輕財愛士。

translations.literal: Youth had clear fame—light wealth loved gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Young he was generous and esteemed scholars.

sentences.zh: 與諸王俱來朝，武帝歎顒可以為諸國儀錶。

translations.literal: With various kings together came court—Emperor Wu sighed Yong could be various states model.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu called him a model prince.

sentences.zh: 元康初，為北中郎將，監鄴城。

translations.literal: Yuankang start—North Central Army general supervised Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: Early Yuankang he guarded Ye.

sentences.zh: 九年，代梁王肜為平西將軍，鎮關中。

translations.literal: Ninth year replaced Prince Rong of Liang as General Who Pacifies West garrisoned Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Year nine he replaced Prince Rong holding Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 石函之制，非親親不得都督關中，顒于諸王為疏，特以賢舉。

translations.literal: Stone coffer system—not intimate kin cannot supervise Guanzhong—Yong among kings distant—specially by worth promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Non-kin rarely held Guanzhong—Yong won it on merit.

sentences.zh: 及趙王倫篡位，齊王冏謀討之。

translations.literal: When King Lun usurped Prince Jiong plotted punish.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun seized the throne Jiong plotted.

sentences.zh: 前安西參軍夏侯奭自稱侍御史，在始平合眾，得數千人，以應冏，遣信要顒。

translations.literal: Former West Adjutant Xia Hou Shi self-called Attendant Censor—at Shiping gathered masses obtained several thousand—responding Jiong—sent messenger summon Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Hou Shi raised troops for Jiong and summoned Yong.

sentences.zh: 顒遣主簿房陽、河間國人張方討擒奭，及其黨十數人，于長安市腰斬之。

translations.literal: Yong dispatched chief clerk Fang Yang and Hejian native Zhang Fang on campaign to capture Shi—and his faction over ten persons—in Chang'an market waist-chopped them.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yang and Zhang Fang seized Xia Hou Shi and his band and executed them at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 及冏檄至，顒執冏使，送之於倫。

translations.literal: When Jiong proclamation arrived Yong seized Jiong envoy—delivered to Lun.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong's manifesto came Yong bound his courier for Lun.

sentences.zh: 倫徵兵於顒，顒遣方率關右健將赴之。

translations.literal: Lun recruited troops from Yong—Yong dispatched Fang leading Guanyou stalwarts to join.
translations.idiomatic: Lun drafted Yong's army—Zhang Fang led west-country veterans east.

sentences.zh: 方至華陰，顒聞二王兵盛，乃加長史李含龍驤將軍，領督護席薳等追方軍回，以應二王。

translations.literal: Fang reached Huayin—Yong heard two kings' armies mighty—thereupon promoted Chief Clerk Li Han Dragon-Soar general commanding protectors Xi Wei etc pursue Fang's army back—to respond two kings.
translations.idiomatic: At Huayin Yong recalled Fang when coalition grew strong.

sentences.zh: 義兵至潼關，而倫、秀已誅，天子反正，含、方各率眾還。

translations.literal: Righteous army reached Tong Pass yet Lun and Xiu already executed Son of Heaven reversed correctness—Han and Fang each led masses back.
translations.idiomatic: By Tong Pass Lun had fallen—Fang and Li Han marched home.

sentences.zh: 及冏論功，雖怒顒初不同，而終能濟義，進位侍中、太尉，加三賜之禮。

translations.literal: When Jiong judged merit—although angry Yong first disagreed—yet ultimately aided righteousness—advanced Palace Attendant Grand Commandant added three presentations rites.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong still promoted Yong despite early hesitation.

sentences.zh: 後含為翊軍校尉，與冏參軍皇甫商、司馬趙驤等有憾，遂奔顒，詭稱受密詔伐冏，因說利害。

translations.literal: Later Han became Colonel of Guards Army—with Jiong adjutant Huangfu Shang Major Zhao Xiang etc had grudge—thereupon fled Yong—falsely claimed received secret edict campaign Jiong—thereby explained profit harm.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han fled to Yong and forged orders against Jiong.

sentences.zh: 顒納之，便發兵，遣使邀成都王穎。

translations.literal: Yong accepted—then raised troops—dispatched envoy inviting Prince Ying Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Yong mobilized and summoned Prince Ying.

sentences.zh: 以含為都督，率諸軍屯陰盤，前鋒次於新安，去洛百二十里。

translations.literal: Named Han commander-in-chief leading various armies garrison Yinpan—forward van halted Xin'an—one hundred twenty li from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han camped at Yinpan near Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 檄長沙王乂討冏。

translations.literal: Proclamation Prince Yi Changsha campaign Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: His manifesto ordered Yi to strike Jiong.

sentences.zh: 及冏敗，顒以含為河南尹，使與馮蓀、卞粹等潛圖害乂。

translations.literal: When Jiong defeated Yong named Han Henan Intendant caused with Feng Sun Bian Cui etc secretly plot harm Yi.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiong fell Yong made Li Han Henan governor to murder Yi.

sentences.zh: 商知含前矯妄及與顒陰謀，具以告乂。

translations.literal: Shang knew Han former falsehood and Yong conspiracy—fully reported Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Shang exposed Li Han to Yi.

sentences.zh: 乂乃誅含等。

translations.literal: Yi then executed Han etc.
translations.idiomatic: Yi executed Li Han's cabal.

sentences.zh: 顒聞含死，即起兵以討商為名，使張方為都督，領精卒七萬向洛。

translations.literal: Yong heard Han died—immediately raised troops under pretext campaigning Shang—sent Fang commander-in-chief leading picked troops seventy thousand toward Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yong marched on Huangfu Shang with seventy thousand.

sentences.zh: 方攻商，商距戰而潰，方遂進攻西明門。

translations.literal: Fang attacked Shang—Shang resisted battle yet routed—Fang advanced attacking West Bright Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang routed Shang at Ximing Gate.

sentences.zh: 乂率中軍左右衛擊之，方眾大敗，死者五千餘人。

translations.literal: Yi led central army left-right guard struck—Fang masses greatly defeated—dead five thousand odd.
translations.idiomatic: Yi shattered Fang losing five thousand.

sentences.zh: 方初于駃水橋西為營，於是築壘數重，外引廩穀，以足軍資。

translations.literal: Fang first at Kuai River Bridge west built camp—thereupon piled ramparts several layers—outside drew granary grain—to equip army supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Fang fortified beyond Kuai Bridge with granaries.

sentences.zh: 乂復從天子出攻方，戰輒不利。

translations.literal: Yi again followed Son of Heaven out attacking Fang—battle repeatedly unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Hui attacked Fang without luck.

sentences.zh: 及乂死，方還長安。

translations.literal: When Yi died Fang returned Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fang withdrew to Chang'an after Yi fell.

sentences.zh: 詔以顒為太宰、大都督、雍州牧。

translations.literal: Edict named Yong Grand Tutor Grand Commander Yongzhou Shepherd.
translations.idiomatic: Hui named Yong Grand Tutor and Yongzhou governor.

sentences.zh: 顒廢皇太子覃，立成都王穎為太弟，改年，大赦。

translations.literal: Yong deposed Crown Prince Tan—established Prince Ying Chengdu imperial younger brother—changed era—great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yong replaced Tan with Prince Ying as heir.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍陳眕奉天子伐穎，顒又遣方率兵二萬救鄴。

translations.literal: Left Guard Chen Zhen upheld Son of Heaven campaigning Ying—Yong again dispatched Fang troops twenty thousand rescue Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhen attacked Ying while Yong reinforced Ye.

sentences.zh: 天子已幸鄴。

translations.literal: Son of Heaven already favored Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was already at Ye.

sentences.zh: 方屯兵洛陽。

translations.literal: Fang garrisoned troops Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang held Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及王浚等伐穎，穎挾天子歸洛陽。

translations.literal: When Wang Jun etc campaigned Ying—Ying seized Son of Heaven returning Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ying brought Hui back from Ye.

sentences.zh: 方將兵入殿中，逼帝幸其壘，掠府庫，將焚宮廟以絕眾心。

translations.literal: Fang led troops entering hall—pressing Emperor favor his camp—plundered treasury—would burn palace temples to cut masses' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Fang looted Luoyang and meant to torch the palace.

sentences.zh: 盧志諫，乃止。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi remonstrated—then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi stopped the burning.

sentences.zh: 方又逼天子幸長安。

translations.literal: Fang again pressed Son of Heaven favor Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fang dragged Hui west.

sentences.zh: 顒及選置百官，改秦州為定州。

translations.literal: Yong together installed hundred officials—changed Qin Province to Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yong reshuffled offices and renamed Qin to Ding.

sentences.zh: 及東海王越起兵徐州，西迎大駕，關中大懼，方謂顒曰：「方所領猶有十餘萬眾，奉送大駕還洛宮，使成都王反鄴，公自留鎮關中，方北討博陵。

translations.literal: When Prince Yue Donghai raised troops Xuzhou west welcoming grand carriage—Guanzhong greatly feared—Fang told Yong: "Fang commands still over hundred thousand masses—escort grand carriage return Luoyang palace—cause Prince Chengdu return Ye—duke yourself remain guard Guanzhong—Fang north campaign Boping.
translations.idiomatic: Fang proposed returning Hui while Yong stayed west.

sentences.zh: 如此，天下可小安，無復舉手者。

translations.literal: Thus All-under-Heaven could little settle—no again raising hands.
translations.idiomatic: "Peace would return without further risings."

sentences.zh: 」顒慮事大難濟，不許。

translations.literal: " Yong worried affair hard succeed—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yong refused.

sentences.zh: 乃假劉喬節，進位鎮東大將軍，遣成都王穎總統樓褒、王闡等諸軍，據河橋以距越。

translations.literal: Then lent Liu Qiao staffs—advanced Guard East Grand General—dispatched Prince Ying Chengdu commander Lou Bao Wang Chan etc armies holding river bridge resist Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yong armed Liu Qiao and Prince Ying to hold the Yellow River bridge.

sentences.zh: 王浚遣督護劉根，將三百騎至河上。

translations.literal: Wang Jun dispatched protector Liu Gen leading three hundred cavalry reaching river.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun sent Liu Gen to the ford.

sentences.zh: 闡出戰，為根所殺。

translations.literal: Chan exited battle—was killed by Gen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chan fell to Liu Gen.

sentences.zh: 穎頓軍張方故壘，范陽王虓遣鮮卑騎與平昌、博陵眾襲河橋，樓褒西走，追騎至新安，道路死者不可勝數。

translations.literal: Ying halted army Zhang Fang old rampart—Prince Xiao Fanyang dispatched Xianbei cavalry with Pingchang Boping masses raid river bridge—Lou Bao fled west—pursuit cavalry reached Xin'an—road dead countless.
translations.idiomatic: Coalition smashed Lou Bao at the bridge.

sentences.zh: 初，越以張方劫遷車駕，天下怨憤，唱義與山東諸侯克期奉迎，先遣說顒，令送帝還都，與顒分陝而居。

translations.literal: First Yue because Zhang Fang seized imperial carriage All-under-Heaven resentful—raised righteousness with Shandong lords timed welcome—first dispatched persuade Yong ordering deliver emperor return capital—with Yong divide Shan dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue rallied east against Fang's seizure of Hui.

sentences.zh: 顒欲從之，而方不同。

translations.literal: Yong wished follow yet Fang disagreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yong wavered but Fang refused.

sentences.zh: 及東軍大捷，成都等敗，顒乃令方親信將郅輔夜斬方，送首以示東軍。

translations.literal: When east army great victory Chengdu etc defeated Yong then ordered Fang trusted general Zhi Fu night behead Fang—sent head display east army.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sacrificed Zhang Fang's head to appease the east.

sentences.zh: 尋變計，更遣刁默守潼關，乃咎輔殺方，又斬輔。

translations.literal: Shortly changed plan—again dispatched Diao Mo guard Tong Pass—then blamed Fu killing Fang—again beheaded Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He double-crossed Zhi Fu after using him.

sentences.zh: 顒先遣將呂朗等據滎陽，范陽王虓司馬劉琨以方首示朗，於是朗降。

translations.literal: Yong first dispatched generals Lu Lang etc held Xingyang—Prince Xiao Fanyang Major Liu Kun with Fang head displayed Lang—thereupon Lang surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun showed Fang's head and took Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 時東軍既盛，破刁默以入關，顒懼，又遣馬瞻、郭傳于霸水禦之，瞻等戰敗散走。

translations.literal: At time east army already fierce defeated Diao Mo to enter pass—Yong feared—again dispatched Ma Zhan Guo Chuan at Bashui resist—these defeated scattered fled.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern allies smashed Yong's Bashui line.

sentences.zh: 顒乘單馬，逃於太白山。

translations.literal: Yong rode single horse fled Taibai Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Yong fled to Taibai Mountain.

sentences.zh: 東軍入長安，大駕旋，乙太弟太保梁柳為鎮西將軍，守關中。

translations.literal: East army entered Chang'an—grand carriage rotated—appointed imperial younger brother Grand Protector Liang Liu western general guard Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern troops recovered Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 馬瞻等出詣柳，因共殺柳於城內。

translations.literal: Ma Zhan etc went out to Liu—together killed Liu inside city.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhan murdered Liang Liu inside Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 瞻等與始平太守梁邁合從，迎顒于南山。

translations.literal: Zhan etc allied Shiping prefect Liang Mai—welcomed Yong from southern mountain.
translations.idiomatic: They welcomed Yong from the hills.

sentences.zh: 顒初不肯入府，長安令蘇眾、記室督硃永勸顒表稱柳病卒，輒知方事。

translations.literal: Yong first refused enter mansion—Chang'an prefect Su Zhong registrar Zhu Yong urged Yong memorialize claim Liu sudden death—pretend know Fang affair.
translations.idiomatic: Yong plotted his return with forged Liu death.

sentences.zh: 弘農太守裴暠、秦國內史賈龕、安定太守賈疋等起義討顒，斬馬瞻、梁邁等。

translations.literal: Hongnong prefect Pei Gao Qin interior secretary Jia Kan Anding prefect Jia Ya etc raised righteousness campaign Yong—beheaded Ma Zhan Liang Mai etc.
translations.idiomatic: Heartland prefects rose and executed Ma Zhan.

sentences.zh: 東海王越遣督護麋晃率國兵伐顒。

translations.literal: Prince Yue Donghai dispatched protector Mi Huang leading state troops campaign Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue sent Mi Huang against Yong.

sentences.zh: 至鄭，顒將牽秀距晃，晃斬秀，並其二子。

translations.literal: Reaching Zheng Yong general Qian Xiu resisted Huang—Huang beheaded Xiu together two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Huang killed Qian Xiu at Zheng.

sentences.zh: 義軍據有關中，顒保城而已。

translations.literal: Righteous army occupied Guanzhong—Yong merely guarded city.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was trapped in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，詔書以顒為司徒，乃就征。

translations.literal: Yongjia start edict named Yong Minister of Education—then accepted summons.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia summoned Yong as minister.

sentences.zh: 南陽王模遣將梁臣于新安雍谷車上扼殺之，並其三子。

translations.literal: Prince Nan Yang Mo dispatched general Liang Chen at Xin'an Yong valley cart strangled him together three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mo assassinated Yong en route.

sentences.zh: 詔以彭城元王植子融為顒嗣，改封樂成縣王。

translations.literal: Edict named Pengcheng Prince Yuan Zhi son Rong Yong heir—changed enfeoffment Prince of Lecheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Court adopted Rong as Yong's heir.

sentences.zh: 薨，無子。

translations.literal: Died—no son.
translations.idiomatic: Rong died heirless.

sentences.zh: 建興中，元帝又以彭城康王釋子欽為融嗣。

translations.literal: Jianxing middle Yuan Emperor again Pengcheng Prince Kang Shi son Qin as Rong heir.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Di assigned Qin as heir.

sentences.zh: 東海孝獻王越

translations.literal: Prince Xiaoxian Donghai Yue
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue, Prince Xiaoxian of Donghai

sentences.zh: 東海孝獻王越，字元超，高密王泰之次子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xiaoxian Donghai Yue courtesy Yuanchao—Prince Gao Mi Tai second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue courtesy Yuanchao—second son of Prince Tai of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 少有令名，謙虛持布衣之操，為中外所宗。

translations.literal: Youth had good fame—humble maintained common cloth conduct—central outer all modeled.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned for humility.

sentences.zh: 初以世子為騎都尉，與駙馬都尉楊邈及琅邪王伷子繇俱侍講東宮，拜散騎侍郎，曆左衛將軍，加侍中。

translations.literal: First as heir son Coachman Commandant—with Chief Groom Yang Miao and Langye Prince You son Yao together lectured Eastern Palace—appointed Gentleman Attendant—passed Left Guard general added Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He tutored the heir with Yang Miao and Sima Yao.

sentences.zh: 討楊駿有功，封五千戶侯。

translations.literal: Campaign Yang Jun had merit—enfeoffed five thousand household marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He earned a marquisate crushing Yang Jun.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍、輔國將軍、尚書右僕射，領遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Transferred Gentleman Attendant Supports State general Masters of Writing Right Deputy Director concurrently Raid general.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to secretary deputy and raid general.

sentences.zh: 復為侍中，加奉車都尉，給溫信五十人，別封東海王，食六縣。

translations.literal: Again Palace Attendant added Coachman Commandant given Warm Letter fifty persons separate enfeoffment Prince Donghai eating six counties.
translations.idiomatic: He became Prince of Donghai with fifty messengers.

sentences.zh: 永康初，為中書令，徙侍中，遷司空，領中書監。

translations.literal: Yongkang start Director Palace Secretariat transferred Palace Attendant promoted Minister of Works concurrently Palace Secretariat Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongkang he headed Secretariat and became minister.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎攻長沙王乂，乂固守洛陽，殿中諸將及三部司馬疲于戰守，密與左衛將軍硃默夜收乂別省，逼越為主，啟惠帝免乂官。

translations.literal: Prince Ying Chengdu attacked Prince Yi Changsha—Yi firmly guarded Luoyang—hall generals Three Majors weary battle guard—secretly with Left Guard Zhu Mo night seized Yi separate hall—pressed Yue master—opened Emperor Hui dismiss Yi office.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards seized Yi and forced Prince Yue to lead.

sentences.zh: 事定，越稱疾遜位。

translations.literal: Affair settled—Yue claimed illness yielding position.
translations.idiomatic: Yue feigned resignation.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，加守尚書令。

translations.literal: Emperor not permitted—added provisional Masters of Writing Director.
translations.idiomatic: Hui refused and named him recording minister.

sentences.zh: 太安初，帝北征鄴，以越為大都督。

translations.literal: Tai'an start Emperor north expedition Ye—named Yue Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Tai'an northern march made Yue commander.

sentences.zh: 六軍敗，越奔下邳，徐州都督、東平王楙不納，越徑還東海。

translations.literal: Six armies defeated—Yue fled Xiapi—Xuzhou commander Prince Mao Dongping not admitted—Yue straight returned Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Six hosts lost—Yue fled to Donghai.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎以越兄弟宗室之美，下寬令招之，越不應命。

translations.literal: Prince Ying Chengdu because Yue brothers clan beauty issued generous edict summon—Yue did not respond mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying summoned Yue—ignored.

sentences.zh: 帝西幸，以越為太傅，與太宰顒夾輔朝政，讓不受。

translations.literal: Emperor favored west—named Yue Grand Tutor together Grand Tutor Yong flank assist court government—declined not accepting.
translations.idiomatic: Western court named Yue Grand Tutor—declined.

sentences.zh: 東海中尉劉洽勸越發兵以備穎，越以洽為左司馬，尚書曹馥為軍司。

translations.literal: Donghai lieutenant Liu Qia urged Yue raise troops guard Ying—Yue named Qia Left Major Masters of Writing Cao Fu army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qia spurred Prince Yue's army.

sentences.zh: 既起兵，楙懼，乃以州與越。

translations.literal: Already raised troops Mao feared—thereupon gave province Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mao yielded Xuzhou to Yue.

sentences.zh: 越以司空領徐州都督，以楙領兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Yue with Minister of Works headed Xuzhou commander—named Mao Yan Province Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Yue took Xuzhou and gave Mao Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 越三弟並據方任征伐，輒選刺史守相，朝士多赴越。

translations.literal: Yue three younger brothers together held regional commands expedition appointment chose prefects defending ministers—court gentlemen mostly rushed Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yue clan dominated appointments.

sentences.zh: 而河間王顒挾天子，發詔罷越等，皆令就國。

translations.literal: Yet Prince Yong Hejian seized Son of Heaven issued edict dismiss Yue etc—all ordered go states.
translations.idiomatic: Yong ordered princes home.

sentences.zh: 越唱義奉迎大駕，還復舊都，率甲卒三萬，西次蕭縣。

translations.literal: Yue raised righteousness welcoming grand carriage—restore old capital—led armored soldiers thirty thousand—west halted Xiao county.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue marched west from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史劉喬不受越命，遣子祐距之，越軍敗。

translations.literal: Yu Province Inspector Liu Qiao refused Yue mandate—dispatched son You resist—Yue army defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao defied Yue and beat him.

sentences.zh: 范陽王虓遣督護田徽以突騎八百迎越，遇祐於譙，祐眾潰，越進屯陽武。

translations.literal: Prince Xiao Fanyang dispatched protector Tian Hui with raid cavalry eight hundred welcoming Yue—met You at Qiao—You masses routed—Yue advanced garrison Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hui rescued Yue at Qiao.

sentences.zh: 山東兵盛，關中大懼，顒斬送張方首求和，尋變計距越。

translations.literal: Shandong army fierce Guanzhong greatly feared—Yong beheaded displayed Zhang Fang head seeking peace—shortly changed plan resist Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yong offered Fang's head then relented.

sentences.zh: 越率諸侯及鮮卑許扶曆、駒次宿歸等步騎迎惠帝反洛陽。

translations.literal: Yue led lords and Xianbei Xu Fuli Ju Ci Sugui etc infantry cavalry welcoming Emperor Hui returning Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue escorted Hui east with tribal horse.

sentences.zh: 詔越乙太傅錄尚書，以下邳、濟陽二郡增封。

translations.literal: Edict Yue Grand Tutor record Masters of Writing—added Xiapi Jiyang two commanderies enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Hui restored Yue as tutor with added fiefs.

sentences.zh: 及懷帝即位，委政於越。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended entrusted government Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Huai left policy to Yue.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎周穆，清河王覃舅，越之姑子也，與其妹夫諸葛玫共說越曰：「主上之為太弟，張方意也。

translations.literal: Personnel Gentleman Zhou Mu Prince Tan Qing uncle Yue's aunt son—with brother-in-law Zhuge Mei together persuaded Yue: "Lord above becoming imperial younger brother—Zhang Fang intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mu urged restoring Tan.

sentences.zh: 清河王本太子，為群凶所廢。

translations.literal: Prince Qing Tan originally crown prince—was villain gang deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was true heir.

sentences.zh: 先帝暴崩，多疑東宮。

translations.literal: Former emperor sudden death—much doubt Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Sudden death bred suspicion.

sentences.zh: 公盍思伊、霍之舉，以寧社稷乎？

translations.literal: Why not ponder Yi Huo deed—to settle altars?
translations.idiomatic: Why not play Yi Yin?

sentences.zh: 」言未卒，越曰：「此豈宜言邪！

translations.literal: " Words not finished—Yue said: "How dare speak thus!
translations.idiomatic: Yue cut them off.

sentences.zh: 」遂叱左右斬之。

translations.literal: " Then barked attendants behead.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Zhou Mu and Zhuge Mei.

sentences.zh: 以玫、穆世家，罪止其身，因此表除三族之法。

translations.literal: Because Mei Mu noble houses—guilt stopped bodies—thereby memorial abolished three-clan law.
translations.idiomatic: He spared their kin but ended three-clan punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝始親萬機，留心庶事，越不悅，求出籓，帝不許。

translations.literal: Emperor began personally myriad cares attending common affairs—Yue unhappy—requested outer fief—Emperor not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Huai tried ruling—Yue sulked.

sentences.zh: 越遂出鎮許昌。

translations.literal: Yue then went out garrison Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yue moved to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，自許昌率苟晞及冀州刺史丁劭討汲桑，破之。

translations.literal: Yongjia start from Xuchang led Gou Xi Ji Province Inspector Ding Shao campaign Ji Sang defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia saw him crush Ji Sang from Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 越還于許，長史潘滔說之曰：「兗州天下樞要，公宜自牧。

translations.literal: Yue returned Xu chief clerk Pan Tao urged: "Yanzhou realm pivot—duke ought self shepherd.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Tao urged taking Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 」及轉苟晞為青州刺史，由是與晞有隙。

translations.literal: " Then transferred Gou Xi Qing Province Inspector—thereby with Gou Xi had rift.
translations.idiomatic: Moving Gou Xi soured their alliance.

sentences.zh: 尋詔越為丞相，領兗州牧，督兗、豫、司、冀、幽、并六州。

translations.literal: Shortly edict Yue Chancellor Yanzhou Shepherd supervise Yan Yu Si Ji You Bing six provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Court named Yue chancellor over six provinces.

sentences.zh: 越辭丞相不受，自許遷於鄄城。

translations.literal: Yue declined chancellor not accepting—from Xu moved Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He refused title and camped Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 越恐清河王覃終為儲副，矯詔收付金墉城，尋害之。

translations.literal: Yue feared Prince Qing Tan ultimately heir-apparent—falsely edict seized delivered Brick Granary fortress—soon harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yue murdered Tan at Brick Granary.

sentences.zh: 王彌入許，越遣左司馬王斌率甲士五千人入衛京都。

translations.literal: Wang Mi entered Xu—Yue dispatched Left Major Wang Bin leading armored soldiers five thousand enter guard capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yue sent Wang Bin to Luoyang against Wang Mi.

sentences.zh: 鄄城自壞，越惡之，移屯濮陽，又遷于滎陽。

translations.literal: Juancheng self collapsed—Yue ill-omened—moved garrison Puyang—again moved Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Juancheng fell—Yue relocated.

sentences.zh: 召田甄等六率，甄不受命，越遣監軍劉望討甄。

translations.literal: Summoned Tian Zhen etc six commands—Zhen refused mandate—Yue dispatched surveillance Liu Wang campaign Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zhen defied orders.

sentences.zh: 初，東嬴公騰之鎮鄴也，攜并州將田甄、甄弟蘭、任祉、祁濟、李惲、薄盛等部眾萬餘人至鄴，遣就谷冀州，號為乞活。

translations.literal: First Duke Teng Dongying garrisoned Ye—carried Bingzhou generals Tian Zhen Zhen younger brother Lan Ren Qi Qi Ji Li Yun Bo Sheng etc masses over ten thousand arrived Ye—dispatched seek grain Ji Province—called Begging Survival.
translations.idiomatic: Teng brought Begging Survival troops from Bing.

sentences.zh: 及騰敗，甄等邀破汲桑於赤橋，越以甄為汲郡，蘭為钜鹿大守。

translations.literal: When Teng had been defeated, Zhen and his men intercepted and routed Ji Sang at Red Bridge; Yue appointed Zhen Grand Administrator of Ji commandery and Lan Grand Administrator of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: After Teng fell, Tian Zhen broke Ji Sang at Red Bridge; Sima Yue rewarded him with Ji commandery and made Tian Lan governor of Julu.

sentences.zh: 甄求魏郡，越不許，甄怒，故召不至。

translations.literal: Zhen sought Wei commandery; Yue did not permit it; Zhen grew angry, and therefore when summoned he failed to appear.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zhen asked for Wei commandery; Yue refused; Zhen sulked and ignored further summons.

sentences.zh: 望既渡河，甄退。

translations.literal: Once Liu Wang had crossed the river, Zhen withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Surveillance Officer Liu Wang crossed the Yellow River, Tian Zhen pulled back.

sentences.zh: 李惲、薄盛斬田蘭，率其眾降，甄、祉、濟棄軍奔上黨。

translations.literal: Li Yun and Bo Sheng executed Tian Lan, led his troops in surrender, and Zhen, Ren Zhi, and Qi Ji abandoned their army and fled to Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun and Bo Sheng killed Tian Lan and surrendered his force; Tian Zhen, Ren Zhi, and Qi Ji bolted and ran for Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 越自滎陽還洛陽，以太學為府。

translations.literal: Yue returned from Xingyang to Luoyang and made the Imperial Academy his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue came back from Xingyang to Luoyang and quartered his staff in the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 疑朝臣貳己，乃誣帝舅王延等為亂，遣王景率甲士三千人入宮收延等，付廷尉殺之。

translations.literal: Suspecting that court ministers were divided against him, he falsely accused the Emperor's maternal uncle Wang Yan and others of rebellion, dispatched Wang Jing at the head of three thousand armored soldiers to enter the palace and seize Yan and the rest, handed them to the Commandant of Justice, and had them executed.
translations.idiomatic: Paranoid about the bureaucracy, he framed Emperor Huai's uncle Wang Yan for treason, sent Wang Jing with three thousand guards into the palace, and had Yan and his alleged accomplices executed.

sentences.zh: 越解兗州牧，領司徒。

translations.literal: Yue relinquished the office of Yanzhou shepherd and concurrently served as Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He stepped down as Yanzhou shepherd and took the portfolio of Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 越既與苟晞構怨，又以頃興事多由殿省，乃奏宿衛有侯爵者皆罷之。

translations.literal: Yue had already nursed a grudge against Gou Xi; moreover, because recent troubles had largely originated in the palace halls, he memorialized that all night guards holding marquis ranks should be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Already at odds with Gou Xi, he blamed palace insiders for recent unrest and cashiered every night guard who held a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 時殿中武官並封侯，由是出者略盡，皆泣涕而去。

translations.literal: At that time the martial officers of the palace halls had all been enfeoffed as marquises; accordingly almost all who departed left weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Those martial officers had all been made marquises; nearly every one left his post in tears.

sentences.zh: 乃以東海國上軍將軍何倫為右衛將軍，王景為左衛將軍，領國兵數百人宿衛。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed He Lun of the Donghai kingdom's Superior Army as General of the Right Guard and Wang Jing as General of the Left Guard, placing several hundred troops of the kingdom on palace duty.
translations.idiomatic: He assigned He Lun of Donghai's superior army to the Right Guard, Wang Jing to the Left Guard, and left several hundred royal troops to watch the palace.

sentences.zh: 越自誅王延等，大失眾望，而多有猜嫌。

translations.literal: After Yue himself had executed Wang Yan and the others, he forfeited popular expectation and was subject to much suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Murdering Wang Yan destroyed his credibility and fed endless mistrust.

sentences.zh: 散騎侍郎高韜有憂國之言，越誣以訕謗時政害之，而不自安。

translations.literal: Gentleman Attendant Gao Tao spoke words that showed concern for the state; Yue falsely accused him of slandering current policy and brought harm upon him, yet did not feel secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Tao voiced patriotic concern, Yue framed him for defaming the court and had him killed, yet remained uneasy.

sentences.zh: 乃戎服入見，請討石勒，且鎮集兗、豫以援京師。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appeared in martial dress for audience, requested a campaign against Shi Le, and proposed gathering Yanzhou and Yuzhou forces to relieve the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He appeared in armor, pledging to strike Shi Le while rallying Yan and Yu to shield Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「今逆虜侵逼郊畿，王室蠢蠢，莫有固心。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Now the rebel bandits press against the royal suburbs; the royal house trembles, and none hold firm resolve."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai replied that rebels besieged the capital region and the court had lost its nerve.

sentences.zh: 朝廷社稷，倚賴於公，豈可遠出以孤根本！

translations.literal: "The court and the altars of soil and grain rely upon you—how can you go far away and isolate the root!"
translations.idiomatic: "The throne depends on you—how can you abandon the capital?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣今率眾邀賊，勢必滅之。

translations.literal: Yue replied, "Your servant now leads the host to intercept the bandits; the situation will surely destroy them."
translations.idiomatic: Yue insisted his army would intercept the enemy and crush them.

sentences.zh: 賊滅則不逞消殄，已東諸州職貢流通。

translations.literal: "Once the bandits are destroyed, then unrestrained evil will be extinguished, and tribute from the provinces east of Xiao will flow without obstruction."
translations.idiomatic: Victory, he said, would pacify the east and restore tribute routes.

sentences.zh: 此所以宣暢國威，籓屏之宜也。

translations.literal: "This is how to broadcast the state's majesty—the proper duty of a frontier shield."
translations.idiomatic: That, he argued, would project imperial prestige along the border marches.

sentences.zh: 若端坐京輦以失機會，則釁弊日滋，所憂逾重。

translations.literal: "If one sits idle in the capital coach and misses the opportunity, then blame and decay will grow daily, and our worries will weigh heavier still."
translations.idiomatic: Staying put, he warned, would only deepen the crisis.

sentences.zh: 」遂行。

translations.literal: With that, he set out.
translations.idiomatic: He marched anyway.

sentences.zh: 留妃裴氏，世子、鎮軍將軍毗，及龍驤將軍李惲並何倫等守衛京都。

translations.literal: He left Consort Pei, the heir Pi (General Who Guards the Army), and General Who Flies His Dragons Li Yun together with He Lun and others to defend the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He left Consort Pei, heir Pi, Li Yun, He Lun, and others to hold Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 表以行台隨軍，率甲士四萬東屯于項，王公卿士隨從者甚眾。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the mobile headquarters should follow the army; leading forty thousand armored soldiers he encamped east at Xiang, and many nobles, ministers, and gentlemen accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: His field headquarters followed forty thousand armored men to Xiang; a host of nobles and officials trailed along.

sentences.zh: 詔加九錫。

translations.literal: An edict added the nine bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: The throne stacked the nine ceremonial gifts on him.

sentences.zh: 越乃羽檄四方曰：「皇綱失禦，社稷多難，孤以弱才，備當大任。

translations.literal: Yue then sent feathered summons to the four quarters, saying, "The imperial net has lost its governance; the altars face many hardships; I, weak in talent, have been charged with a great duty."
translations.idiomatic: He issued a manifesto lamenting lost control and naming himself the burdened rescuer of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 自頃胡寇內逼，偏裨失利，帝鄉便為戎州，冠帶奄成殊域，朝廷上下，以為憂懼。

translations.literal: "Recently Hu bandits have pressed inward; lieutenants have suffered defeat; the imperial district has become a barbarian zone; caps and sashes have suddenly turned into alien lands—above and below at court all feel alarm and fear."
translations.idiomatic: He described barbarian pressure, defeated wings, and the heartland slipping into foreign hands.

sentences.zh: 皆由諸侯蹉跎，遂及此難。

translations.literal: "All this is because the feudal lords hesitated and dragged their feet, until we reached this calamity."
translations.idiomatic: He blamed rival princes for dithering until disaster struck.

sentences.zh: 投袂忘履，討之已晚。

translations.literal: "They cast aside sleeves and forgot shoes—the time to punish them is already late."
translations.idiomatic: They had stirred too late—vengeance now came behind events.

sentences.zh: 人情奉本，莫不義奮。

translations.literal: "Human hearts cling to their sovereign; none fail to rise in righteous zeal."
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty to the throne, he urged, should galvanize every commander.

sentences.zh: 當須合會之眾，以俟戰守之備。

translations.literal: "We must assemble united hosts and await readiness for battle and defense."
translations.idiomatic: He called for united armies ready to fight and hold ground.

sentences.zh: 宗廟主上，相賴匡救。

translations.literal: "The ancestral temples and our sovereign depend upon one another for rescue."
translations.idiomatic: Altar and emperor alike needed joint rescue.

sentences.zh: 檄至之日，便望風奮發，忠臣戰士效誠之秋也。

translations.literal: "On the day this summons arrives, let all rally when they hear the wind—the hour when loyal ministers and warriors prove their devotion."
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed this the moment for loyalists to answer.

sentences.zh: 」所征皆不至。

translations.literal: None of those summoned came.
translations.idiomatic: Nobody responded.

sentences.zh: 而苟晞又表討越，語在《晞傳》。

translations.literal: Gou Xi moreover memorialized for a campaign against Yue; the account is given in the biography of Gou Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi attacked him—the story belongs to Gou's biography.

sentences.zh: 越以豫州刺史馮嵩為左司馬，自領豫州牧。

translations.literal: Yue appointed Feng Song, Inspector of Yuzhou, as Left Major and himself concurrently served as shepherd of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He named Feng Song Left Major and took the Yuzhou shepherd's seal himself.

sentences.zh: 越專擅威權，圖為霸業，朝賢素望，選為佐吏，名將勁卒，充於己府，不臣之跡，四海所知。

translations.literal: Yue monopolized awe-inspiring authority and plotted hegemonic rule; eminent courtiers of plain renown were selected as his clerks; famed generals and crack troops filled his own mansion—conduct unbefitting a minister was known throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He hoarded power like a warlord: eminent ministers became his clerks, elite troops his household guard—everyone knew he no longer behaved as a subject.

sentences.zh: 而公私罄乏，所在寇亂，州郡攜貳，上下崩離，禍結釁深，遂憂懼成疾。

translations.literal: Yet public and private stores were exhausted; banditry arose everywhere; provinces and commanderies wavered in loyalty; high and low split apart; calamity and ill will knotted deep—thereupon anxiety and fear turned into illness.
translations.idiomatic: Exhaustion and rebellion everywhere, provinces turning coat, court split—fear sickening him.

sentences.zh: 永嘉五年，薨于項。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of the Yongjia reign he died at Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongjia year five at Xiang.

sentences.zh: 秘不發喪。

translations.literal: His death was concealed and mourning was not announced.
translations.idiomatic: His staff hid the corpse.

sentences.zh: 以襄陽王范為大將軍，統其眾。

translations.literal: Prince Fan of Xiangyang was named Grand General and placed in command of his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fan of Xiangyang took command of the army.

sentences.zh: 還葬東海。

translations.literal: His remains were returned for burial in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: His body went home to Donghai for burial.

sentences.zh: 石勒追及于苦縣甯平城，將軍錢端出兵距勒，戰死，軍潰。

translations.literal: Shi Le overtook them at Ningping city in Ku county; General Qian Duan led troops out to oppose Le, died in battle, and the army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le caught the procession at Ningping in Ku county; Qian Duan died resisting and the column dissolved.

sentences.zh: 勒命焚越柩曰：「此人亂天下，吾為天下報之，故燒其骨以告天地。

translations.literal: Le ordered Yue's coffin burned, saying, "This man threw All-under-Heaven into chaos; your servant avenges All-under-Heaven; therefore I burn his bones to inform Heaven and Earth."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le burned Yue's coffin, calling it cosmic justice.

sentences.zh: 」於是數十萬眾，勒以騎圍而射之，相踐如山。

translations.literal: Thereupon, amid several hundred thousand troops, Le ringed them with cavalry and shot them down; they trampled one another like a mountain.
translations.idiomatic: His horsemen surrounded hundreds of thousands and shot them into a writhing heap.

sentences.zh: 王公士庶死者十餘萬。

translations.literal: More than a hundred thousand nobles, gentlemen, and commoners perished.
translations.idiomatic: Over a hundred thousand nobles and commoners died.

sentences.zh: 王彌弟璋焚其餘眾，並食之。

translations.literal: Wang Mi's younger brother Zhang burned the remainder of the host and devoured them together.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi's brother Wang Zhang burned survivors and fed on the dead.

sentences.zh: 天下歸罪於越。

translations.literal: All-under-Heaven laid the blame on Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The realm blamed Yue for the catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 帝發詔貶越為縣王。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict demoting Yue to Prince of a county.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai stripped him to a county-level princedom.

sentences.zh: 何倫、李惲聞越之死，秘不發喪，奉妃裴氏及毗出自京邑，從者傾城，所經暴掠。

translations.literal: He Lun and Li Yun, hearing of Yue's death, concealed it and did not announce mourning; escorting Consort Pei and Pi they quit the capital; their followers emptied the city, and wherever they passed they plundered violently.
translations.idiomatic: He Lun and Li Yun smuggled Consort Pei and Pi out of Luoyang without mourning Yue publicly; their train looted half the city.

sentences.zh: 至洧倉，又為勒所敗，毗及宗室三十六王俱沒於賊。

translations.literal: When they reached the Wei granary, they were again defeated by Le; Pi and thirty-six princes of the imperial clan together fell to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Near the Wei granary Shi Le smashed them; Pi and thirty-six imperial princes perished.

sentences.zh: 李惲殺妻子奔廣宗，何倫走下邳。

translations.literal: Li Yun killed his wife and children and fled to Guangzong; He Lun fled down to Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun slaughtered his family and ran to Guangzong; He Lun fled toward Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 裴妃為人所略，賣于吳氏，太興中，得渡江，欲招魂葬越。

translations.literal: Consort Pei was seized by others and sold to the Wu clan; in the Taixing era she was able to cross the Yangzi and wished to summon his soul and bury Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Kidnappers sold Consort Pei into the Wu household; she later crossed south in Taixing and wanted a soul-summoning burial for Yue.

sentences.zh: 元帝詔有司詳議，博士傅純曰：「聖人制禮，以事緣情，設塚槨以藏形，而事之以凶；

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan ordered the relevant offices to deliberate in detail; Erudite Fu Chun said, "The sages instituted ritual so that affairs follow feeling: they set mound and outer coffin to hide the form and serve it with the accursed rites;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan asked the ministry; Fu Chun argued that burial rites hide the body under ill-omened observance.

sentences.zh: 立廟祧以安神，而奉之以吉。

translations.literal: they established distant shrine temples to settle the spirit and served it with auspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral temples house the spirit under auspicious cult.

sentences.zh: 送形而往，迎精而還。

translations.literal: Send the form away; welcome the essence back.
translations.idiomatic: You escort the corpse out and welcome the spirit home by another path.

sentences.zh: 此墓廟之大分，形神之異制也。

translations.literal: This is the great distinction between tomb and temple—the different systems for body and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Graves and temples answer to different rules for body and soul.

sentences.zh: 至於室廟寢廟祊祭非一處，所以廣求神之道，而獨不祭於墓，明非神之所處也。

translations.literal: As for side-chamber and distant temples, side sacrifices not being in one place—thereby they broadly seek the way of the spirits; yet they alone do not sacrifice at the tomb, making clear that it is not where the spirit dwells.
translations.idiomatic: Because worship ranges across shrines, the dead are not venerated at the burial mound—that place is not the spirit's seat.

sentences.zh: 今亂形神之別，錯廟墓之宜，違禮制義，莫大於此。

translations.literal: Now we confuse the distinction of body and spirit and invert the propriety of temple and tomb; nothing greater violates ritual and rightness than this."
translations.idiomatic: Equating tomb cult with temple rites, he said, was the grossest breach of ritual.

sentences.zh: 」於是下詔不許。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued forbidding it.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused her request.

sentences.zh: 裴妃不奉詔，遂葬越於廣陵。

translations.literal: Consort Pei did not obey the edict and buried Yue at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: She buried him at Guangling anyway.

sentences.zh: 太興末，墓毀，改葬丹徒。

translations.literal: Near the end of Taixing the tomb was destroyed; he was reburied at Dantu.
